Japanese prime minister Sanae Takaichi, who is increasingly seen secluding herself at home, said she is using her official residence next to her office more for work to maximise efficiency.

In December, Ms Takaichi moved into the official residence, a brick-and-stone mansion that opened in 1929. It used to be the original prime minister’s office until its replacement was built right next to it.

Ms Takaichi said on X that living in the official residence, or “kotei”, is good because its proximity requires no commute and lets her immediately get down to work in time of an emergency.

open image in gallery FILE - The Prime Minister's official residence is seen in Tokyo in February 1978. (AP Photo, File) ( AP )

Ms Takaichi said she has reinforced office functions at the residence so she can work and have meetings there remotely or in person with her staff whenever needed, even after office hours.

She also takes home documents to read.

“To me, the official residence is also a workplace,” she said.

But Ms Takaichi, whose work mantra and her recent revelation on X of zero to three hours of sleep at night because of her homemaking burden on top of her heavy workload as prime minister, triggered criticisms that Japan's first female leader was setting a wrong example for a work-life balance and gender-equality.

Ms Takaichi has seen her support ratings rapidly drop as she pushed unpopular policies such as a revision to the Imperial House Law to reinforce a male-only succession system, while delaying economic measures to address rising prices.

Media reports have said that Ms Takaichi was avoiding parliamentary sessions and largely holed up at the residence at night and on weekends, saying that she's having significantly less interactions and communication with other lawmakers and officials than her predecessors.

open image in gallery Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi enters her prime minister's office in Tokyo, Friday, Aug. 21, 2026. (Keisuke Hosojima/Kyodo News via AP) ( AP )

Ms Takaichi frequently posts comments and policies on X instead of talking to the media.

The official residence was the site of two bloody coup attempts in the 1930s, and legend has it that the building is haunted by ghosts.

Ms Takaichi apparently doesn’t mind spending long hours at the residence despite that.

“I’ve never seen a ghost, but I have often screamed because of my encounters with cockroaches,” she said. “I was shocked when a cockroach ran past my feet.”

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.



Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Frustrated Russell fails to make up ground as Norris wins incident-packed Dutch GP
News.content:
George Russell had another frustrating Sunday as the Dutch Grand Prix weekend slipped by with him failing to reduce his deficit to leader Kimi Antonelli. In a thrilling finale to the 72-lap race at the Dutch seaside, Lando Norris took his second victory in a row with two bold overtakes in one lap.

Yet compatriot Russell was irritated by Mercedes team orders for him to let Antonelli through into second place in the closing stages. It was a decision he believed risked a double podium for the team and threatened to put him even further behind his team-mate in the standings, with two charging Ferraris close behind. It was a race that, once again, fell away, despite Russell doing little wrong.

“Is he [Antonelli] fighting for the win or is he planning to catch Norris?” he asked, when the McLaren driver was 11 seconds down the road – the margin he would win by. “Yeah – we just lost a double podium here, mate,” was his response after moving aside.

Whilst Norris, who lost his lead from pole to Antonelli on the first lap, sealed the victory with two superb overtakes on lap 54 – first the Italian and then Lewis Hamilton – Russell had to mount a stout defence from Hamilton to secure third. It was against the odds, as both Ferraris, like Antonelli, were on fresh rubber after pitting under a late virtual safety car. Like Russell, Hamilton was critical of his team for their strategy choices.

Russell’s first podium finish since Silverstone – with his sprint victory on Saturday – means he at least retakes second place in the championship from Hamilton, but trails Antonelli by the same 59 point-gap he had after Hungary. That is despite him looking the faster and more comfortable Mercedes driver on Friday and Saturday.

News.title: Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win
News.content:
Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

News.title: How to spend a weekend in Lake Garda
News.content:
Lake Garda’s glittering wind-swept waters have long attracted poets, artists, writers and politicians, from DH Lawrence to Wolfgang Goethe – not least Mussolini, who ran the Italian Socialist Republic from the lakefront town of Salò on the western shore.

Fringed by the Dolomites to the north, Italy’s largest lake is Mediterranean both in feel and in flavour, with a mild, temperate climate and a decidedly slow pace of life. Hills are carpeted in olive trees and vineyards, while citrus groves are thick with plump, juicy lemons. In lakefront villages, restaurant tables spill out onto pretty waterfront squares, while boats zip across glimmering waters.

The lower basin is punctuated with sandy coves and gentle rolling hills, while travelling north, the lake takes on a new appearance, with hills replaced by sheer jagged cliffs that plunge into the waters. The northern shore is swept by mountain winds that create the perfect conditions for watersports, with windsailing, kitesurfing, and flyboarding making this a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts.

News.title: How to spend a perfect weekend in Lake Como
News.content:
An hour drive north of Milan, Lake Como is the most glamorous of Italy’s lakes, hemmed in by the snow-capped Alps with picture-perfect villages on the water. Milanesi pop here for the day for a breath of fresh air and to soak up the fabulous vistas, while international visitors – the Clooneys, the Kennedys – have long been drawn by the grand lakefront hotels and the elegant mahogany Riva boats that zip along the lake’s deep blue waters.

Smart hotels and expensive boats aside, Lake Como is rich in culture, with opulent villas that once belonged to artists, writers, opera singers and explorers. Pliny the Elder, author of the first encyclopaedia, was born here, while 19th-century soprano Giuditta Pasta is known to have entertained composers Bellini and Donizetti in her lakefront residence on the eastern shore.

Though famous spots such as pretty Bellagio still pull in the majority of visitors, the lake has retained its authenticity, with plenty of sleepy fishing villages, such as Laglio, Torno and Nesso, home to rustic, family-run trattorias serving up traditional hearty fare, including risotto al pesce persico (risotto with perch).

News.title: Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair
News.content:
It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

News.title: Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions
News.content:
The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

News.title: All Blacks stun Springboks in statement win
News.content:
Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry did not begin with the year’s greatest game, but a New Zealand victory against the odds, at high altitude in Johannesburg, has poured intrigue and interest on to a series which was already brimming with them.

The All Blacks’ recent record at Ellis Park, the Springboks’ spiritual home, is by no means shabby – this was their fourth victory from the last six visits – but few fancied Dave Rennie’s galvanised Kiwis on Saturday, against the back-to-back world champions, after a week which had been dominated by chat of officials and law interpretations.

Yet, this stunning victory was almost as comfortable as it was surprising. New Zealand outscored their hosts by five tries to one and, by the end, a 13-player Springboks outfit – both Marco van Staden and Cobus Reinach were sin-binned within a minute of each other – were left chasing shadows in an Ellis Park which had been stupefied into silence.

It was at the beginning of that 13-player period when New Zealand put the game to bed, with Will Jordan crossing for his second try. But the damage had already been done by a cast of Kiwi conquerors. Ardie Savea, captain and No 8, could not have delivered more for the cause; Luke Jacobson and Tupou Vaa’i on the flanks were more than deputies to Savea; the locks, until Josh Lord’s unfortunate departure just before half-time, were magnificent; and, behind them, Cam Roigard continues to look every bit the equal of those phenomenal French scrum-halves. The New Zealand midfield got the upper hand on their much vaunted counterparts, too, on the day of Damian de Allende’s 100th cap for South Africa.

Sports.title: Diego Simeone addresses brutal Julian Alvarez jeers as Arsenal target blockbuster transfer
Sports.content:
Diego Simeone addresses brutal Julian Alvarez jeers as Arsenal target blockbuster transfer

Julian Alvarez has been linked with a move away from Atletico Madrid and the Arsenal target was booed by his own fans during the 2-2 draw with Villarreal on Sunday

View 2 Images Arsenal have been linked with a move for Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez. (Image: (Photo By Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press via Getty Images))

Diego Simeone says it was planned that Arsenal transfer target Julian Alvarez would not stand with his teammates to show appreciation to Atletico Madrid supporters after the full time whistle on Sunday. The forward was jeered off the pitch by his own fans and had to be escorted down the tunnel by club staff after Atleti's 2-2 draw with Villarreal.

‌



Alvarez forward has been heavily linked with a departure from Simeone's squad throughout the summer transfer window. The club turned down an approach from city rivals Real Madrid at the start of the window, before Barcelona made their intentions clear that they were keen to snap up Alvarez.

‌



The former Manchester City star has made no secret of his desire to leave the club, publicly declaring his wish to join the reigning La Liga champions. However, Atleti have stood firm in their refusal to sell to their domestic rivals, leaving Alvarez increasingly frustrated.

‌



Gabriel Martinelli poised to hand Arsenal huge payday as £60m transfer option emerges READ MORE :

Julian Alvarez 'contacted' by Mikel Arteta as Arsenal transfer response given READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Alvarez was named amongst the substitutes for the 2-2 draw with Villarreal, entering the fray in the second half to a chorus of boos from the home faithful. He played his part as ten-man Atletico fought back to salvage a point, yet was met with a hostile reception from his own supporters throughout his time on the pitch.

Alvarez was led down the tunnel by staff while his teammates went over to applaud the supporters at the final whistle. As he departed the pitch, Alvarez was once again subjected to jeers and whistles, casting further uncertainty over his future at the club.

‌



View 2 Images Arsenal continue to pursue a transfer for Julian Alvarez (Image: (Photo by Manu Reino/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images))

Addressing the situation, Simeone said: "It was a club decision to not let Julian Alvarez go over with his teammates to greet the fans."

Ahead of the match, the Atleti manager said: "For me, Julian is an extremely important player for us to achieve our objectives. As long as he's with the team, I'm going to look after him."

‌



Arsenal are believed to be strongly interested in securing the striker's services as they look to strengthen Mikel Arteta's squad. The Gunners are aiming to defend their Premier League title and go one step further by lifting the Champions League trophy.

Landing Alvarez would send out a powerful message of intent, and according to reports emerging from Spain, Arsenal could be the sole remaining route for the Argentine frontman should he wish to depart the club.

Alvarez's remarks about joining Barcelona have sparked a fierce backlash, with posters appearing around Atleti's training ground on Friday morning reading "JULIAN FUERA" ("JULIAN OUT") and featuring the striker's No. 19 crossed out.

Sports.title: Brighton fan dies after Aston Villa win as club chief speaks on 'heartbreaking' incident
Sports.content:
Brighton fan dies after Aston Villa win as club chief speaks on 'heartbreaking' incident

Brighton secured an emphatic win over Aston Villa to begin their Premier League season but a fan was taken unwell as he left the Amex, later dying despite the efforts of the emergency services

View Image A Brighton fan was taken ill after Sunday's win and later died

A Brighton fan who attended their Premier League win over Aston Villa has died, the club have confirmed.

‌



The Seagulls enjoyed the perfect start to their campaign as they hammered Unai Emery's side on Sunday, recording a 4-0 win. However the club have since confirmed that a fan felt unwell as he left the Amex, but the emergency services couldn't save him.

‌



A Brighton statement read: “Following today’s game against Aston Villa, sadly a 72-year-old male Brighton & Hove Albion supporter passed away after the match. The gentleman took unwell as he was leaving the stadium to board a supporters’ club bus in the coach park. Despite the best efforts of emergency services and club staff, the medical team were unable to save him.

‌



“South East Coast Ambulance Service paramedics, St John’s Ambulance, Sussex Police, MB Medical Solutions, the club’s crowd doctor and our stewards worked together to ensure the individual was given the best possible care, including prolonged CPR on the scene.”

CEO Paul Barber added: “What should have been an ordinary and happy journey home ended in heartbreaking circumstances, and we are all shocked and saddened by the loss of one of our supporters. We extend our sincere condolences to the gentleman’s family and friends.”

It is the second year in a row that a man has died after attending Brighton’s opening game of the season.

Sports.title: Alejandro Balde gives transfer green light as Man Utd handed huge Barcelona boost
Sports.content:
Alejandro Balde gives transfer green light as Man Utd handed huge Barcelona boost

Manchester United are looking to sign a new left-back this summer, with Barcelona's Alejandro Balde emerging as a potential target

View 2 Images Alejandro Balde could be on the move (Image: Alex Caparros, Getty Images)

Manchester United have seen a significant boost in their bid to snap up Alejandro Balde from Barcelona. While the Red Devils are thought to see Lewis Hall as an ideal successor to an ageing Luke Shaw, Newcastle United's determination to hold onto the youngster is proving difficult.

‌



It has been reported that the Magpies will only facilitate a departure for the 21-year-old should United cough up a fee surpassing Lucas Hernandez's record-breaking £68million move from Bayern Munich to Real Madrid in 2019.

‌



As a result, United have started to look further afield for reinforcement to their defensive backline. Barcelona's Balde is considered a potential candidate to fit the bill.

‌



The 22-year-old has been at the Catalan club since coming through their youth academy in 2021. However, owing to fierce competition for places and injury setbacks, he has recently fallen out of favour in Hansi Flick's thinking.

Wayne Rooney blasts one Man Utd star for 'schoolboy' level in Hull embarrassment READ MORE :

Marcus Rashford sends Man Utd message after dismal Hull City loss READ MORE :

According to Sport, the Spaniard has given Portuguese super-agent Jorge Mendes the green light to source him a new club. Balde has been left out of Flick's first-team squad for their La Liga opener away at Elche on Sunday evening, with the head coach making clear he only wishes to call upon players who are 100 per cent committed to the club.

As a result, United could secure a bargain alternative to Hall in the coming days. Nevertheless, the Red Devils will face stiff competition for the full-back's signature, with clubs in Portugal and Italy also understood to be keen.

‌



It follows United's apparent focus on bolstering their midfield following Casemiro's departure on a free transfer, with several new arrivals at the heart of the engine room and potentially more additions on the horizon.

View 2 Images United have also taken a keen interest in Newcastle full-back Lewis Hall (Image: (Photo by Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images))

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



United snapped up Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa in a £35m deal, before securing Andrey Santos from Chelsea for £52m. The club are also targeting Brighton and Hove Albion's Carlos Baleba, a year after interest in the 22-year-old first emerged.

United have struck a £70m agreement for the midfielder, inclusive of £5m in add-ons, with a five-year contract on the table for the youngster - who missed the Seagulls' Premier League curtain-raiser against Aston Villa on Sunday through injury.

It comes as United will be looking to make amends for a 2-0 defeat to Hull City on Saturday when they welcome fellow Premier League newcomers Ipswich Town to Old Trafford in seven days' time.

Sports.title: Dominik Szoboszlai rescues last-gasp point for Liverpool at Newcastle - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Dominik Szoboszlai rescues last-gasp point for Liverpool at Newcastle - 5 talking points

NEWCASTLE UNITED 2-2 LIVERPOOL: Dominik Szoboszlai scored a stoppage time penalty to rescue a point for the Reds after Joe Willock's second-half strike looked poised to win the game for the hosts

View 4 Images Liverpool were rescued by Dominik Szoboszlai's penalty in stoppage time

Liverpool salvaged a point in the 99th minute as a Dominik Szoboszlai penalty ensured Newcastle's Matthias Jaissle era didn't start with a win at St James' Park.

‌



The Magpies were ahead inside five minutes thanks to Anthony Elanga's strike, his first for the club in the Premier League. They retained that lead going into half-time but Andoni Iraola's side came fighting back and Cody Gakpo fired home the visitors' equaliser on 55 minutes.

‌



Liverpool weren't level for long though as Joe Willock completed another counter attack to retake the lead. Newcastle looked set for three points but, just as there was stoppage time drama last year, Szoboszlai converted from 12 yards after Lewis Hall felled Victor Munoz.

‌



Newcastle broke with real pace to score the opener inside four minutes as William Osula ran at the Liverpool defence before sending Elanga clear, with the winger finishing impressively to ignited St James' Park.

Florian Wirtz forced Lukas Hornicek into a smart save as the Reds went in search of an equaliser, but that's as close as they would come in the opening 45 minutes with the hosts continuing to offer a threat in attack.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Liverpool would bring themselves back into the game when Gakpo fired home their equaliser. The Dutchman adopting a good position 25 yards out before receiving the ball in the space and firing home from range after being afforded time to take aim.

The Reds looked to have a spring in their step in the moments following their equaliser, but parity in the game only lasted three minutes. Newcastle again hit Liverpool on the counter with Yoane Wissa travelling half the pitch before finding Willock, who finished neatly.

The Magpies had almost completed their mission before Hall's foul gifted Liverpool a penalty deep into stoppage time, which Szoboszlai hammered into the roof of the net to rescue a point.

‌



Here's five talking points from the north east.

Not so doom and gloom for the Toon

After a summer that saw Newcastle cash in on three of their leading lights for more than £240million plenty have tipped the Magpies to have a season of struggle, especially after their change of manager midway through pre-season.

View 4 Images New boss Matthias Jaissle was denied the perfect start to life in Newcastle

‌



But Sunday's performance showed that this Newcastle side still have it in them to give it to the country's top teams. The St James' Park crowd also still believe and only need a bit of desire from their team to play their part from the stands. There's still much to like about the Newcastle game plan, even if they don't have the stellar names of years gone by. Had you gone into hiding over the summer and reappeared for the opening weekend, you wouldn't have known so much negativity had swirled about the Toon, but conceding so late will make Sunday's outing feel like a defeat.

Iraola learning scale of the job

Last season it was hard to gauge whether the title win of 2025 was the outlier or a fair reflection of where Liverpool should be, given they dropped to fifth last term.

That demise cost Arne Slot his job and Iraola was quickly bought in as his replacement. Results in pre-season, where the Merseysiders twice gave up two-goal leads to lose, exposed defensive flaws with the Spanish boss admitting the team weren't yet primed to play the style he demanded. Sunday was his first genuine chance to show what Iraola's Liverpool looked like, bar a ten minute spell to start the second-half and Gakpo's impressive outing, it looked set to end in defeat. Szoboszlai's penalty ensured the former Bournemouth boss doesn't begin with a defeat, but he did little more than clap, knowing mass improvement is needed.

‌



View 4 Images Joe Willock thought he'd score the winner in the second-half

Elanga the speedster

If there's one thing Newcastle lost when Anthony Gordon left for Barcelona it was out and out pace. But its easy to forget in Elanga they still have that outlet of raw speed, which proved crucial for the opening goal early on.

Elanga had a frustrating debut season at St James' Park, especially given he'd cost £55m, but he couldn't have began in better fashion. The winger only started 14 games in the league last year, appearing more often from the bench, but with the exodus of players his role will be magnified and he possesses the pace that Newcastle so often relied on when Gordon was in full flow.

‌



Isak's return

Last season when this fixture was played Isak was in the midst of trying to force his move from Newcastle to Liverpool and as a result was absent. He would eventually get his way, destroying the legacy he'd built in the north east, before enduring a wholly disappointing injury-hit campaign at Anfield.

View 4 Images Alexander Isak underwhelmed on his return to St James' Park

Sunday was Isak's first Liverpool-Newcastle clash as a Red and, inevitably, his every touch was booed by the home crowd. His every error or misplaced touch was roared even louder. His biggest chance came with 20 minutes remaining, but the Swede fired his effort well over to mark a forgettable first return. His Hungarian team-mate at least ensured he didn't leave having lost.

‌



The Wirtz problem continues

Last year didn't go to plan as Liverpool desperately tried to get the most out of the German, who was briefly the British record signing. He was played from the flanks and centrally. Iraola decided that Wirtz's best role was at the heart of the attack.

But on the hour mark, and with Liverpool needing a goal, the Reds boss chose to hook his playmaker. A damning verdict and the camera was quick to pan to the former Bayer Leverkusen man, who looked unimpressed as he took his spot on the bench. Liverpool's investment in Wirtz means they have to persevere with him, but the weight on his shoulders is only increasing.

Sports.title: Gabriel Martinelli poised to hand Arsenal huge payday as £60m transfer option emerges
Sports.content:
Gabriel Martinelli poised to hand Arsenal huge payday as £60m transfer option emerges

Arsenal are in talks over a potential deal for Gabriel Martinelli, with the Brazilian slipping down the pecking order following Christos Tzolis' summer arrival

View Image Gabriel Martinelli could leave Arsenal before the transfer deadline day (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal are holding discussions with Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal over a potential transfer for Gabriel Martinelli. The Brazilian has slipped out of favour under Mikel Arteta and the club are prepared to consider offers if their asking price is met.

‌



Martinelli has been consistently linked with a move away from the Premier League champions this summer. Galatasaray held talks earlier this month, while AS Roma have also expressed interest in the 25‑year‑old.

‌



The Athletic now report that Al Hilal are actively pursuing a deal and are in discussions with Martinelli’s representatives over a prospective move. Arsenal are believed to be seeking around £60million.

‌



11 top Premier League players in final year of contract including Man Utd and Liverpool stars READ MORE :

While no deal has been struck, talks are continuing - and Martinelli is understood to be receptive to the prospect of playing in Saudi Arabia.

He finds himself at a career crossroads, with regular first-team football in north London appearing improbable following the arrival of Christos Tzolis and Arsenal's efforts to recruit another forward, with Julian Alvarez amongst those linked.

Mikel Arteta omitted Martinelli from his matchday squads for both the Community Shield and the home victory over Coventry City on Friday night.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal legend Ian Wright has confessed he feels 'uncomfortable' with the manner in which Martinelli is being handled. "With respect to Martinelli and the way he's being treated at the moment, it really makes me uncomfortable," he told Sky Sports.

"He always gives 100%, we're not saying he's the greatest, but he's come up with some big moments for Arsenal in big games, and the way he's being treated at the end here.

‌



"I know they might want him out and there's a lot of guys saying it's time for him to move on, but there's ways of doing that should suit him as well."

Martinelli has 12 months remaining on his existing contract, and while Arsenal possess an option to prolong it by another year, triggering that clause now seems improbable. The winger joined the Emirates Stadium in 2019, arriving from Brazilian outfit Ituano in a £6m transfer.

Arsenal are also prepared to part ways with Gabriel Jesus, with the Brazil international anticipated to depart as a free agent at the conclusion of the season should he fail to secure a transfer this summer or in January.

Sports.title: Kevin Keegan's cause of death as Liverpool and Newcastle prepare to pay tribute
Sports.content:
Kevin Keegan's cause of death as Liverpool and Newcastle prepare to pay tribute

There will be emotional scenes when Newcastle host Liverpool in their first competitive match since the death of Kevin Keegan

View 3 Images Kevin Keegan's life will be celebrated on Sunday (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Newcastle and Liverpool fans have united to celebrate the life of the late Kevin Keegan. Fittingly, the English clubs where he is most revered meet in their opening Premier League match of the season at St James' Park on Sunday.

‌



Keegan, a star of Liverpool's 1970s side who went on to become adored on Tyneside as player and manager of Newcastle, died on July 20 aged 75. He had been undergoing treatment for stage four stomach cancer.

‌



Keegan's family revealed in January that he had been diagnosed with the disease. Speaking at an event in Newcastle in May, Keegan said he would like to return to St James' Park to say goodbye. He said: "I want to say goodbye. I didn't get the chance when I left the club last time."

‌



As tributes poured in from around the football world, his death was felt most on Tyneside and Merseyside, with the Magpies and the Reds holding talks over how to commemorate an incredible life and career when the sides met.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

A Newcastle statement said: "The opening Premier League match of 2026/27 sees Newcastle United hosting Liverpool – where Kevin made 323 appearances between 1971 and 1977.

‌



Tribute to a true footballing legend, Kevin Keegan READ MORE :

"To ensure his memory is marked fittingly before the game, the club is in communication with Liverpool and will work closely with supporter groups, including its Fan Advisory Board, the Newcastle United Supporters Trust and Wor Flags, as well as the Premier League, to shape tributes."

Liverpool said: "LFC is also in direct contact with Newcastle United, ahead of the Premier League opener at St. James' Park, regarding special tributes to Keegan, who represented both clubs so successfully.

"In addition, a further tribute will be held ahead of the Reds' first Premier League home match of the season, on Saturday, August 29 against Nottingham Forest.

‌



View 3 Images Tributes to Keegan outside St James' Park (Image: PA)

"This will provide another opportunity for supporters to pay their respects with a special fan mosaic and a period of applause observed before kick-off, with players also wearing black armbands."

Born in Doncaster, Keegan started his career at Scunthorpe before being signed for Liverpool by Bill Shankly in 1971. While at Anfield, Keegan won the First Division title three times as well as the FA Cup, the UEFA Cup twice and the 1977 European Cup.

‌



Following that success, Keegan joined German side Hamburg and was twice named European Footballer of the Year. He is the only British player to have won the award, now called the Ballon d’Or, more than once.

View 3 Images Keegan is one of Liverpool's greatest ever players (Image: Mirrorpix)

Keegan returned to England with Southampton in the summer of 1980 before moving to Second Division Newcastle, helping the club win promotion back to the top flight, only to then retire at the age of 33.

‌



He won 63 England caps, scoring 21 goals, playing at the 1982 World Cup and captaining the national team. In 1992, Keegan made his first step into management at Newcastle, leading them into the Premier League and to within touching distance of the 1995/96 title.

He later managed Fulham, England and Manchester City before a short-lived return to Newcastle, where he spent just eight months before resigning after a fallout with owner Mike Ashley.

Sports.title: Barcelona make Alejandro Balde decision after Man Utd boss Michael Carrick drops hint
Sports.content:
Barcelona make Alejandro Balde decision after Man Utd boss Michael Carrick drops hint

Alejandro Balde wants to leave Barcelona before the transfer window closes and he's been linked with joining Manchester United amid their search for a left-back

View 2 Images Alejandro Balde is a target for Manchester United (Image: Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Manchester United target Alejandro Balde has been left out of Barcelona's squad for their La Liga opener against Elche. Balde, 22, is on the Camp Nou chopping block and wants to secure a move away ahead of the transfer window closing on September 1.

‌



The Spaniard is an option for United, who are scouring the market for a left-back. Talks have reportedly been held with Balde's agent, Jorge Mendes, with the Red Devils preparing a bid of €40million (£34m).

‌



On Sunday, Barcelona announced their 25-man travelling squad to face Elche and Balde wasn't included. Marc Casado and Hector Fort were also left out, with all three players up for sale.

‌



Both Balde and Fort's chances of game time took a hit this week when Barca welcomed back Joao Cancelo, who can play on the left and right-hand side of defence. Cancelo's arrival on loan in January led to a reduction in minutes for Balde, whose 2025-26 campaign was also blighted by hamstring injuries.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Barca boss Hansi Flick hailed the 22-year-old in his pre-match press conference but isn't sure whether he can compete with Cancelo. "He's a player of immense quality, and it's important to know if he's confident he can compete in his position," Flick said.

"That's what I want to see from all my players. Every day I observe what they do, their level, whether they demonstrate that they're at the level to play."

Flick's comments come after Michael Carrick was quizzed on United's left-back search before they started the Premier League season with a limp 2-0 loss away to newly promoted Hull. "I just think we're looking to strengthen the squad," Carrick replied.

‌



Should Manchester United sign Alejandro Balde? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Alejandro Balde has been left out of Barcelona's squad (Image: Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

"We're certainly working towards that, making the most of the situation that we have and trying to improve things and trying to move forward. You know, I said the same thing to you last time.

‌



"So, yeah, certainly trying to make the most of the opportunities to finish the window stronger than we went into it. And I think we're a good way to doing that, so far."

Lewis Hall of Newcastle was United's top left-back target earlier in the window, but he's seen as unattainable this summer for a variety of reasons. Newcastle don't need to sell and have already lost three key players, while United have spent most of their budget on midfielders.

Sports.content:
Frenchman Arthur Fils may have played himself into contention to win the US Open after sealing the biggest title of his career at the Cincinnati Open on Sunday.

The 21st seed, who won the Barcelona Open in April, added the Cincy crown to his growing list of achievements with a topsy-turvy 6-3 1-6 6-0 victory over Frances Tiafoe in Ohio.

Fils became the third Black man to win a Masters 1000 title, joining Ben Shelton, who won the Canadian Open twice, and Jo-Wilfried Tsonga, who won Paris in 2008 and Canada in 2014.

Tiafoe, playing in his second Cincinnati final, responded in kind in the second set.

The 28-year-old broke in ‌the second game en route to a 3-0 lead, with his forehands pulling Fils wide. Although Fils got on the board with a hold to ⁠love, the 17th seed Tiafoe broke ​again for a 5-1 advantage before forcing ​a decider.

Fils quickly regained control in ​the third set, breaking twice to race into ⁠a 4-0 lead as Tiafoe's backhand errors piled up.

The 22-year-old's pace and movement proved too much ⁠for the American, and he ​closed out the match with a bagel ​final set after a lengthy rally to lift the trophy.

Sports.title: Late Clark magic holds off McIlroy and Cantlay in PGA Tour thriller
Sports.content:
Wyndham Clark overcame blowing a five-shot lead to edge out Rory McIlroy with a dramatic three-shot victory at the PGA Tour's BMW Championship.

Clark saw his big overnight lead disappear during a thrilling Sunday at Bellerive Country Club, where the US Open champion bogeyed three of his first 10 holes to give hope to McIlroy and the chasing pack.

McIlroy found three birdies in a four-hole stretch around the turn to sit level with Clark heading into the closing stretch, only for his playing partner to post a three-birdie finish to cap off a roller-coaster victory in style.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy's chances of victory slipped away with a bogey on the 17th at the BMW Championship

A level-par 70 was enough for Clark to end the week on 17 under and close out a third PGA Tour victory of the season, following on from the CJ Cup Byron Nelson and the US Open, with Patrick Cantlay claiming solo second to progress through to next week's season-ending Tour Championship.

McIlroy was tied for the lead with three to play but ended four back after a penultimate-hole bogey and Clark's impressive birdie burst, while Gary Woodland, Collin Morikawa and Chris Gotterup shared fourth place.

How Clark held off McIlroy to BMW Championship win

Clark's overnight advantage was immediately cut with a two-shot swing at the first, where he three-putted from 65 feet for bogey as McIlroy holed from 10 feet for birdie.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy makes a dream start on the final round of the BMW Championship to chase Wyndham Clark, who bogeyed the first

McIlroy failed to get up and down to save par at the fourth but holed from seven feet to avoid back-to-back bogeys, as Woodland - two groups ahead - made three birdies in his first five holes to get within two.

Clark bogeyed the par-three sixth after a clunky chip from just off the green, with Woodland halving his advantage by birdieing the par-five eighth before inexplicably topping his tee shot into water at the next.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Woodland made a huge error by topping his tee shot on the ninth at the BMW Championship

McIlroy made a two-putt birdie at the eighth and picked up a shot at the ninth to reach the turn two back, only to pull level with a birdie at the 11th after Clark had started his back nine with a bogey.

Cantlay also briefly shared the lead until a double-bogey at the 11th, while McIlroy and Clark traded pars to leave the pair tied at the top of the leaderboard with three holes to play.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy had overturned a five-shot deficit to share the lead with Wyndham Clark late in the final round

Clark was birdie-free during the final day until he edged ahead with a 15-footer at the 16th, before adding another at the par-five next - after McIlroy went from bunker to bunker and carded a bogey - to extend his advantage.

Cantlay reduced the lead by birdieing each of his final three holes to set the clubhouse target at 14 under, as Clark closed out his fifth PGA Tour win by pouring in a 15-foot birdie to extend his winning margin.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the late birdie burst that saw Wyndham Clark close out BMW Championship victory

"As much as I would have loved to have run away with this, it was fun to get the juices going," Cantlay told CBS Sports. "I think it shows that I'm one of the best players in the world. Three wins in one season is my best year yet, coming off my worst year ever and I'm just very pleased with where I am at right now."

On claiming third, McIlroy said: "I'm still not in a spot where I'm super happy with where my game is or where my swing is, so I just have to keep working on it. It's nice to know even when I'm not super happy with everything I can still piece it together and get it around and still give myself a chance to win tournaments."

Sports.title: Brilliant Beau wins back-to-back Women's Series titles
Sports.content:
Beau Greaves defeated Lisa Ashton and Aileen de Graaf on Sunday to close in on her 60th title on the Women's Series circuit.

Sunday's Women's Series double-header saw Events 19 and 20 take place at the Matiolli Arena, as Greaves returned to winning ways on the circuit after missing yesterday's action.

Greaves opened her account Sunday morning with three consecutive whitewash victories over Jane Hawtin, Sue Lowther and Vicky Pruim respectively,

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Women's World Matchplay final between Beau Greaves and Fallon Sherrock in Blackpool

The 22-year-old was almost denied a 58th Women's Series title, as she fought back from 3-2 down to beat Gemma Hayter to book her spot in the quarter-final stage.

Greaves raced into the semi-final, as she beat Aileen de Graaf 5-1 with an average of over 96, before booking her place in the Event 19 showpiece as she raced past Kirsty Hutchinson 5-2.

In a repeat bout of the 2025 Women's World Matchplay semi-final between 'Beau 'n' Arrow' and Lisa Ashton, it was Greaves' who came out victor in the final as she beat Ashton 5-3.

Despite dropping the opening leg in the final, Greaves responded with three legs of her own in quick succession to gain a two-leg advantage on Ashton, before sealing the victory with a brilliant 14-dart leg.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chris Murphy suggests Greaves should be given more opportunities to play against the men after she won the Women's World Matchplay

Greaves opened her Event 20 campaign in the same manner as she did earlier in the day, winning back-to-back matches in quick succession, beating Leanne Halls and Felicia Bay 4-0.

The Doncaster star - who only dropped three legs in the entire event - won consecutive matches 4-1 over Louise Pearson and Rhian O'Sullivan respectively, before dispatching Angela Kirkwood 5-0 to seal her spot in the final four.

There, she raced into the final, as Greaves beat Karolina Ratajska 5-1, opening her account in that match with a brilliant 11-dart leg.

De Graaf's below-par performance in the final meant that Greaves was victorious once again and claimed her 59th Women's Series, averaging upwards of 91 and whitewashing the Dutchwoman.

Greaves remains on top of the Women's Series rankings, with Ashton and Sherrock solidifying their positions in second and third respectively, as Hayter sits just behind the pair in fourth spot and in the final qualification spot for the 2026/27 World Darts Championship.

Sports.title: Hits and misses: Maresca's Man City experiment gets lucky
Sports.content:
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Manchester City and Bournemouth.

Enzo Maresca described his first Premier League win as Manchester City boss "the perfect day", but also conceded that his side remain a "work in progress" after beating Bournemouth. That was evident for all to see as Marc Guehi hauled up surprisingly in midfield and Rico Lewis was staged at right-back.

Neither will be expected to continue the campaign in those positions. But City are worryingly short of options. Their performance bearing all the hallmarks of the unfinished article Maresca referenced.

Man City will not challenge Arsenal or any side at the top in this condition, with so many of their best stars obviously undercooked. Erling Haaland and Phil Foden were both muted. Elliot Anderson lost more duels than he won. Guehi is just not a central midfielder.

But if City can continue to win games while Maresca figures things out, there is reason for optimism. All of those players will get sharper. Guehi will return to being a defender. And help will arrive from elsewhere, with Ayyoub Bouaddi's signing on the horizon. City know they have work to do before the transfer window shuts.

What felt like an afternoon destined to end in disappointment and frustration morphed into one of success for Maresca. The Italian can take credit for the changes he made in the second half to ensure his Etihad bow ended all smiles. He won't be so lucky every week.

Laura Hunter

Image: Alexander Isak takes a tumble at St James' Park

Alexander Isak was back at St James' Park.

One of the strangest things about his emotional reunion with Newcastle was how little impact he had.

Just under 12 months since that acrimonious departure, the balance of the transfer already feels remarkably different. Liverpool may still have the long-term prize, but on the evidence of this 2-2 draw, Newcastle have got the better of the deal so far.

The Isak who used to glide around this stadium with an effortless swagger was missing.

There are some mitigating circumstances. Injuries have interrupted his rhythm since moving to Liverpool and, when a forward's body isn't right, sharpness and confidence can disappear quickly. This was never going to be an easy afternoon either, with the St James' Park crowd making their feelings known.

But even allowing for all of that, this did not look like the Isak Newcastle supporters remember.

He lacked the movement. The explosiveness. The menace.

Most importantly, he lacked that aura.

There is plenty of time for Isak to change that story yet whether the 'old Isak' will ever resurface is a debatable question.

Lewis Jones

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Newcastle and Liverpool.

Yoane Wissa was signed by Newcastle to be the finisher, not the conductor of the orchestra.

However, against Liverpool the Newcastle forward operated predominantly as a No 10 and, for long periods, ran the show.

Wissa didn't just look sharp again after a difficult spell but Matthias Jaissle appears to have found a role capable of bringing the best out of him.

There was the intensity, of course. Jaissle's football demands it. Newcastle were relentless without the ball, pressing, counter-pressing and trying to suffocate Liverpool whenever possession was lost.

Wissa was at the heart of that.

But what made his performance particularly encouraging was that the running never came at the expense of quality.

He drifted into pockets of space that Liverpool's midfield struggled to control, linked play intelligently and repeatedly looked to turn possession into something dangerous. That was shown by his magnificent burst and pass to set up Joe Willock's goal that made it 2-1.

The Liverpool draw felt like a statement of intent from Newcastle under their new manager. But within the chaos of a 2-2 classic, Wissa's performance may have been the most interesting subplot.

Lewis Jones

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Brighton and Aston Villa.

The Aston Villa fans began their afternoon on the south coast in fine voice. They weren't shy in singing and reminding everyone about being champions of Europe but that bravado would have quickly turned to concern after four Brighton goals in 31 first-half minutes left them shell-shocked.

Villa arrived at the Amex Stadium having sold a host of star names since last season's Europa League triumph and they started the game without a recognised striker amid transfer speculation surrounding the absent Ollie Watkins.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez was also missing from the matchday squad amid talk he and Watkins will join Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Morgan Rogers through the exit door.

What was left behind struggled at the Amex. Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof looked uncertain at the back, while Joao Gomes suffered a nightmare debut, being shown a straight red card. They also lacked a focal point in the absence of Watkins as they tasked Emiliano Buendia, Ross Barkley and full debutant George Hemmings with leading the line.

The mauling at Brighton only heightens Villa's need to get their squad in shape ahead of the transfer deadline on Tuesday September 1, with the speculation an unwelcome distraction for Unai Emery.

Oliver Yew

Aston Villa became only the second team in Premier League history to concede four goals, receive a red card and score an own goal in the first half of a match, after Southampton against Manchester United in February 2021.



Meanwhile, Brighton are only the fourth side to score four goals in the first half of their opening game of a Premier League season, after Bolton in 2001/02 (vs Leicester), Manchester United in 2006/07 (vs Fulham), and Liverpool in 2019/20 (vs Norwich).

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jack Hinshelwood scores a rapid-fire brace to make it FOUR for Brighton in the first half against Aston Villa.

Brighton just always find a way.

Fabian Hurzeler's side have had a summer overhaul of their own, losing key players and with further departures set to come, it's been a testing time down on the south coast.

Hurzeler has already had to say goodbye to Danny Welbeck, Jan Paul van Hecke, Joel Veltman and James Milner, to name just a few players, while Carlos Baleba and Yakubu Minteh could also be on their way out before the transfer window closes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Maxim De Cuyper taps home Brighton's second goal against Aston Villa inside 20 minutes.

But like they have done time and time again in recent seasons, Brighton coped.

Not only did they cope, the 4-0 win over Aston Villa provided a statement of intent for this season with a performance full of intensity as the Brighton show gets set to roll on.

Oliver Yew

Sports.title: Nev: Wirtz and Isak Liverpool's biggest disappointments - they must improve
Sports.content:
Gary Neville called on Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak to improve after a year of "being kind to" Liverpool's £200m+ duo, but said he had faith the pair would come good despite being their "biggest disappointments" at Newcastle.

Isak played the entire 90 minutes on his first return to St James' Park since becoming the Premier League's most expensive player last summer, though offered little more than Wirtz who was substituted just after the hour mark for Alexis Mac Allister.

Both had offered hope in pre-season of better times to come after encouraging performances in Liverpool's friendlies under new boss Andoni Iraola, but neither could transfer that optimism into Sunday's league opener at St James' Park.

Speaking on the Gary Neville Podcast, Neville said: "The big thing for Liverpool is they've got this quarter-of-a-billion-pound front two, Isak and Wirtz and bloody hell, we've been kind to them.

"They're going to have to start playing sooner or later or else, to be fair, they're going to get quite a lot of criticism. For a start, they're too nice, and if you're going to be nice, you'd better be incredible at football.

"I don't see the tenacity in Wirtz in particular. I just see a nice player moving around the pitch, not really ever looking like he's busting a gut to do anything.

"Now, that can happen. Sometimes players have that flow about them, but I want to put a rocket up him. I want to put a rocket up him because there's ability there, there's talent there, the understanding of his position.

"The biggest disappointment for me [Sunday] is those two."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Newcastle and Liverpool.

Despite their issues at St James' Park, Neville said he retained confidence the pair, who had impressed so consistently at Newcastle and Bayer Leverkusen respectively, could recreate that form on Merseyside with a year each under their belts at Anfield.

"I've watched them both for 12 months, and I do actually have faith in them," he said. "I think Isak's an exceptional player and we've seen it.

"I never saw anybody give Gabriel and Saliba or Van Dijk and Konate a tougher time as Isak did when he played at Newcastle in a black and white shirt. I've seen him be devastating.

"Now Liverpool fans and his team-mates and coaching staff, they need to see that - because that's £125m they've spent on him.

"And then Wirtz, he needs to sort himself out. Enough's enough now, we've talked about him enough. He's young and he's come to a different country - and I'm all for willing him on.

"They have both had a bit of a free ride. Obviously Isak was injured last season but Arne Slot loses his job, and Wirtz has played like that, so let's be clear, this has got me to start some real focus now.

"I can see a real player there, but can't keep watching this stuff and he's been subbed after an hour and they need a goal, but they're 2-1 down, so no that's not right."

Image: Liverpool had to rely on a Dominik Szoboszlai last-gasp penalty to earn them an opening-weekend draw at Newcastle

'Wirtz should be closer to Isak'

Wirtz had impressed as a shadow striker in pre-season, particularly in Liverpool's eventual 3-2 defeat to Monaco a fortnight before their league opener.

But having played further away from Isak at St James Park, the 23-year-old was urged to return to that role by Neville to have a greater impact on games for the rest of the season, having contributed just eight league goal involvements since his nine-figure move from Leverkusen a year ago.

"Sometimes I think he moves around too much," he said. "Sometimes I don't think he's close enough to his striker, I don't think he understands where the game's going to be won and lost.

"When I played football and No 10s sometimes drifted too deep, or too wide, they would get a right rollicking off our manager.

"The game's not going to be won out there, the game's not going to be won back there, the game's going to be won in the final third, in and around the box.

"Combining with your striker, getting crosses in, getting little passes, getting little side passes down the side of the centre-backs, being close enough to your forward so that you can combine with him. And I don't see him combining with Isak.

"I just feel like Wirtz has got to think about being involved in the build-up less and think about being a second striker. He's got to think about his output and what he needs to do, and that is feed Isak with little passes down the side of centre-backs. He might only get the ball two or three times in that position in tight games where teams are lying deep."

Sports.title: Ceferin brands Infantino’s failed World Cup plan as ‘even worse than the Super League’
Sports.content:
The Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, has described Gianni Infantino’s doomed attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup as “even worse than the Super League plan” and warned his embattled Fifa counterpart that he will face an opponent if he runs for re-election next March.

Ceferin has led Uefa’s firm collective stance against the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, which was shelved amid widespread opposition at the start of August. Uefa are pushing for Infantino to quit, also drawing on support from Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation, and are yet to drop a threat to boycott Fifa competitions while talks are under way with Concacaf to set up a combined Nations League tournament.

In an interview with the podcast The Rest is Politics: Leading, Ceferin denounced Infantino’s project as more damaging than the breakaway Super League that was shelved in 2021 after large-scale protests. “I think this plan is even worse than the Super League plan,” he said. “In the first case, super-important clubs wanted to do their own league, which is wrong and would destroy football. But in this case, football would be literally sold.

“I’m absolutely sure that the [FFE] plan is dead. For me, the most important thing is that we stopped another try to sell the sport. It’s hard to imagine what kind of people would sell the sport that belongs to everyone.”

Earlier this month it was reported that Infantino had held talks about running the Super League under Fifa branding. Ceferin is confident that any revival of that plan would be decades away. “It might happen in 20 years, you never know, but for now we cooperate with everyone in a great way. I’m sure it cannot happen in the next 10 years,” he said.

Infantino spent much of the weekend courting support from Concacaf members at a meeting in the Dominican Republic, infuriating many of those present. Ceferin, who revealed the pair had not been in contact since the FFE scandal broke, believes the Fifa president’s path to survival is narrowing.

“I didn’t speak with him, he didn’t contact me since this happened,” he said. “But there are two options. One option is that he realises that he doesn’t have the support, and that’s not only political support of the ones who vote, but the political support of the football community, the political support of fans, the political support of the players, former players, coaches.

“And the second option [is] that he goes to the elections in March, but in that case, I think he will have a candidate against him. I don’t know yet who.” The Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, has been tipped as a potential opponent for Infantino if he chooses to run in Rabat.

Ceferin has proponents of his own but ruled out making his own bid for the Fifa presidency. “My credibility is much, much, much higher if I’m not interested in the position,” he said. The Slovenian is expected to run unopposed for a fourth term at the helm of Uefa, with the election due next April.

Asked whether Infantino had become too close to Donald Trump, with whom he forged a close relationship before the recent World Cup, Ceferin said: “To be honest, I think you are naive if you think that a politician like that, or any politician, is your good friend. The moment you are a problem, you stop being a friend of a politician.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

That friendship came under the spotlight last month when Trump said he had called Infantino to ask for a review of the red card given to the US striker Folarin Balogun, whose ban for the last-16 tie against Belgium was later suspended. “That was more than shocking,” Ceferin said. “We have rules and if you don’t respect your own rules, then the game doesn’t make any sense. That’s shocking and, trust me, almost everybody was shocked. Just not everybody dared to speak.”

Meanwhile, in a fresh show of European opposition to Infantino, the six Nordic football associations issued a statement saying they had “lost confidence in the Fifa president and have serious concerns about the governance and high-level decision making of the organisation”. They asked for binding assurances that Fifa will never again “open its governance or competitions to private ownership” and called for a full third-party review into the FFE scheme.

Earlier in August the Norwegian Football Federation was the first member association to call directly for Infantino to step down.

Infantino travelled straight from the Dominican Republic to Paris on Sunday, attending the closing ceremony of the Esports World Cup. Television footage showed him exchanging greetings with the president of France, Emmanuel Macron.

Sports.title: Newcastle and Liverpool crank up the entertainment for emotional send-off | Sam Dalling
Sports.content:
It’s 4.35pm on Tyneside. William Osula sets Anthony Elanga away, slightly right of centre and just short of 50,000 draw collective breaths. Pace is no issue; Elanga has no shortage of that, and Milos Kerkez won’t catch him.

But Newcastle fans have seen this clip before and remember the ending. Muscles tighten, cheeks clench, as they brace themselves for it to start again like it carried on before. (Yet) another memeable‑moment inbound.

A tiny part of each of them, though, thinks: “Wait, hang on, this is a new season, a fresh start.” The slate is not just clean but has been entirely replaced and is now AI-operated.

Elanga takes a touch, a tad heavier ideal but it pushes the ball away from Alisson. A moment of composure follows and Newcastle lead. An entirely goalless league season passed after Elanga’s £55m transfer from Nottingham Forest and now, within five minutes of a new one, his drought is broken.

Elanga missed a much easier opportunity against Aston Villa on the 2025-26 opening day, and his confidence never recovered. Can you walk back through a sliding door?

Nearly two hours later, there remain just a few precious seconds for Liverpool to salvage something. Victor Muñoz is brought down clumsily by Lewis Hall. Dominik Szoboszlai converts the resulting penalty. 2-2.

Muñoz apparently gave Newcastle positive noises about joining them during summer. Then, in a flexing of financial muscle, Liverpool met the Osasuna forward’s release clause and to Anfield he went. What was that about sliding doors?

View image in fullscreen Liverpool’s Víctor Muñoz – a summer target for Newcastle – is brought down by Lewis Hall to hand the visitors a late penalty. Photograph: Ian Hodgson/AP

Those two goals bookended an afternoon that was, if you want to do go down that road, a fitting tribute to the recently departed Kevin Keegan. Entertaining but flawed.

As a term, legend is so chronically overused now that it is meaningless. But Keegan is a prime example of the word’s proper application. Shortly before kick-off everyone present paid an emotional tribute to him. Legend. Hero. King. All subjective labels essentially turned objective.

With Liverpool, Keegan’s seven trophies in six years – including three titles and the European Cup – set the club up to be the behemoth they now are. Across three spells at Newcastle, he jabbed syringes of hope into a flailing, helpless shell.

St James’ Park is not quite the house that Keegan built, but it is no stretch to say it is the house built because of him. Without his steering Newcastle to Second Division safety in 1992 as manager, the club in its current guise might not exist.

So, why does Keegan remain so adored? He is in effect a symbol of what football once was and should still be, can be even. Maybe.

Forget spreadsheets, financial acronyms and PR-doused messaging. Ignore expected this and that, low blocks and cancelling each other out. Find the joy. Forget perfect; take a risk. Failure and fallibility? Both absolutely OK.

Those are sentiments Andoni Iraola and Matthias Jaissle would do well to remember as they look to settle themselves into new gigs.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The former, with Liverpool being champions two seasons ago, will be under the greater pressure. A repeat of his start at Bournemouth, where he won only at the 10th time of asking, would be difficult to tolerate.

There were promising signs for Iraola, sure. Jérémy Jacquet grew into his debut. Cody Gakpo had only just whipped a strike narrowly off target before his fine equaliser just after half-time. Rio Ngumoha was quiet but that he has impressed sufficiently to start the season opener is itself a plus.

View image in fullscreen Florian Wirtz (centre) and former Newcastle man Alexander Isak again both struggled to make an impact for Liverpool. Photograph: George Wood/Getty Images

But there were familiar failings, too. The full-backs looked shaky and Iraola needs more (much, much more) from both the sums and the whole of the £241m Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak combo.

Isak is about as popular in Newcastle as government-mandated balaclava wearing in a heatwave would be, but the stick-cum-abuse he received didn’t seem to bother him. However, what should keep Isak up at night is how he can and must refind the level that rightly saw him tagged one of the Premier League’s best forwards not so long ago. A skied left-footed effort was the closest he came to silencing the heckles.

Jaissle is likely to get more slack. Everyone is aware of what Newcastle have, where they are and, most pertinent, what they have lost.

Something fresh was absolutely needed but that requires time and patience. There are, and will continue to be, warts, imperfections, things that Bruno Guimarães might have done.

A midfield pair sold for north of £180m were replaced on Sunday by a double pivot with a combined aged of 38 and less than 50 league starts. Lewis Miley and Sean Steur looked the part but made mistakes. That they did so seeking the positive option will only endear them to fans. As will more similar performances from Yoane Wissa. A player who last season looked sluggish and largely static, was suddenly full of everything in the No 10 role.

A decent start. Room for improvement. Apply that to both sides.

Sports.title: ‘Call his agent’: Emery feels Watkins should explain absence from Villa’s rout by Brighton
Sports.content:
Unai Emery did nothing to deny that Ollie Watkins had refused to play for Aston Villa in their sobering 4-0 defeat by Brighton at the Amex on Sunday. The head coach had a selection crisis up front with Brian Madjo and Tammy Abraham injured. However, he did not include Watkins in the matchday squad as the England striker considers a move to Al-Hilal in Saudi Arabia.

Emery was forced to rely on the attacking midfielder Emiliano Buendía as an emergency striker and his team disappeared without trace on the south coast. They were 4-0 down after 31 minutes and had their new signing João Gomes sent off on his debut in the 40th minute. Gomes kicked up and out at the Brighton striker Georginio Rutter after being dispossessed by him.

Al-Hilal have made a number of bids for Watkins, all of which have been rejected. It is understood the 30-year-old is open to the move and Emery talked on Friday like a manager who was realistic about the sale happening. Villa would plainly like to replace Watkins should he depart as they approach the end of another difficult summer window. They have already sold Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne and Youri Tielemans, while they are expected to move on Emiliano Martínez.

Emery was asked why he had not picked Watkins against Brighton. “This question is for him,” he said. “I can answer only with my silence.” Emery was then asked if Watkins had refused to play, to which he said: “I think you can call him and you can call his agent and he can respond.”

The Guardian have contacted Watkins’s agent for comment.

“He [Watkins] can only explain his answer, I can’t,” Emery added, after being asked if he felt let down by Watkins.

Emery reported that Madjo would be out for “two weeks more … more or less” while attacking midfielder Johan Manzambi – who has been the club’s marquee summer signing – would “need maybe some days more [than that]”. He was unclear about a timeframe for Abraham’s return.

Quick Guide How do I 

Emery talked up the resistance of his players in the second half against Brighton and said he was optimistic about finding solutions for the season ahead. But he returned to the difficult preparations for the opening fixture, noting that: “Two strikers are injured and another striker gives his answer.”

The head coach added: “This problem [with the transfer market] … we had every season and every season we overcame it. It’s something we have to accept and always we reacted, especially the players. This is something hard for us every year but we are calm. With this result, it’s more difficult to explain but calm, work, be positive and find solutions for the next week and after the transfer window.”

Sports.title: Maresca concedes Manchester City ‘a work in progress’ after hair-raising escape
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca said Manchester City remain a “work in progress” after Sunday’s last-gasp win over Bournemouth at the Etihad Stadium.

Marc Guéhi’s 85th-minute equaliser and Josko Gvardiol’s 91st-minute winner gave City’s new manager victory in his first game, after Marcus Tavernier’s first-half strike for the visitors.

Maresca thought his side performed similarly to last Sunday’s 3-0 Community Shield loss to Arsenal. “I feel in the same position as after Arsenal,” the Italian said. “It’s normal you judge after results but I don’t see big changes. Unfortunately, this is a work in progress and I’m looking for solutions. For sure when you win games it helps.

“If you think of the Premier League – it won’t happen that you will concede nothing. The goal we conceded was their first shot. They had two or three dangerous moments but it’s how you react. We’ve still got [Erling] Haaland, Elliot [Anderson], Marc [Guéhi], Nico O’Reilly [who all started], who are in pre-season still. It’s a huge difference in terms of physicality and we are going to get better and better.”

Before the game City unfurled a huge tifo bearing his image that said: “Welcome back Enzo.” He said: “It is the perfect day. I was very pleased to see the banner when the game started. We gave them [fans] the joy at the end. It was quite emotional. The spirit was fantastic. It’s a game we deserved to win [but] you don’t need to wait for the last five minutes. We missed chances, then they scored and it became more complicated.”

Maresca fielded Guéhi in an unfamiliar midfield role. “I know Marc from [ Crystal] Palace and I always thought he could play as a midfielder because he is very good,” the manager said. “So we tried it for a few days and I think he was quite good. He gives us a solution for the future,.”

In his first game managing Bournemouth, Marco Rose came close to leading them to a first away win against City. “We’re competitors, we came here to win for the first time,” said the German. “We were in a good way to do so. But we did many good things. We have a lot of things to improve. At the end, how the game went was quite unlucky to lose that way. We had two situations – one corner kick and one attacking [move] – when we defended too passively.
