“We need to defend the corner better and the second goal was just too passive. We always try to push up – we want to defend higher. Here you need to find the right triggers and it’s hard to press. We did it really well until the end.”

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 3: Birmingham City
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 12th (NB: this is not necessarily Tom Garry’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 1st (WSL2)

Prospects

Founding members of the Women’s Super League when it launched in 2011, Birmingham are back in the top flight after four years in the second tier, having won promotion as WSL2 champions on the final day of last season. After a decent summer transfer window, Birmingham look to have a fighting chance of staying up, and perhaps even surprising a few teams, while off the pitch they are the best-equipped of the three promoted sides to cement themselves in the top division.

Forwards Lily Crosthwaite and Wilma Leidhammar and defender Neve Herron, are all 23-years-old and likely to continue improving. Birmingham have also added players with WSL experience, such as the former Brighton goalkeeper Sophie Baggaley and the centre-back Millie Turner.

Inconsistency was nearly their downfall last season; they won the most games in WSL2, but also lost six times. They delivered under pressure, boosted by the performances of Leidhammar after her club-record arrival in January, ensuring they avoided a repeat of the heartbreak of 12 months earlier when they missed out on promotion on the final day. Nonetheless, Birmingham are still a long way off from the days when they were runners-up in the top tier and their first two away fixtures are against Manchester City and Chelsea. They also host fellow promoted sides Crystal Palace and Charlton relatively early in the campaign and those home fixtures could be key to building confidence.

Off-field picture

Birmingham’s women’s team were sold to the club’s ownership group in February, with Shelby Companies Limited – an affiliate of Knighthead Capital Management – owning 97%. The remaining 3% was purchased by investors including the former England midfielder Karen Carney and the four-time grand slam tennis champion Kim Clijsters. The club appear to be in a relatively healthy position with ambitious owners determined to reestablish the 2012 FA Cup winners as a regular, competitive presence in the WSL. They train at the recently renovated Knighthead Performance Centre, on the same site as the men’s team’s former Wast Hills training base, with a new gym among other extensive refurbishments.

The manager

Amy Merricks has been in charge since April 2024 She holds a Uefa Pro Licence and was 30 years old when she was appointed by Birmingham. She has previously coached within the England youth setup as well as at Gillingham, Millwall and Brighton, where was stepped up to be interim manager three times.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Lisa Naalsund arrives from Manchester United to boost Birmingham’s midfield. Photograph: DeFodi Images/Getty Images

Birmingham have recruited players with international experience, including the Canada defender Marie Levasseur from Montpellier, but their two most eyebrow-raising additions are Turner and Lisa Naalsund from Manchester United. They were starting members of United’s FA Cup-winning side of 2024 and played in a Women’s Champions League quarter-final as recently as April. Naalsund will be an influential force in the midfield – she has won 39 caps and was part of Norway’s squad at last year’s Euros.

Stat attack

Birmingham topped WSL2 last season despite not scoring the most goals or conceding the fewest. One stat they led was big chances, Opta’s metric for opportunities where it is reasonable to expect the attacker to score. While their tally will be much harder to repeat in the top flight, their attacking process looks in good order.

Set for a breakthrough

There is plenty of excitement at Birmingham about another of their new signings, the 19-year-old France youth forward Chancelle Effa Effa, who arrived from Le Havre for a fee understood to be about €120,000 (£100,000) this month. She broke into Le Havre’s first team at the age of 15 and scored 17 times in 28 games for France’s Under-17 and Under-19 teams, having helped France win 2023’s Under-17 Euros.

What they say …

“We know it’s going to be a massive challenge, but it’s a challenge that, as players, you thrive upon. As long as we can take that togetherness, that relentlessness, into the games, I’m sure we’re going to be just fine” – Chelsea Cornet.

Where are they playing their home games?

Birmingham play their home fixtures at St Andrew’s, which has been the women’s team’s home since 2021. They set a club record attendance for a women’s game there on the final day of the 2024-25 season – 8,749. Long-term, the club have announced plans to build a new women’s team stadium as part of the ‘Sports Quarter’, which also includes the proposed 62,000-seater men’s team Powerhouse Stadium as well as an indoor arena, training ground facilities and a new railway station.

Sports.title: European football: Torres double rescues PSG point after Rennes threaten shock win
Sports.content:
Ferran Torres came off the bench to score a late double ⁠on his debut as Paris Saint-Germain rallied from two goals down to draw ⁠2-2 with ⁠hosts Rennes in their Ligue 1 season opener on Sunday. Sebastian Szymanski and Esteban Lepaul gave ⁠the home side a 2-0 lead at half-time but PSG piled on the pressure in ⁠the second period and were rewarded with a point.

Rennes led ​inside nine minutes as ‌Szymanski’s shot went ‌in off the post to provide the perfect start ‌to the season for the hosts. Désiré Doué thought he had levelled for PSG, but his effort was ruled out for offside, and the home side made it 2-0 seven minutes before the break. Przemyslaw Frankowski found space ‌on the right wing and his low cross into the box was turned into the ​net by Lepaul.

PSG pulled a goal back with 19 minutes remaining as Torres’ clever run beat the offside trap and he collected a Fabián ⁠Ruiz pass and scored his first goal for the ​club since ​his move from Barcelona. Torres ​then levelled the scores in the 83rd ​minute, and again ‌Ruiz was ​the provider ​with a cross from the left, as the Spanish duo dragged their side back into the contest but could not help them find a winner.

Atlético Madrid salvaged a 2-2 draw against Villarreal in La Liga despite having defender Robin Le Normand sent off. Giuliano Simeone grabbed his team a draw after penalties from Gerard Moreno and Georges Mikautadze put Villarreal in front following Marc Pubill’s 59th-minute opener for the hosts.

The Atlético head coach, Diego Simeone, brought Julián Álvarez on as a second-half substitute to a chorus of boos from home supporters. The forward walked down the tunnel alone at the end, while his teammates were thanking the Atlético supporters.

View image in fullscreen Julián Alvarez leaves the pitch at the end of the game after Atlético Madrid fans booed him during the 2-2 draw with Villarreal. Photograph: Europa Press Sports/Europa Press/Getty Images

Barcelona began their title defence ⁠and bid for a third successive crown with ⁠a 5-0 victory ⁠at ​Elche as Raphinha and Fermín López ⁠scored twice each.

Mohamed Salah scored his first goals for Trabzonspor with a brace in their 2-1 win over Istanbul Basaksehir. The former Liverpool forward joined the Super Lig side on a two-year deal at the start of August and made his debut for the club from the bench in their 1-1 draw at Kasimpasa last week. Salah was named in the starting lineup for the clash with Basaksehir and made an instant impact, opening the scoring in the eighth minute.

Basaksehir levelled in the 19th minute when Eldor Shomurodov slotted home from the penalty spot, but Salah restored his side’s lead just three minutes into the second half. His brace was enough to clinch victory for Trabzonspor, who return to Super Lig action on 31 August against Amed SK.

In Serie A, Ruben Amorim started his Milan reign with a 2-1 victory at Torino. The second-half substitute Adrien Rabiot set up Alphadjo Cissè’s 64th-minute opener and then scored himself three minutes later. Ché Adams scored a stunning consolation deep in stoppage time for Torino.

View image in fullscreen Adrien Rabiot scores Milan’s second goal against Torino. Photograph: Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images

Juventus secured a 1-0 away win against newly promoted Frosinone, but failed to impress in their opening match of the season.

Juve, who finished sixth last season, secured all three points thanks to Gleison Bremer’s 22nd-minute header. Luciano Spalletti’s side went on to dominate but failed to put the game beyond doubt. The goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario, on loan from Tottenham, picked up a leg injury and had to be substituted late on, which nearly cost Juve as Frosinone pressed hard in stoppage time, hitting the crossbar.

Another of the newly promoted teams, Monza, were thrashed 4-1 by the champions, Inter, on Saturday in the season opener. Lecce made a strong start to the season against the third promoted side, Venezia, on Sunday as they defeated their hosts 2-0 courtesy of second-half goals from Olaf Gorter and Tiago Gabriel.

The Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane was voted the 2026 player of the year in Germany by an association of sports journalists on Sunday, finishing ahead of teammate Michael Olise. Kicker magazine revealed the results of its yearly polls of members of the Association of German Sports Journalists. Kane, the England captain, won the award after a stellar season in which he won the Bundesliga and German Cup while Bayern also reached the Champions League semi-finals. Bayern’s Vincent Kompany was named coach of the year, while their women’s captain, Giulia Gwinn, won the award for best female player.

Sports.title: Manchester City agree deal worth up to €100m for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi
Sports.content:
Manchester City have agreed a deal with Lille worth €95m (£81.4m) plus €5m in potential add-ons for Ayyoub Bouaddi, with the Morocco midfielder’s arrival to take the club’s summer spend to nearly £200m after Elliot Anderson’s £116m signing earlier in the window.

The 18-year-old was stood down from Lille’s Ligue 1 match against Angers on Sunday before a medical with City and his transfer becoming official in the next few days.

Bouaddi, who operates mainly as a No 6, started five of Morocco’s six games at the World Cup tournament this summer, including the 2-0 quarter-final defeat by France. That was only his eighth international appearance. His Lille debut came in an October 2023 Conference League group game– at 16 years and three days, it made him the youngest footballer to play in the competition.

The majority of the fee for Bouaddi will come from the £65m sale of Rodri to Barcelona, which was sealed last week.

Anderson, who is making his debut in City’s Premier League opener against Bournemouth on Sunday, can play as No 6 or No 8, so Bouaddi may not go directly into Enzo Maresca’s starting XI.

City remain interested in Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández, also a midfielder. The west London club want £120m for the Argentinian but City are thought to value him at a lower figure.

Sports.title: West Brom surge back to floor Flemming-less Burnley amid transfer speculation
Sports.content:
West Brom’s head coach, James Morrison, insisted his side must “stay humble” after Isaac Price inspired them to a 3-1 comeback win against promotion favourites Burnley in the Championship at the Hawthorns. The Northern Ireland international scored twice in the second half after setting up Harry Whitwell’s equaliser to cancel out Callum Styles’s early own goal.

“I felt it was a top performance. I enjoyed it at times for the intensity with the lads willing to run for each other,” Morrison said. “We did the basics really well – we won tackles, and when we lost the ball, we ran back and when the opportunities were given to us, we took advantage.

“I felt like Burnley couldn’t handle our intensity, and I could smell that at half-time, so the message was to up the intensity.”

Burnley, without injured star striker Zian Flemming amid intense speculation of a move, failed to match their lofty billing in a disappointing second-half display. Albion continued their 100% start to the season, gaining their third straight win in all competitions and second in the league to lie second in the early table, behind Millwall on goal difference.

In a fast and furious start, there were two goals in the first 18 minutes. Styles put into his own net in the eighth minute from Jacob Bruun Larsen’s cross. Albion complained that Hannibal Mejbri fouled Felix Horn Myhre in the buildup 70 yards away, with several passages of play unfolding before the goal. Styles had to make contact to prevent Oliver Sonne getting the chance but the ball hit his left heel and it flew into the net.

Whitwell equalised on 18 minutes when he slotted home low to Max Weiss’s left from 12 yards for the 20-year-old’s first league goal for Albion. Burnley appeared wrongfooted by Jimmy-Jay Morgan’s flick-on from Price’s cross, before Bashir Humphreys failed to clear. But it was Burnley who went closest to scoring again when Bruun Larsen sidefooted against the foot of the post from Marcus Edwards’s searching cross.

View image in fullscreen Harry Whitwell’s strike pulls the Baggies level. Photograph: Ryan Browne/Shutterstock

It was a different story after the break. Inspired by Price, Albion produced a dominant second-half performance, with the perfect start. Price put them ahead for the first time, in the 46th minute, curling the ball beyond Weiss, who had strayed five yards off his line, into the far corner. The goal came from a loose ball when Morgan tried to help back Styles’s cross and Hannibal challenged.

Burnley made a triple change in the 57th minute with the arrival of Ugo Raghouber, Zeki Amdouni, and Dastan Satpayev. Amdouni tried to test Max O’Leary with a rising, curling effort from 20 yards but it flew straight at the Albion keeper.

Instead it was Albion who struck next to effectively seal it, after Humphreys upended Whitwell for a clear penalty. Price made no mistake from the spot, firing low to Weiss’s right with the keeper going the wrong way.

Afterwards, Morrison said: “We enjoy competing against the so-called bigger teams and we competed really well today. We don’t want to get carried away. We have to keep our feet on the ground, keep working hard and stay humble.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Burnley head coach, Nicky Hayen, said: “I think we didn’t have the energy, desire and hunger of the home team. You also have to give credit to West Brom. You can always say we played a bad game but they had the structure, a lot of good energy, hunger and desire.

“We had problems and no solutions. I didn’t expect this – it was an eye-opener for everyone, myself included.

Morrison went on to defend Aune Heggebø, as the Norway striker missed Sunday’s game following his retrospective Football Association two-match ban for “deception of a match official”. The sanction came after the incident against Norwich when his goal went in off his hand. Albion have appealed against the ban.

“We were really frustrated and shocked. Bo was disappointed so we had to back him and we wanted to appeal,” said Morrison. “He was deemed to have cheated the referee which he didn’t. Yes the ball hit his hand but with the pace of the cross and the keeper touching it, it’s very hard to get out of the way.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa have second bid to sign England international as potential Ezri Konsa replacement rejected
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have second bid to sign England international as potential Ezri Konsa replacement rejected

Aston Villa have had an improved offer for Taylor Harwood-Bellis rejected by Southampton, talkSPORT understands.

Villa are looking to sign a new centre-back before the end of the summer transfer window on September 1 with Ezri Konsa completing a £50million move to Arsenal earlier in the week.

2 Villa's first offer is some £10million below Southampton's valuation of the player Credit: Getty

Tosin Adarabioyo and Fikayo Tomori are among a list of centre-back targets for Villa.

Another option is Harwood-Bellis, although Villa's offers have been rebuffed with Saints valuing him at £30million.

The first offer is understood to be a package worth £20m, and the second is an improved one but still not to the satisfaction of the Championship club.

talkSPORT understands that Villa are confident they will get a deal done, however.

Harwood-Bellis is a graduate of the Manchester City academy before making a permanent move to Southampton in 2024.

He initially joined on loan for the 2023/24 season, with his move then made permanent for a £20m fee after promotion to the top flight.

Harwood-Bellis, who is engaged to and is set to have a child with Roy Keane's daughter Leah, has made 134 appearances in defence for the Saints and been captain on numerous occasions.

The 24-year-old is also an England international as he earned his sole cap and scored against the Republic of Ireland in November 2024.

Who have Villa sold this summer?

Villa have experienced a summer of big change, despite winning the Europa League at the end of last season.

Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers and Lucas Digne are among the key departures for Unai Emery's side.

2 Villa need a new defender with Konsa sealing a move to Arsenal Credit: Getty

Ollie Watkins is pushing for a move to Al Hilal having missed Villa's 4-0 defeat at Brighton on Sunday, with Unai Emery hinting the striker refused to play.

Meanwhile, Emi Martinez could still leave amid a failed transfer to Juventus.

Should the pair exit Villa Park along with Konsa, then only five of the starting XI that beat SC Freiburg in the Europa League will be left.

They would be Matty Cash, Pau Torres, Victor Lindelof, John McGinn and Emi Buendia.

However, Villa have been active in terms of incomings, with Swiss star Johan Manzambi joining in a £51.2m move from Freiburg.

Joao Gomes, who endured a Villa debut from hell on Sunday, then joined from West Midlands rivals Wolves for £35m.

On Wednesday, Villa completed the signings of Matteo Ruggeri and Zion Zuzuki.

The former has arrived from Atletico Madrid, whilst the latter signed from Parma.

Sports.title: Footballer to have cheekbone reconstruction surgery after sickening collision with opponent
Sports.content:
Footballer to have cheekbone reconstruction surgery after sickening collision with opponent

A non-league footballer will undergo cheek reconstruction surgery after a horror collision with an opponent.

Joe Tennent, who plays for Dartford FC in the Isthmian Premier League, was slammed into by a Welling United striker.



2 Tennent was crunched to the ground by the brutal challenge that caused his injury

Tennent was looking to play the ball out from defence before Nahum Melvin-Lambert chased him down and smashed into him.

Melvin-Lambert charged into the Dartford star and seemed to connect with his right arm on Tennent's head.

The sickening moment left Tennent in a heap on the ground and he eventually had to be substituted after the incident.



Meanwhile, Melvin-Lambert was only booked for the foul.

Dartford went on to lose the game 4-0 to Welling on Saturday.

Update on Tennent issued

Dartford then gave an update on Tennent on Sunday afternoon.

The non-league side revealed that he was going to have to undergo surgery for his serious facial injuries.

The club wrote: "Joe sustained displaced facial fractures and will undergo cheekbone reconstruction surgery on Wednesday.



"We wish Joe and his family our very best and a speedy recovery.

"The club will explore official channels following the incident."

2 Tennent was left completely flattened by the horrendous collision

Immediate concern

Dartford boss Ben Greenhalgh was concerned about Tennent post-match and believed his injury played a big part in his side's loss.



Greenhalgh said: “I think a really big, key part of today was losing Joe Tennent.... it was a derby game so we knew there were going to be moments.

"I can’t blame the ref for the game. That has changed it but our second-half performance was really poor.

“We lost Joe and I’m not saying we capitulated, but we went a bit off-script.

“I am disappointed to lose Joe in that manner. I don’t know how it works from here onwards.



“It didn’t seem like a concussion from what we’re told, but it’s a possible broken jaw that doesn’t sound good at all.”

Sports.title: Julian Alvarez ordered down tunnel by Atletico Madrid as fans wildly boo Arsenal-linked star
Sports.content:
Julian Alvarez was left humiliated as he faced backlash from the Atletico Madrid fans amid his persistent transfer rumours.

Alvarez openly admitted in June that he wanted to leave Atletico and join La Liga rivals Barcelona to 'fulfill his dream'.



2 Alvarez faced some huge backlash at Atletico's game on Sunday Credit: Getty

Barca had an £86million bid rejected before those comments, while Arsenal are also interested in signing the Argentinian.

talkSPORT understands that the Gunners are still actively exploring a move for Alvarez before the transfer window closes.

And they may have received a boost in their bid to sign him after he was hounded by Atletico's supporters on Sunday.



Alvarez angered his own club's fan base by admitting his wish to leave and join Barca, with an exit now seemingly looking inevitable.

What happened to Alvarez?

Diego Simeone named Alvarez as a substitute for Atletico's first home game of the new La Liga season against Villarreal.



As his name appeared on the big screens at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano, wild boos and loud whistles rang out.

Footage showed him sitting and looking solemn on the bench as he faced some huge backlash from the stands.



It got worse for Alvarez too, as Simeone then decided to bring him on, with him being met with even more boos and whistles.

Atletico went on to draw 2-2 with Villarreal on the day, but post-match, things managed to hit a new low for Alvarez.

As his teammates stayed as a group to clap their fans after the full-time whistle, he walked straight down the tunnel alone, leading to further backlash and a scarf being thrown down at him.

2 Simeone says the decision for Alvarez to go down the tunnel was made above him Credit: Getty



Why did Alvarez walk away from the fans?

Alvarez faced a massive negative reaction as supporters assumed that he had chosen to walk down the tunnel alone.

But manager Simeone explained that he was actually told to leave his teammates and not stand in front of the fans.

"The club staff told me that the club decided Julian should not go over with his teammates to greet the fans, and that it was not Julián’s decision," Simeone said post-match.

"The club made the decision to keep him away and have him head to the dressing room."



On the fans' reaction to Alvarez throughout the afternoon, he added: "No, I’m not in a position to give advice to the fans. I think I need to focus on my work, which is to give my best on the sporting side for the good of Atlético de Madrid."

Meanwhile, Alvarez's teammate and Simeone's son, Giuliano Simeone, stood by his fellow Argentina international.

He said: "Julian is a top player, and we stand by him. We have to support him, and as long as he’s part of our team, we’ll fight alongside him until the very end.”

Sports.title: Brighton fan dies after being taken unwell at Aston Villa match
Sports.content:
Brighton fan dies after being taken unwell at Aston Villa match

Brighton have announced that a fan has sadly died after being taken unwell at their match against Aston Villa on Sunday.

The 72-year-old supporter was leaving the Amex Stadium to board a bus following the Premier League game when he fell ill.

2 Brighton announced the very sad news on Sunday evening after the match Credit: Getty

In a statement, Brighton wrote: "Following today’s game against Aston Villa, sadly a 72-year-old male Brighton and Hove Albion supporter passed away after the match.

"The gentleman took unwell as he was leaving the stadium to board a supporters’ club bus in the coach park.

"Despite the best efforts of emergency services and club staff, the medical team were unable to save him.

"South East Coast Ambulance Service paramedics, St John’s Ambulance, Sussex Police, MB Medical Solutions, the club’s crowd doctor and our stewards worked together to ensure the individual was given the best possible care, including prolonged CPR on the scene."

Brighton's chief executive and deputy chairman Paul Barber said: "What should have been an ordinary and happy journey home ended in heartbreaking circumstances, and we are all shocked and saddened by the loss of one of our supporters.

"We extend our sincere condolences to the gentleman’s family and friends."

Many fans sent their condolences to the supporter too, after the club announced the sad news on social media.

One supporter posted: "Horrible news. Best wishes to his family."

Another replied: "So sorry to learn this. My condolences. RIP."

"That 4-0 is for him RIP," a third Brighton fan said.

2 The Brighton fan sadly passed after the Seagulls beat Villa 4-0 Credit: Getty

Devastating news

Brighton will have been devastated to learn the news post-match after what was such an impressive win.

The Seagulls beat Aston Villa 4-0 at the Amex Stadium on Sunday afternoon in completely dominant fashion.

All four goals came in the first 31 minutes, with Jack Hinshelwood scoring two, Maxim De Cuyper netting one and Victor Lindelof deflecting home an unfortunate own goal.

Fabian Hurzeler's side are now sitting top of the Premier League table after the thrashing, sitting above Arsenal.

But the joy has turned to sadness following the match, with the terrible news of their fan's passing.

talkSPORT sends our condolences to the gentleman and his family and friends.

Sports.title: Premier League explain why Liverpool penalty decision stood as Matthias Jaissle bemoans ‘soft’ call
Sports.content:
The Premier League have explained why Liverpool were awarded their last-gasp penalty to claim a point against Newcastle.

Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the spot in the ninth minute of stoppage-time as VAR stood by the referee's on-field decision.



2 Hall brought Munoz down in the box in stoppage time to give Liverpool a penalty Credit: Getty

With the match entering the final seconds, Liverpool launched a desperate ball towards the box, looking for a chance.

It was cleared at first, but fell to new signing Victor Munoz, who drove into the box and attempted to go past Newcastle's Lewis Hall.

As he did so, Hall stepped to his left, bringing his knee and thigh across the Spanish winger and bringing him down.



Referee Stuart Atwell quickly pointed to the spot, awarding a penalty for Andoni Iraola's side in the dying moments.

VAR took a look at the incident and agreed that it was a spot-kick, much to the distaste of fans inside St. James' Park.



Szoboszlai would go on to emphatically find the top corner from the penalty, saving Liverpool as they took home a point.

Premier League explain Liverpool penalty

The awarding of the penalty was met with plenty of boos and groans from Newcastle supporters, with manager Matthias Jaissle going on to label it 'soft' when speaking post-match.



It certainly split opinion, but the Premier League have revealed their reasoning behind their decision on social media.

Posting on their Match Centre account, they explained: "The referee’s call of penalty for the challenge by Hall on Muñoz was checked and confirmed by VAR.

"REF: 'He doesn’t play the ball. He makes clear contact.' VAR: 'It’s knee into thigh contact. Confirming the on-field decision of penalty'."

2 The referee pointed to the spot after Hall made contact with Munoz Credit: Getty



Did the referee make the right decision?

Despite the explanation, former Newcastle and Crystal Palace manager Alan Pardew disagreed with the penalty decision.

He said on talkSPORT's The Final Word: "They launch it into the box, it comes to him...it's light in my opinion.

"I think the referee should have let it go and not given it."

And Newcastle boss Jaissle was of a similar mind, telling Sky Sports post-match: "It's a really soft one. If you give that, then there will be so many penalties in the future.

"I am not a fan of that, but I cannot say any more."

Meanwhile, in the Liverpool camp, Ryan Gravenberch has said that he believes it was a 'clear foul' on Munoz by Hall.



That was echoed by Micah Richards and Daniel Sturridge on Sky Sports too, with the pair believing that it was 'harsh' but that the contact was there, making it a 'thoroughly deserved penalty'.

Sports.title: ‘Come on’ – Michael Carrick fumes at reporter’s ‘ridiculous’ question after Man United defeat
Sports.content:
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick snapped back at a reporter for asking if his players lacked passion during defeat to Hull City.

Carrick was left baffled as doubts were raised over the United players' passion following their shock 2-0 defeat on Saturday.

2 Carrick's United were shocked by Hull in their opening game of the season Credit: Getty

The Red Devils were beaten comfortably by newly-promoted Hull, who have been heavily tipped to finish bottom of the Premier League this season.

But Carrick didn't believe that a lack of fight from his squad was the reason for their loss on the opening weekend.

And he made that very clear to former Premier League striker Jan Aage Fjortoft, who interviewed him for Viaplay post-match.

What question did Carrick snap back at?

"I guess in management there are so many buzzwords like passion, intensity and go for it - but would you accept that there was a lack of passion in the first half?" Norwegian Fjortoft asked.

Carrick, who looked angered by the question, quickly replied: "Oh, come on. That's ridiculous."

The United boss then stared back at Fjortoft, who went on to say: "That's not what you would assess?"

"You played football," Carrick said back. "You understand. That's a ridiculous thing to say. Just because you get beaten, it doesn't mean you don't care about it."

Fjortoft added: "Would you accept they were on the front foot?"

To which Carrick said: "No, their two goals came from set plays. Other than that, we had opportunities. That was where the game was.

"I don't think it was passion or anything to do with that. I think it was just their moments that made the difference in the game."

What else did Carrick say post-match?

Carrick backed his players when speaking to Fjortoft, and in his press conference, he called on them to 'come back stronger'.

He admitted: "It's hugely disappointing, of course it is.

"We came here to win like we do any game. So to not take anything away is hugely disappointing.

"It's not more than that. It's not less than that. It's just one game that we're disappointed we haven't won.

"So we've got to soak it up and come back stronger."

Man United will be back in action for their second Premier League game of the season next Sunday, when they take on Ipswich Town.

2 Man United got their campaign off to a concerning start on Saturday Credit: AFP

They face a second newly-promoted side in two games and will hope for a better outcome at Old Trafford.

A clash against Everton follows on September 6, before the first Manchester derby takes place on September 13.

Sports.title: Tottenham warned over transfer decision after ‘scary’ Brentford defeat
Sports.content:
Tottenham have been told to make a move for Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez before the transfer window closes.

That's the opinion of former Villan Tony Cascarino who believes Antonin Kinsky is not good enough to be the long-term replacement for Guglielmo Vicario.

3 Kinsky didn't cover himself in glory against Brentford conceding three times Credit: Getty

Kinsky has had a rollercoaster ride on the way to becoming Spurs' new No.1 under Roberto De Zerbi.

The calamitous Vicario has left the club to join Juventus on loan this season, a move that comes after the Italians failed to get a deal done for Martinez.

Vicario suffered a severe downturn in form and missed the end of last season with a hernia.

That saw Kinsky step-up in his place after signing in January 2025.

His initial foray into the first-team was fine in their Europa League winning campaign.

However, as Tottenham entered a tailspin last season Kinsky was thrown into a Champions League tie with Atletico Madrid and was substituted after just 17 minutes having conceded three goals.

The move, by then-manager Igor Tudor, drew plenty of criticism but the Czech goalkeeper bounced back impressively.

Key saves against Wolves, Leeds, and Everton were vital in saving Spurs from relegation.

Instead of a replacement being signed for Vicario, Kinsky was handed a new contract and the starting role ahead of free transfer signing Martin Dubravka.

In the 3-0 opening game defeat to Brentford, though, it wasn't a vintage performance with Cascarino believing him to be at fault for the second goal, scored by Vitaly Janelt.

3 Vicario has joined Juventus on loan with the option to make it permanent Credit: Getty

Kinsky could only parry a Mathias Jensen strike straight into the path of the German to stab home.

He wasn't the only poor performer with Lucas Bergvall, who had previously been agitating for a summer transfer, struggling before being substituted at half-time.

But Cascarino couldn't believe what he saw from both Tottenham and their goalkeeper, reckoning it's a mistake not to sign a new shot-stopper.

"Watching them yesterday was scary," he said on talkSPORT's Weekend Sports Breakfast.

"The goalkeeper, Kinsky, for the second goal. You cannot do that. And again I'm moaning all morning. I will be because I'm watching goalkeepers who can't catch the ball.

"Now, it was an effort that, okay, he could palm it round the post or whatever. But it's also to me an effort that goalkeepers used to catch."

Asked if Kinsky should remain in the No.1 role this season, he replied: "No. I thought they needed a new goalkeeper. And if they could get Emiliano Martinez out of Aston Villa, because he looks like he could go, I'd take him. An experienced goalkeeper, a lot more solid.

3 Martinez could be an option for Tottenham, reckons Cascarino Credit: Getty

"I wasn't a fan of Guglielmo Vicario and it's been a tough period for Spurs but Kinsky doesn't look like an answer to me. You know when he's doing things like that.

"We've all had bad games. I've had plenty of them in my career but when you do certain things, which is a simple catch for me, that ends up making it 2-0 for Vitaly Janelt, who's on the end of that.

"He's basically set up Janelt to just knock it in the back of the net."

Sports.title: EFL thug who has served bans for biting and headbutting set to leave for Serie A
Sports.content:
EFL thug who has served bans for biting and headbutting set to leave for Serie A

Controversial Preston North End striker Milutin Osmajic has agreed a transfer to Serie A side Genoa.

Osmajic, who has served multiple bans for biting, headbutting and alleged racism, will depart Preston after three years.



2 Osmajic leaves Preston after a controversy-filled three years at the club Credit: Getty

The 27-year-old featured in the club's pre-season and started their first two competitive games of the campaign.

He played 90 minutes in Preston's defeat to Bolton last weekend, but then played no part in their loss to Wolves on Saturday.

And after that Championship match, manager Paul Heckingbottom confirmed that he would be leaving the club imminently.



Heckingbottom revealed to the Lancashire Post: “Yes, I think that [the transfer to Genoa] has been agreed today.

"I think we’ve come off and I think that's been agreed today.”

Osmajic's constant controversy

Osmajic will leave England with a terrible reputation, having been banned on three separate occasions for Preston.



His first came in October 2024, when he was handed an eight-match suspension and a £15,000 fine for biting an opponent.

The Montenegro international admitted to biting then Blackburn defender Owen Beck and was charged by the FA.



Then, in February 2025, Osmajic was involved in another major controversy, as he was accused of racially abusing Burnley's Hannibal Mejbri during a Championship match.

Mejbri reported the incident and explained it on social media, while Osmajic strongly refuted the accusations, but he was eventually charged by the FA and a hearing took place in September.

2 Osmajic received multiple lengthy bans during his time in the Championship Credit: Getty

The FA would go on to slap the Preston forward with a nine-match ban and a £21,000 fine following the incident.



Osmajic was suspended in November, with another controversy coming just two months later in January 2026.

He headbutted Hull City midfielder John Lundstram in the final seconds of a defeat to the Tigers in the Championship.

The ever-angry frontman pushed Lundstram over in reaction to a drag back before going on to headbutt him too.

Osmajic was shown a straight red card and banned for three games, with a melee ensuing on the touchline after full time.



Now, after years of trouble, he is going to leave England for Italy to feature in Serie A for Genoa, who lost 2-0 at home to Napoli in their opening game of the new season on Saturday.

Sports.title: Journey to Wembley: After a fortnight of fretting over floodlights on the fritz, Nelson's FA Cup journey ends at Witton Albion - where home fans toasted victory with pina coladas!
Sports.content:
It’s the annual pina colada festival in the Witton area – the song about the drink, which topped the US charts in the late 1970s, was written by someone local to the place and they’ve spotted the commercial opportunity – so there are people walking around dressed as pineapples and wearing big yellow glasses on Saturday lunchtime. But life has not exactly been a cocktail party for Nelson just lately.

They breeze through one of the challenges which faces them after arriving to face eighth tier opponents one step above them in the pyramid. Their new yellow away kits for the season haven’t arrived and last season’s issue, which they’re still using, don’t have a No 18 jersey – needed today because you’re allowed seven subs in the FA Cup. Someone finds a white marker pen and inks the number on to a plain yellow away shirt. Wearing numbers on your back is mandatory in the tournament.

This is a minor obstacle compared with floodlights problem which has been testing Nelson minds since we left them celebrating extra preliminary round victory at their ‘Little Wembley’ ground two weeks ago. That was the first part of our journey to Wembley told in 13 instalments, following a club as far as they go and then picking up with the next winning team, all the way to the final.

They’d signed off on a £30,000 contract, helped by FA grants, to replace the system of lights which had started to fail during evening games, only to find that the new ones still didn’t work.

The approved contractors didn’t seem to have mentioned that the cables and wiring supplying the lights also needed ripping out, and yet were sending the club legal letters demanding payment, as Nelson’s directors sought advice from the FA about the black hole they risked disappearing into.

Inside the home dressing room at the Bedspace Trust Community Stadium

Nelson captain Bill Priestley receives some treatment ahead of kick-off

A home steward - proudly sporting Witton Albion's colours - tucks into a pie at half-time

When we caught up with Nelson at their league away game at Charnock Richard in Lancashire, last Tuesday night, the floodlights were the prime topic of conversation as the players arrived in the car park. There had even been talk of a temporary ground move, which did not exactly delight the North West Counties League. Nelson’s proactive club sponsor Monks Contractors had offered supplying temporary structures.

In the end, they just went to work again. Volunteers helped dig two 100m trenches to lay the new cabling to the new lights and on Wednesday, they flicked the switch once more. ‘Let there be light?’ The look on Witton Albion director Rob Doherty’s face as the visiting contingent are welcomed into Witton’s snug little boardroom suggests so. ‘As of three days ago, they were working,’ he relates. The FA provided emergency funding.

Both these teams badly want to win this FA Cup Preliminary Round game. In his extremely modestly proportioned office Witton manager Benny Harrison, whose day job is a teacher at a special educational school, reflects at 2pm on the profound effects Marine experienced after playing Tottenham in the Third Round in 2021. The windfall helped win them two promotions in three years.

But as the rival teams’ executives gather in that boardroom, there’s a sense of mutual empathy about the existential threats which can be just around the corner for any non-league club.

‘There’s what goes on out on the pitch, and the fans and all that the lovely stuff,’ says Witton director Paul Sanderson, when Nelson relate their floodlight troubles. ‘And then there’s survivability stuff that fans don't know about. Trying to navigate things that can threaten your existence if you’re not prepared for anything.’

Nelson were on a precipice before new co-owners Stewart Fort and Chris Price arrived three years ago, invested and built up the team of volunteers who are their lifeblood. But Witton’s excellent little club museum, charting a 139-year history and signposted ‘Probably the best non-League football museum in the world’, shows that they’ve also ridden football’s rollercoaster.

The museum chronicles the club’s journey to the 1992 FA Trophy final at Wembley, where they lost to Colchester. That period, which included a brief stay in the Vauxhall Conference, saw them splashing the surplus earned after selling their old ground to Sainsburys and building a new one, on players. The rewards were painful temporary. Witton struggled when the money ran out and the new stadium required major repair sooner than anticipated.

The sun’s out, though, and the FA Cup is blowing everyone’s troubles away. ‘Welcome to the best football competition in the world by a long chalk,’ states the stadium announcer. The appropriately named Witton groundsman James Spruce is reversing his mower out onto the excellent playing surface, his partner Katy Hulse is nursing a pina colada and her friend Barbara Bazley is watching the warm-up.

Groundsman James Spruce applies the finishing touches to the playing surface

Katy Hulse (left) enjoys a pina colada with her friend Barbara Bazley

Albion statistician Phil Chadwick has helped to curate one of the best club museum's in non-League

Nelson's 87-year-old superfan Harry Manning’s immaculate handwritten notes will be converted into a match report for the local Nelson Leader

‘When you make s*** decisions, it goes pear-shaped, so if someone makes a s*** decision, back them up and help sort it out,’ shouts assistant coach Liam Lishman, as he puts the squad through their paces. Thursday’s training session focussed on not allowing Freddie Garbutt, Witton’s towering 22-year-old striker, the chance to control and shoot.

At Charnock Richard, Nelson won 2-0, led by their own dangerous target man Sefton Gonzalez, who scored and hurled himself through his trademark somersault. Today, goalkeeper Chris Thompson is back after a bout of sciatica. There’s optimism in the air.

Against the backdrop of the chemical plants in salt-mining territory, Nelson discover what they’re up against in Garbutt and Witton’s attacking pace. Nelson wing-back Darren Holden, outstanding in the previous round and at Charnock in midweek, is operating in his own half far more, protecting Nelson territory, yet removing one of the Lancashire team's attacking dimensions.

Jamie Edwards, Nelson’s force field, draws a sharp save and Gonzales has just headed a great opportunity into the ground when Witton’s Garbutt leaps to meet a corner and send his team ahead.

He’s one of only two players Witton have signed up to a contract, protecting his match fee if he’s injured and protecting the club if someone else tries to sign him, Witton chairman Graham Wood relates, back in the boardroom at half-time.

The winners today will collect £1,444 in prize money and that would be just as precious to Witton, a fan-owned club with 400 registered shareholders, none of them hugely wealthy, who are currently trying to make a community football facility out of neighbouring land they’ve leased from the local chemical firm.

Nelson players warm up at the side of the pitch before kick-off

Witton Albion play in the Northern Premier League Division One West, one divsion higher than Nelson

Visiting goalkeeper Chris Thompson keeps a Witton Albion player at bay

Freddy Garbutt's first-half goal settled the game and sent Witton through to the next round of the FA Cup

Home boss Ben Harrison addresses his players at full-time

‘That will bring us an income to put back into the club,’ says Wood, who has helped bring a commercial sponsorship deal with a locally based homelessness charity.

Nelson dominate a second half in which Holden is pushed forward more, encouraged by his wife Abi, who is live tweeting the match for the club’s website with another volunteer, Amy Holden, and taking photographs for next week’s match programme and the website.

In the main stand, 87-year-old superfan Harry Manning’s immaculate handwritten notes, which will be converted into a match report for the local Nelson Leader, reflect the growing frustration. The ‘18’ inked onto sub James Hooper’s jersey is impressive. But it’s raining in Nelson hearts when the whistle blows and they tumble out of the competition.

Manager Arron Ripley stands in the sun-dappled centre circle ten minutes later and reflects on the way his ambitious side are evolving. ‘Last year we’d have kept launching it in a situation like that but we’re looking after the ball. We look like we’re enjoying it. We just weren’t clinical enough.’

Nelson can return fortified to their league campaign, confident, in so many ways, that the lights will stay on.

Sports.title: Alexander Isak's Newcastle return was full of vitriol and vicious noise - the £125m man looked paralysed by pressure in performance that will not have endeared him to ambivalent Liverpool fans, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
Alexander Isak's Newcastle return was full of vitriol and vicious noise - the £125m man looked paralysed by pressure in performance that will not have endeared him to ambivalent Liverpool fans, writes CRAIG HOPE

Four, four-letter words. Love. Hate. King. Isak.

Just when we thought the most emotionally-charged collective of the afternoon would be the minute's applause for Kevin Keegan, Alexander Isak stepped from the line of red jerseys to take kick-off.

How foolish of the visitors. How naive to play so willingly into the hands - and mouths - of their hosts. As if they needed any extra encouragement. They had already hissed their hatred when Isak left the team bus. This time, he could not hide behind his AirPods.

From Keegan to Isak, The Messiah to The Pariah, this was a different noise entirely. Hostile does not come close. This was vicious. This was vitriol. The Toon Army had waited a year to take aim at their former striker and, when the moment came, they did not miss. It set the tone for what followed.

The home crowd had to wait only four minutes more for Isak's first touch to go wrong. Sixty seconds later and, for Newcastle at least, everything felt so right. The breakaway goal was the sort that used to involve Isak - fast, direct and ruthless.

How fitting, then, that it was a Swede who scored. Anthony Elanga was bought last summer to play with his compatriot, before he defected to Merseyside. Unlike Keegan, Isak is not loved by both sets of supporters. In fact, you wonder if Liverpool's are even that keen. His performance here would have done nothing to endear him. It said everything that those in black and white loved it, as Keegan might say.

Alexander Isak endured a difficult afternoon on his first return to Newcastle since leaving

His long-awaited return to St James' Park saw him greeted by a vitriolic and vicious reception

Indeed, there were two moments to rival Newcastle's goals for noise, and they both, to little surprise, involved Isak. First, after a challenge by Lewis Hall to leave the Premier League's most expensive player clutching his ankle, new Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle, standing only yards away, threw his arms in the air. Not in protest at Isak staying down, but in invitation of a little more Geordie scorn for this fallen foe. They duly obliged. Isak did not like it and was quickly on his feet to let the German know. Not that he cared.

Jaissle, you suspect, will care for little beyond that which affects him and his team. For 95 minutes, he got the better of fellow managerial debutant Andoni Iraola on the pitch, and when it came to animation and aggression, the touchline too. His cajoling, his snarl and disregard for the boundaries of his technical area will quickly win him friends on Tyneside. Mocking their enemy with not hurt, either. That brings us to the second explosion of noise.

At 2-1 in the 69th minute, Isak was presented with his first big chance. It would prove to be his last. Those in the low rows of the Leazes End were ready to bury their heads in their hands - Isak had a clear sight at goal from 14 yards - only to use those same palms as a form of protection. Isak's shot flew hopelessly into the stands.

As the clock then ticked beyond the last of five added minutes, it felt like Isak's miss would be Liverpool's last inglorious act in front of goal. When they then won a penalty, you wondered whether he would take it. You wondered, too, whether his own fans would have wanted him to - the odds on redemption felt considerably longer than those on ridicule. Dominik Szoboszlai was a wiser choice and, with his blast, the points were shared.

Maybe that is what Keegan would have wanted, albeit without the reminder of a stoppage-time goal from Liverpool. The sight of him slouched behind the Anfield advertising hoarding in 1996, following Stan Collymore's 92nd-minute winner in the 4-3 classic, will forever capture the ecstasy and agony of Keegan and his great Entertainers side, who were all present here.

Newcastle fared better in terms of result this time, but the hurt was just the same. They had deserved to win. They had done what teams are told to avoid - they had played the occasion. They played it with, at times, some beauty. But more so, a brutal intensity that suggests they will not be feeling sorry for themselves on the back of a turbulent summer.

The challenge, of course, is to replicate that when the likes of Bournemouth and Hull City come to St James' Park in the coming weeks. There will be no occasion to play then, no former hero to vilify or emotional current to ride. The emphasis will be on breaking teams down as opposed to running them over.

Still, Newcastle's supporters would have left this opener more enthused than Liverpool's. The Reds were unconvincing and Isak was not alone in appearing paralysed by pressure. The man who now wears his old No 9, Yoane Wissa, was the game's best player, save for the miss that would have made it 3-1 four minutes from time.

Newcastle fans paid homage to Kevin Keegan before the match following his recent death

Before the match, Newcastle supporters unfurled a Keegan quote about dreaming big

Before the game, a Keegan quote was unfurled across the Gallowgate End. 'I want people to dream about their football club. They should. We should all be dreamers at heart. Some people are the opposite and say, "we can't do that". But when you ask them why they can't give a reason. Well, I say, "why not?".'

Until the very last kick, at least, this was the dream the Geordies had imagined - and the nightmare they had wished upon Isak. Then came the equaliser. Four, four-letter words had framed the afternoon. Four goals settled it.

And, for Newcastle, there was one more. Pain.

Sports.title: Why Andoni Iraola should be concerned after Newcastle draw: The key problem Liverpool must solve, the player they desperately need in the transfer window and a worrying lack of depth in attack
Sports.content:
Nearly a year to the day that Rio Ngumoha scored a 100th-minute winner at St James's Park, Liverpool fans were again toasting a last-second goal as they descended the many steps down from the away end up in the skies.

Last August, they were singing and dancing as they left the stadium. They were doing the same here but with a nagging worry in the backs of their minds.

When the pulses and emotions lowered as they trudged back down the A1(M), everyone connected to Liverpool would know that, despite the drama and joy that came from the last-gasp equaliser, there are a lot more issues than this time last year.

Back then, remember, the Reds were the reigning champions and had started the defence on fire. Many observers, like they do now with Arsenal, expected this team to win the league at a canter. Now, there are hints of optimism but that is overridden by uncertainty.

Twelve months on and a change of manager later, this opening performance prompted more questions than answers. The issues that ultimately led to Arne Slot losing his job were still evident and, despite the late celebrations, fans might be worried for the season ahead.

The chief problem for new boss Andoni Iraola was the midfield – or lack thereof. Both goals were accomplished counter-attacks from Newcastle but both were highly preventable as Liverpool were cut through at ease.

Dominik Szoboszlai salvaged a point for Liverpool at Newcastle with a last-gasp penalty

Ryan Gravenberch, Florian Wirtz and late hero Dominik Szoboszlai are all incredibly talented footballers. But do they work as a midfield three? They are all more naturally inclined to be attack-minded and the back door is left ajar to let teams punish them.

This summer has been all about replacing Mohamed Salah, who scored on his Trabzonspor league debut on Sunday, but why has there been no attempts to sign a midfielder?

It is not like this is a new problem. Alexis Mac Allister and Gravenberch were both poor for the entirety of last season and Liverpool have needed a deep-lying player since Fabinho left in the summer of 2023.

'The team needs a defensive midfielder, we have been talking about this at Liverpool for three years,' said Daniel Sturridge on Sky Sports. 'Gravenberch changed that philosophy but if you analyse the midfield, they are all naturally more attacking players.

'You look at Mamadou Sangare at Brentford, the stats jump off the page, he was only £39million which is not a load of money.'

Both of Newcastle's goals came from Gravenberch having possession on the edge of the home penalty area. Before they knew it, Liverpool were chasing back, there was no midfield enforcer to stop the counter-attack, the defence was stretched and they conceded.

Think of some of the great Premier League teams, they have always had someone happy to sit in and break up the play: Claude Makelele, Ngolo Kante, Rodri, Fernandinho, some of the greats at Manchester United.

Gravenberch was adept in 2024-25, when Liverpool won the title, but has not reached that same level since. Mac Allister likewise. Szoboszlai is a mercurial footballer but better further forward, as is Wirtz who was anonymous again here at the start of a defining season for him.

Ryan Gravenberch was at fault for both of Newcastle's goal and Liverpool should focus on signing a No6

Dominik Szoboszlai is far too attacking of a midfielder to fill the need deeper in the middle

Liverpool remain hopeful of signing Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola this week and are weighing up whether to make a third bid for Brighton's Yankuba Minteh. Those will be crucial additions, given the wide options are limited at present.

But signing a deep-lying midfielder is just as important. They could have the best front three in the world yet they will win no trophies if they are so vulnerable and exposed to the counter-attack like they were here.

Lionel Messi, Xavi and Andres Iniesta took the headlines in Pep Guardiola's Barcelona super-team, but No 6 Sergio Busquets was the most important cog in that machine.

Iraola thought Liverpool were the better team here but might be delighted with the point given, for most of the match, they looked likely to leave with nothing.

At Bournemouth, he played with an energetic and dynamic double-pivot of Tyler Adams and Lewis Cook. So far, the Basque boss seems unsure about the make-up of his top-heavy midfield. How to get the best of Wirtz and Szoboszlai but also keep the team solid?

It is now over to those upstairs to ensure the impressive Iraola has the tools to thrive this season, as the bench looked weak.

A winger or two would be great but a new holding midfielder should join the wide forwards at the top of that shopping list.

Isak's day to forget

We cannot repeat the words used by Newcastle fans but you can have a good guess at the sentiments expressed towards Alexander Isak, once of this parish.

Most words were four letters long and let us just say that they were not kind.

Isak, all £125m of him, saw his every touch jeered and booed by the hostile, raucous crowd at St James'.

This was a day to forget for the Swede, who has looked sharp in pre-season but failed to translate that form to when it really matters.

He had a couple of chances but fluffed his lines, much to the delight of the home fans. If Liverpool are to succeed this season, they need a lot more from Isak and Wirtz.

A returning Alexander Isak was booed with every touch and struggled against his former side

Lack of depth in attack is a real worry

Lewis Koumas has been impressive in pre-season, is a talented player who can play across the front three and the manager has taken a shine to the Welshman in training.

But the sight of him coming on as a substitute to try to salvage a point might worry some Liverpool fans.

Koumas, son of former Premier League midfielder Jason, spent the second half of last season at Hull City – and was an unused substitute in the play-off final despite scoring some important goals on the way to promotion for the Tigers.

He has deserved his top-flight debut but fans are right to ask why Iraola was left to rely on a player who has spent the last few years in the second tier, with loans also at Birmingham and Stoke.

The other wingers had mixed afternoons. Victor Munoz looked bright off the bench, asking constant questions and winning the foul that led to the decisive penalty.

Cody Gakpo took his goal incredibly well with a fine hit from distance and was Liverpool's most effective attacker – yet he has question-marks over his future given Tottenham have shown interest in signing him this summer.

Ngumoha is an exciting talent and has all the tools to be a future world-beater but failed to make a serious impression here, with just 21 touches. The 17-year-old is better on the left flank and was largely ineffective on the right flank.

All this came as, 2,000 miles south-east, Salah was scoring on his Turkish Superlig debut for Trabzonspor. With little over a week left of the window to go, the Egyptian King has still not been replaced.

Sports.title: Arsenal target Julian Alvarez BOOED by his own fans amid attempt to force move away from Atletico Madrid
Sports.content:
Julian Alvarez was given a hostile reception from his own Atletico Madrid supporters to further intensify doubt around his future at the club.

During the World Cup, the Argentine expressed his desire to leave the LaLiga outfit in order to 'fulfil my dream' - with Arsenal, Real Madrid and especially Barcelona among his suitors.

'I try to be an honest person,' he said while representing his nation at the World Cup. 'I spoke with the people at Atletico Madrid, and I think the best thing for everyone is a transfer. I want to fulfil my dream.'

His dream hasn't been fulfilled as of yet and on Sunday he saw the ramifications of his words as Atletico's fanbase voiced their anger towards him during their 2-2 LaLiga home draw with Villarreal.

The encounter was simmering with tension before Alvarez came on as a second-half substitute as he was booed while warming up, jeered again when his name was announced among the substitutes and met with louder whistles when he came on in the 66th minute.

A section of the crowd also chanted: 'Let him leave once and for all, let him leave.'

Julian Alvarez não se despede dos adeptos do Atleti 😬#DAZNLALIGA pic.twitter.com/0WSIhLeMmc — DAZN Portugal (@DAZNPortugal) August 23, 2026

Julian Alvarez trudged off the pitch to a cacophony of boos from his own Atletico Madrid fans

The 26-year-old has angered Atletico's fan base after publicly stating his desire to leave

The Arsenal, Real Madrid and Barcelona target was even booed while warming-up on Sunday

And as the full-time whistle came, the hostility grew even more as the 26-year-old headed straight to the changing room while his team-mates saluted the fans, drawing another heavy round of boos.

Discussing the situation in the post-match press conference, Atletico boss Diego Simeone revealed it was the club's decision for Alvarez to not acknowledge the fans.

'The club staff told me that the club decided Julian should not go over with his team-mates to greet the fans, and that it was not Julian's decision.

'The club made the decision to keep him away and have him head to the dressing room.

'No, I'm not in a position to give advice to the fans. I think I need to focus on my work, which is to give my best on the sporting side for the good of Atletico Madrid.

'The only thing I know is that if Atletico Madrid wants to win a title, we have to be united. We need forwards, and we need important forwards.

'For that, of course, we all have to work in that direction to give the team what it needs.'

Although reports have suggested Barcelona are Alvarez's preferred destination, Atletico have remained steadfast in their position that he is not for sale. Chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin said last month that the club would not entertain any offers for the striker, even in the region of £170million.

📺 DIRECTO @JijantesFC



💥 Este ha sido el recibimiento de la afición del Atlético cuando han dicho el nombre de Julian Álvarez por megafonía



🔗 https://t.co/OGW0AKAWMl pic.twitter.com/QIscCIc2jj — Jijantes FC (@JijantesFC) August 23, 2026

Diego Simeone (second right) said it was the club's decision for Alvarez to head straight off

Alvarez has a £428m release clause and Atletico have already rejected a £129m bid from bitter rivals Real Madrid.

Simeone has his son Giuliano to thank for rescuing them a point after with his 85th-minute equaliser in an afternoon that saw his side reduced to 10 men after Robin Le Normand was sent off on 76 minutes.

Atletico, who sit third in LaLiga with four points from their opening two matches, travel to table-toppers Sevilla next on Saturday.

Sports.title: 'I want to put a rocket up him!': Gary Neville hits out at Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak, claiming £240m Liverpool duo are 'too nice' as he warns 'enough is enough' after another poor display
Sports.content:
Gary Neville has warned Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak they need to improve and become more tenacious if they are to succeed as Liverpool players.

The pair are the most expensive signings in the club's history with Wirtz's £116million price-tag only bettered by Isak's £125m transfer as a Premier League record signing.

The pair endured underwhelming debut seasons at Liverpool last season as the club finished fifth, relinquishing their Premier League crown to Arsenal.

Both started in Sunday's 2-2 draw at Newcastle United - in what was the Reds' opening fixture of this campaign.

However, both failed to shine with Wirtz hooked after 63 minutes, while Isak failed to perform against a backdrop of vitriol in his first appearance back at St James' Park since his acrimonious exit last year.

And reflecting on their output, Neville believes the pair are 'too nice' and need a nastier side to their game.

Florian Wirtz (left) and Alexander Isak (right) have come under-fire from Gary Neville

Neville believes both are 'too nice' and has warned them they need to improve due to their fees

'The big thing for Liverpool is they've got a quarter-of-a-billion-pound front-two, Isak and Wirtz, and bloody hell we've been kind to them,' the Manchester United legend said on his Gary Neville Podcast.

'They are going to have to start playing soon or else to be fair they're going to get a lot of criticism. They're going to have to start delivering.

'For a start they're too nice and if you're going to be nice, you better be incredible at football.

'I don't see a tenacity in Wirtz in particular - Isak maybe a bit more - but in Wirtz I just see a nice player moving around the pitch, not really ever looking like he's busting a gut to do anything.'

Expanding further about Wirtz, Neville wants the playmaker to sharpen up - insisting he wants to put a 'rocket up him' at times due to his languid style on the pitch, adding that he needs to redefine his role to start producing goals and assists.

'You have players that are more graceful that just flow around the pitch - like [Mesut] Ozil and [Kai] Havertz - but I want to put a rocket up him,' he continued.

'There's ability and talent there and an understanding of his position. Sometimes I think he moves too much and isn't close enough to his striker. Sometimes I don't think he understands where the game is going to be won and lost.

'I don't see him combining with Isak. So for me, and I've said this for 12 months, he drifts too much. I just feel like Wirtz has got to think about being involved in the build-up less, he's got to think about being a second striker rather than a third midfield player, and has got to think about his output and what he needs to do, which is feed Isak with little passes and down the side of centre backs.

Speaking about Wirtz, Neville said he would like to put a 'rocket' up the £116million signing

'They've got to improve. I'm laying it on them now as I've watched them for 12 months but I have faith in them. I think Isak is an exceptional player - I never saw anyone give Gabriel and Saliba, or Van Dijk and Konate, a tougher time than he did when he was at Newcastle - so I've seen him be devastating.

'Liverpool's team-mates and coaches need to see that because it's £125m, and Wirtz needs to sort himself out. Enough is enough now. He's young and come into a different country and I can see a real player there, but we can't keep watching this stuff. He's been subbed after an hour and they need a goal. That's not right. The biggest disappointment for me is those two.'

Wirtz and Isak can let their feet do the talking on Saturday when Liverpool host Nottingham Forest in the 12.30pm kick-off.

Sports.title: Tiger Woods FINALLY set for first court appearance five months on from shock DUI arrest and rollover crash
Sports.content:
After months out of the spotlight, golf legend Tiger Woods is set to return to the public eye for his first court appearance following his shock DUI arrest and car crash.

Woods, 50, was detained on March 27 after flipping his SUV while trying to overtake a truck and trailer at high speed in the billionaire enclave of Jupiter Island.

After police found two opioid painkillers in his pocket, Woods was charged with DUI, property damage and refusal to submit to a lawful test.

Woods sought professional help in Zurich, Switzerland, afterwards, briefly returning to Florida after girlfriend Vanessa Trump revealed her breast cancer diagnosis.

Nearly five months on from the initial crash, it's been revealed that Woods will finally make his first courtroom appearance over the matter in early September.

The date had reportedly been postponed a number of times amid prosecutors continuing the investigation process in South Florida.

Tiger Woods is set to return to the public eye for his first court appearance after his DUI arrest

Woods has completed a rehab program in Switzerland after being arrested for DUI on March 27

The 15-time major winner will be represented by attorney Douglas Duncan. Woods had waived his arraignment and requested a jury trial over the matter.

His most recent hearing was held on August 4, following a July ruling that allowed prosecutors to obtain Woods' hospital records that were connected to the crash.

Martin County circuit court judge Darren Steele approved an agreement between the State Attorney's Office and Woods' legal team that allowed prosecutors to request records from the hospital that treated the PGA legend following his crash.

Back in May, Steele approved a similar agreement granting prosecutors access to Woods' prescription medication records from his Palm Beach pharmacy between January 1 and his March crash.

Prosecutors and Woods' attorney have agreed to a protective order that limits the release of any hospital or prescription records to the State Attorney's Office, law enforcement, state experts and the defense.

Woods was closing in on a return to golf and was widely expected to compete at The Masters in the days before the crash.

He hasn't competed since the 2024 Open Championship at Royal Troon in Scotland and has since undergone surgery to repair a torn Achilles as well as a seventh back procedure.

After police found two opioid painkillers in his pocket, Woods was charged with DUI, property damage and refusal to submit to a lawful test

Woods was detained on March 27 after his arrest for DUI in Martin County, Florida

Woods was in rehab in Switzerland when Vanessa Trump received her breast cancer diagnosis

The latest saga is the fourth time he has been in trouble after being behind the wheel of a car.

He was arrested for another DUI in 2017 after police found him slumped in his car in Florida with five drugs in his system, including two painkillers.

Woods was later involved in a similar crash in 2021 in California, which shattered his right leg after he was trapped under the vehicle. He needed multiple surgeries in order to recover from his injuries and has struggled with the troubling heel issue plantar fasciitis ever since.

He also crashed into a fire hydrant in November 2009 as he tried to flee his Florida home after his then-wife Elin Nordegren discovered his infidelities.

Carlos Baleba passes Man United medical ahead of £70m move as Old Trafford chiefs monitor Barcelona star Alejandro Balde

Baleba has been in Manchester over the weekend and was at the Carrington training complex on Sunday.

Carlos Baleba's move to Man United is on the verge of completion after he passed his medical

Sports.title: New season, new hairstyle for Haaland! Man City star Erling chops off iconic long hair and shows off new look ahead of Premier League campaign
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Erling Haaland has shocked fans by debuting a new hairstyle.

The Manchester City striker has abandoned his trademark Viking-style long locks and opted for a buzz cut.

He teased the new trim in a short Instagram video on Sunday morning and fans will get to see it in all its glory as City take on Bournemouth in their Premier League opener.

Haaland has varied his hairstyle down the years, sometimes adopting a ponytail and other times letting his plumage fall freely, but this is a new aesthetic for the 26-year-old.

'No way,' former City boss Pep Guardiola said in reaction to Haaland's new look on his YouTube channel. 'You are lucky you have hair!'

Former Barcelona and Inter Milan star Zlatan Ibrahimovic - who once told Haaland his power comes from his long hair - asked if he shaved it all off 'for a bet', while Jack Grealish admitted 'I can't stop looking at the top of your head.'

Erling Haaland has ditched his iconic long locks for a buzz cut, as he revealed on Instagram

Former City boss Pep Guardiola was stunned by his old striker's new look

The forward has enjoyed a free-spirited summer holiday since reaching the World Cup quarter-finals with Norway.

He spent time hanging out with Pretty Little Thing founder Umar Kamani on a yacht in the French Riviera and also went on a boat trip around Sicily.

Haaland also had the chance to meet basketball legend Michael Jordan, a link-up brokered by one of Kamani's friends, as exclusively revealed by Daily Mail Sport.

He and Kamani were merrymaking at the Hotel du Cap-Eden-Roc, a stunning coastal resort in Antibes where suites break the bank at up to £7,058 per night.

Then again, that's merely a drop in the ocean for Haaland, who nets close to £1million per week, and Kamani, whose net worth is estimated to be around $1billion (£797m).

Haaland recently claimed on Snapchat that his brain is 'fried' after playing in 67 games for club and country last season, so a break was needed.

You could say he has been letting his hair down - but that won't be possible with this new chop.

The Norwegian has garnered plenty of popularity for his hair in the past. Former Manchester City ace Kevin De Bruyne revealed that his children were inspired by his look.

‘Erling is a superstar. All three children have long hair. I see that with the kids at [my son's] school too. They all have hair like that. It's funny,' he said in 2023.

For the Community Shield last week, Haaland sported a ponytail and proved to be ineffective.

He sported a ponytail for last week's Community Shield match with Arsenal but was ineffective

Join the discussion Will Haaland's goals survive the loss of his long locks?

Manchester City lost 3-0 to Arsenal, submitting a languid and toothless performance which saw new manager Enzo Maresca come under fire.

Replacing Pep Guardiola after his trophy-laden decade was always going to be an uphill task.

Haaland was limited to 13 touches and had zero shots on target before being hooked against the champions.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Fresh Julian Alvarez meeting held as update issued on £85m target
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Fresh Julian Alvarez meeting held as update issued on £85m target

A big development has emerged in Arsenal's pursuit of Atletico Madrid superstar Julian Alvarez

View 2 Images Arsenal are still pursuing Julian Alvarez (Image: Getty )

Arsenal’s pursuit of two elite forwards made headlines this weekend. After ending their 22-year Premier League trophy drought last term, the north Londoners appear to be on course for another stellar season.

‌



They began the 2026/27 campaign by blowing away Manchester City in the Community Shield earlier this month. Mikel Arteta’s men then sent out a clear message by dismantling Coventry City in their Premier League opener last Friday, making it two 3-0 victories from their first two competitive fixtures of the campaign.

‌



Having already boasted a strong enough squad to reach the Champions League final last term while challenging for the league, Arsenal made a clear effort to strengthen this summer through the transfer market. Sporting director Andrea Berta successfully brought in five players worth a combined £200million - and the Gunners have been rewarded with stellar performances.

‌



Yet, Arteta believes the final piece of the jigsaw puzzle before the window closes on September 1 is a world-class forward, who has so far eluded him. Here, Mirror Football brings you the latest regarding the English champions’ pursuit of Julian Alvarez and Kenan Yildiz.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Granit Xhaka confirms how close he came to Chelsea transfer after Xabi Alonso talks READ MORE :

Julian Alvarez meeting held

Fabrizio Romano reports that Arsenal officials met with Atletico Madrid in London on Friday over a potential deal for Alvarez. The Argentine forward is widely reported to be Arteta’s dream signing this summer but several obstacles have prevented the Gunners from getting their man up to now.

‌



The 26-year-old is desperate to leave Atletico but has always been clear that his preference is to sign for Barcelona. Atletico, meanwhile, insist they will not sell their talisman to a La Liga rival, and would demand a substantial club record-breaking fee from Arsenal if the player even agrees to join the north Londoners.

Romano has now detailed the talks that unfolded between Atleti and Arsenal late last week, stating that Alvarez hasn’t rejected the English champions despite wanting Barcelona. Arsenal are said to be respectful of that fact and know any deal would be expensive.

The Italian journalist claims Arsenal made it clear they want to be kept updated by both the club and player on any changes in the next seven days before the window shuts, so that they can re-enter negotiations if an opportunity presents itself. Amid his stand-off with club bosses, Alvarez was included in Diego Simeone’s squad to face Villarreal on Sunday.

Sports.title: Alexander Isak's subtle action to Newcastle fans after Liverpool's late equaliser
Sports.content:
Alexander Isak's subtle action to Newcastle fans after Liverpool's late equaliser

Alexander Isak and Liverpool snatched a late point at Newcastle, where the Swedish striker faced a hostile reception on his return to St James' Park

View 2 Images Alexander Isak was public enemy No 1 on his return to Newcastle

Alexander Isak offered a little wink as he left the St James' Park pitch after Liverpool rescued a point at Newcastle.

The Swede was back at his former home for the first time since forcing his exit from the Magpies, and he was widely booed by the home crowd. They jeered his every error but the striker was able to celebrate a late equaliser with his team-mates.

Dominik Szoboszlai's penalty in the 99th minute made the game 2-2 late on, denying Newcastle the three points. Isak led the line for Liverpool but found it hard to impact the game. The forward's best chance came in the second-half when he fired in a shot from the edge of the box.

‌



It blazed over, with the Newcastle fans taking great joy in cheering his miss. Isak was able to avoid losing on his return to Newcastle and offered a wink after the final whistle, reports the Chronicle.

Given the acrimonious nature of his exit from the north east Andoni Iraola admits he knew a hostile reception was coming from those who used to cheer his name.
