Sports.title: Hamilton explains Dutch GP radio outburst over Ferrari team orders
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has urged Ferrari to be more like Mercedes with its efficiency after growing frustrated by a lack of team orders during the Formula 1 Dutch Grand Prix.

The Ferrari driver finished fourth in an action-packed contest at Zandvoort on Sunday, with his mid-race battle with stablemate Charles Leclerc arguably being Hamilton’s defining period.

Hamilton had just overtaken McLaren’s Oscar Piastri for fifth on lap 35 and was right behind a much slower Leclerc, so was therefore angling for team orders but they did not arrive.

“Great way of wasting time guys, good job,” complained a sarcastic Hamilton, who eventually took fourth when Leclerc pitted on lap 43 to end a very drawn-out process.

That is compared to Mercedes which swapped its cars with seven laps remaining, as George Russell gave second to Kimi Antonelli, who had fresher tyres so could attack Lando Norris.

Although the McLaren driver still took victory, it was a decision both Antonelli and Russell agreed with as they completed the podium ahead of Hamilton and fifth-placed Leclerc.

“I want to win,” Hamilton told F1 TV. “I want to win. I'm here to win and it is difficult when you're looking ahead and you see the two Mercedes drivers, they get the call and it's done - they execute straight away.

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images

“They let Kimi by and let him get on with the race. I was on a different strategy. It's not the same here and that's a little bit difficult, but we just have to take it.

“We'll take it offline, and when I go back now, I'll speak to them about it.”

Russell did well to take third though, as he feared that Mercedes had “lost a double podium”, because by letting Antonelli by, it put him under instant pressure from Hamilton.

The Mercedes driver held firm though, helped by the lap 70 virtual safety car for debris at Turn 5, and Hamilton reckons the earlier fiasco harmed his chances of overtaking his former team-mate.

When asked by Motorsport.com if the VSC stopped him from getting a podium, the seven-time world champion replied: “It felt like it was the closest opportunity I had.

“I think I'd come out of [Turn] 14 pretty close to him and I was just opening SM [Straight Line Mode] and just getting on the boost.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Michael Potts / LAT Images via Getty Images

“I don't know whether or not we would have got by because the Mercedes is just so quick. You saw the McLaren fly past just on power. We're losing like four tenths of a lap here just on straight lines.

“So that was a challenge, but I do think the time was lost when I was behind Charles, which ultimately meant I had a bigger distance to cover to try and catch up with George at the end.”

The result leaves Hamilton tied with Russell in second and 59 points behind Antonelli with 11 rounds remaining, a run where the Ferrari driver is hoping to add to his Barcelona victory.

But to do so Hamilton thinks the Italian marque must reduce its engine power deficit to Mercedes, despite various chassis upgrades it brought to the Netherlands.

“The one thing I'm definitely really proud of the team, they brought an upgrade here this weekend,” the 41-year-old added.

“We are getting closer to them but half the season we've been down in power. We really need to pick up the power if we're going to be anywhere near trying to fight for them and closing the gap to them.”

Sports.title: What caused Verstappen’s F1 Dutch GP crash
Sports.content:
Making mistakes may be uncharacteristic of Max Verstappen, but that’s exactly what the four-time world champion did on the first lap of his home Formula 1 race.

Starting the Dutch Grand Prix from seventh on the grid after feeling unwell all weekend, Verstappen took a decent getaway but found himself squeezed on the grass in a four-wide moment on the run to Turn 1. He was consequently challenged by Red Bull stand-in Liam Lawson in the following corners – which he didn’t mind: “We are allowed to race, so I think that's normal.”

Verstappen eventually held on to that seventh position, but a rain shower which occurred some 50 minutes before the start had dampened the track, and two drivers lost control in the banked final corner on lap one.

While Gabriel Bortoleto escaped from a 360-degree pirouette unscathed, Red Bull’s superstar couldn’t catch the RB22 and suffered a substantial crash, which caused a red flag.

“I think the start is just a consequence of what is happening on the right. It's OK, it can happen,” Verstappen commented regarding about the incident at lights out.

“Then, yeah, I got caught out. It was still quite wet in that corner, and as soon as I saw the dry patch coming, I was like, ‘Now you can accelerate’, but clearly that didn't work. So probably it was still a bit too early.”

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Photo by: Eric Le Galliot

Verstappen described the impact as “a decent hit” but clarified he’d “had worse”.

Red Bull eventually endured its worst grand prix since the April break results-wise, with Lawson its top car in seventh.

Verstappen did admit to “a disappointing weekend” in terms of pace as McLaren, Ferrari and Mercedes were out of reach, but this situation was no surprise to him.

“I wish for more, but you need to be realistic this season,” the Red Bull racer insisted. “We are the fourth-fastest team, so it's not like walking up to Zandvoort and suddenly we can do some magic things.

“It's just how it is, other teams have brought upgrades, we haven't. When you're already on the back foot, it puts you even more on the back foot. So, there's nothing surprising, it's just the reality that we live in.”

So Verstappen will now focus on resting ahead of the Italian Grand Prix, two weeks from now: “I've just not been feeling well. I'm just looking forward to a break where I can just recover also, because I really didn't feel good.”

Sports.title: F1 Dutch GP: Norris overhauls Antonelli for victory, Verstappen suffers heavy crash
Sports.content:
Formula 1 world champion Lando Norris produced a mega drive to win the Dutch Grand Prix from pole while home hero Max Verstappen caused a red flag by crashing out.

The McLaren driver crossed the line 11.5s ahead of runner-up Kimi Antonelli, with his Mercedes team-mate George Russell completing the podium at Zandvoort.

It came after Norris pipped sprint winner Russell for pole ahead of third-placed Antonelli and they all, like the rest of the grid, started on slicks despite rain an hour before lights out.

But the rain was on and off causing a wet-dry surface, the dangers of which emerged at the end of the opening lap once Norris had a perfect getaway while Antonelli overtook Russell at Turn 1.

That’s because Verstappen dipped a tyre onto the white line on the inside of the final corner, causing the Red Bull driver to spin into the barrier which spread debris on the circuit.

“Yeah that’s it - sorry!,” said the Dutchman via team radio, having brought out the red flag just as Gabriel Bortoleto also had a 360-degree spin at the banking but somehow avoided damage.

So another standing start followed - after Oliver Bearman suffered an engine failure on the formation tour - and much to Norris’ dismay this time, as Antonelli squeezed by at Turn 1 for the lead.

Start action Photo by: Clive Rose / Getty Images

That was despite softs on the McLaren compared to mediums for Antonelli, who essentially had a double delight as title rival Russell lost third to hard runner Oscar Piastri at Turn 7.

Russell just didn’t have the pace, soon being pressurised by Charles Leclerc as he reported balance problems, but the tight track allowed him to hold firm before swapping mediums for hards on lap 18.

McLaren responded the previous lap with Piastri, but this backfired as a slow 5.4s stop put him behind Russell just as Antonelli had streaked 2.2s clear of Norris out front.

That gap closed to a second once the pit window - where all the frontrunners chose hard tyres bar Leclerc on mediums - had passed, yet the reigning champion struggled to make inroads.

The wheel-to-wheel battles were more prevalent lower down: Yuki Tsunoda came out on top in a mega multi-car fight for the top 10, while Leclerc was constantly on Piastri’s tail.

That little battle finally ended on lap 34 when the Ferrari and McLaren went through the opening corners wheel-to-wheel, only for Leclerc to edge by for fourth around the outside of Turn 3.

There was yet more misery for Piastri as he was overtaken for fifth at Turn 1 on the following tour by Lewis Hamilton, who quickly closed in on team-mate Leclerc.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

The seven-time world champion was angling for team orders but they did not arrive and Hamilton sarcastically told his Ferrari squad: “Great way of wasting time guys, good job!”

Hamilton eventually moved by though once Leclerc made his second pitstop on lap 43, two tours after the Mercedes duo, and five before Norris came in for another set of hard tyres.

But Ferrari kept Hamilton out which left him with first on track, yet the battle for the net lead emerged behind as Norris rapidly closed on Antonelli, who complained about his rear Pirellis.

So come lap 54 Hamilton, Antonelli and Norris were all within a second and the reigning world champion made a sweeping move on Antonelli around the outside of Turn 1.

It was that same lap that Norris subsequently took the actual lead at Turn 11 from Hamilton, who dropped behind Antonelli at Turn 1 the following lap - just as Esteban Ocon caused a virtual safety car by stopping at Turn 4.

“Are you using me as a guinea pig,” complained Hamilton, wanting to pit, and that he finally did under the VSC by taking softs - likewise for Antonelli, while Norris and now second-placed Russell stayed out on hard rubber.

Norris admitted he was “worried” by that decision and had reasons to be so, as the advantage of the fresher tyre became evident with Antonelli quickly reducing his gap to Russell.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images

Mercedes eventually told the Briton to let his team-mate by with the swap occurring at Turn 1 on lap 65, but this left Russell vulnerable against Hamilton, claiming “we’ve lost a double podium”.

But Russell held firm, helped by a brief VSC on lap 70 for debris at Turn 5, to take the final podium spot, 4.3s behind Antonelli and 15.8s off Norris who took his second win of 2026.

Hamilton finished fourth, Leclerc took fifth and Piastri was sixth, while Red Bull stand-in Liam Lawson, Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg, Aston Martin’s Fernando Alonso and Alpine’s Pierre Gasly respectively completed the top 10.

The result has extended Antonelli’s championship advantage, as the 19-year-old leaves the Netherlands with a 59-point lead over both Russell and Hamilton in second.

Sports.title: F1 Dutch GP red-flagged after Verstappen crash
Sports.content:
Formula 1's Dutch Grand Prix has been red-flagged after one lap following an enormous accident for home hero Max Verstappen.

At the end of lap 1 on a damp circuit, Verstappen lost control of his Red Bull as he tagged the white line on the inside of Zandvoort's final turn - the banked, flat out Luyendyk corner leading onto the main straight.

Verstappen veered head on into the outside wall, before his car crossed the track and came to a standstill on the inside.

The Dutchman soon reported he was OK and apologised to his team for ending his race early.

Verstappen was fortunate not to be collected by any other cars, with Alpine's Pierre Gasly taking avoiding action, while in the background Audi's Nico Hulkenberg also narrowly avoided a huge accident as his team-mate Gabriel Bortoleto spun in front of him.

Under the red flag all drivers gathered in the pitlane awaiting the restart. They were having to navigate a field of debris before pit entry, but teams are allowed to change tyres under a red flag ahead of the restart. That restart is expected at 15:33 local time.

Max Verstappen Photo by: Anni Graf - Formula 1 via Getty Images

At the time Verstappen was running seventh after a disappointing qualifying session. Polesitter Lando Norris retained his lead during a chaotic start sequence, with championship leader Kimi Antonelli passing George Russell for second.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc gaining two positions to hold down fourth ahead of the second McLaren of Oscar Piastri and team-mate Lewis Hamilton.

For Verstappen, the accident marks an unfortunate end to a six-year spell racing on home soil, winning the first three editions of the Dutch Grand prix revival in 2021, 2022 and 2023. The race will disappear from the calendar after organisers decided not to pursue a contract renewal with F1 management.

Earlier in the week, the four-time world champion announced he had extended his Red Bull contract until the end of the 2030 season.

Sports.title: Wolff jokes that Mercedes already has Verstappen for the "real hero races"
Sports.content:
As is tradition, Mercedes organises a special media session with Wolff and representatives of the Dutch press at Zandvoort. In recent years, those roundtables have often produced some eye-catching comments, much to the amusement of Mercedes team members as well.

Two years ago at Zandvoort, for example, Wolff more or less confirmed Kimi Antonelli's F1 promotion, even though the formal announcement was not scheduled until a week later at Monza.

Last year, Wolff spoke openly about the talks with Verstappen over a potential move to Mercedes and caused some surprise when the subject turned to several AI-generated pictures of the pair. Wolff also joked about AI-generated images of himself and Verstappen, including explicit deepfakes circulating online.

At the start of this year’s conversation, Wolff clearly still remembered all those moments and laughed: “You know, let me get into the groove and then I'll give you a few punchlines!”

Dacia, Verstappen and "hero races" at the Nordschleife

#3 Mercedes-AMG Team Verstappen Racing, Mercedes AMG GT3 EVO: Max Verstappen, Daniel Juncadella, Jules Gounon, Lucas Auer Photo by: Red Bull Content Pool

Wolff then addressed Verstappen’s new Red Bull deal. According to the Mercedes team principal, the chances of a move were greater last year than they have been over the past few months, something that already became clear in the spring.

During last year’s Dutch media session, Wolff said he felt their paths would cross at some point. Asked by Autosport whether Verstappen’s new Red Bull contract has definitively changed that feeling, Wolff clarified that, in his view, their paths are already crossing – just not in F1.

“Well, the paths have crossed already with the GT racing. I think when we jointly developed that programme a year and a half ago it seemed a long shot,” Wolff said. “It seemed to be a long shot because could Red Bull ever allow Max in a Mercedes GT3?

“But they were open-minded and we are thankful for that because the project has been a success, the Red Bull Mercedes project. We have this joint cooperation between the two brands and Max, and it is nice to see that it’s successful.”

#3 Mercedes-AMG Team Verstappen Racing, Mercedes AMG GT3 EVO: Max Verstappen, Daniel Juncadella, Jules Gounon, Lucas Auer Photo by: Qian Jun / MB Media / Getty Images

Wolff then joked that Mercedes therefore gets Verstappen for what he considers the “real hero races” — the endurance events on the Nordschleife, with the Nurburgring 24 Hours as the absolute highlight.

“Exactly! You know, we have these things here in F1 with massive gravel traps and flat run-off zones. The real racing is where you go through the trees and up and downs over crests and blind corners. And against the Dacia!”

With those final words, Wolff is referring to Olli’s Garage Racing, which competes with a Dacia Logan in the iconic 24-hour race in the Green Hell.

After mentioning the Dacia, Wolff immediately turned to the press officer present, telling him that Mercedes should invite the Dacia crew to an actual F1 Grand Prix.

“No, seriously, they are heroes!” Wolff laughed. All of those things contribute to the magic of the Nordschleife, with Wolff enjoying seeing Verstappen behind the wheel of the Winward Mercedes-AMG GT3.

“You race against 150 cars on the Nordschleife in day and night, fog and rain, and ice. So obviously none of these races are 24 hours, but those are the real hero races.”

Could Verstappen ever get the same freedom at Mercedes?

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Mark Thompson / Getty Images

Whether Verstappen and Wolff’s paths will ever cross in F1 is something the latter does not dare to predict, if only because nobody knows what the driver market will look like in two or three years’ time.

“And what the future holds, I don't know, but the mindset is what I have just said. I don't know where the paths are going to cross. Will it be in karting, will it be in GTs, or will it be in F1 or some other joint projects in the future?

“I think that may happen one day, but maybe not necessarily with Max in a Mercedes Formula 1 car.”

The latter may not be necessary either, now that Mercedes already has its star of the future in Kimi Antonelli.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

Another question is whether Verstappen would receive the same freedom to pursue outside racing projects at another F1 team.

“I think every team is different, but I think what I am trying to do is to identify what it is that makes the driver fast within our structure.

“What kind of framework do we need to provide to extract the best performance of the driver, and part of that is obviously the well-being. And that is something that I am very keen on as well.”

Sports.title: Verstappen suffering from "flu-like" illness as Zandvoort exposes Red Bull's fundamental problems
Sports.content:
With three victories since the Dutch Grand Prix returned to the calendar in 2021, Max Verstappen can already look back on a very successful period. The final edition in 2026 has proven an ordeal so far, both in terms of Red Bull’s pace and Verstappen’s physical condition.

"I've felt better before, yes," Verstappen admitted during the Dutch media session in the paddock after qualifying. "I feel a bit flu-like and I’m just not feeling as much energy as normal."

Asked whether that also affects his performance behind the wheel, he continued: "No, I don’t think so. I think once you’re in the car, it’s actually fine."

It does mean Verstappen is experiencing his final home race somewhat differently and is mainly looking forward to the moment he can get some rest: "Of course I still enjoy all the fans in the grandstands, but apart from that, I’m mostly looking forward to getting some sleep."

Why Zandvoort exposes some fundamental Red Bull problems

Aside from Verstappen’s physical condition, Red Bull is also struggling for performance at the circuit in the dunes. The home hero had to settle for seventh on the grid and was more than four tenths behind polesitter Lando Norris in qualifying.

"We changed quite a lot on the car after the sprint, but none of it made any difference," Verstappen said when asked by Autosport.

According to Verstappen, the Zandvoort circuit exposes some of Red Bull’s weaknesses to an exaggerated degree Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

"The balance of the car is the biggest problem. It’s just not consistent throughout the entire corner, but it has been like that all season. It’s just a little worse at some circuits than at others."

In that respect, Zandvoort is a track that exposes the RB22’s weaknesses more than most.

"It depends on the tarmac sometimes, but also on the layout of the track. This one is for sure not our best layout, but we just need to work on it. We can guess on what track it might be a little bit better, but we need to try and just dial it out."

Verstappen added that, in his view, it is not so much related to set-up, as Red Bull has tried everything in that respect: "I think we’re now simply more limited by some fundamental problems with the car that we need to solve.

"At this circuit you also have some fast corners and we’re lacking there as well. In general, if you don’t have a good balance, you can’t really attack the corners. And if you don’t have traction either, you can’t get out of the corners properly, so all of that costs time."

It means Verstappen considers seventh place the maximum achievable result on Sunday under normal circumstances, particularly if there is no chaos caused by rain.

Without rain, Verstappen reckons that P7 will be the best he can hope for in his final home race Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

It may not be the Zandvoort farewell he had hoped for, although the four-time world champion stresses that the Dutch GP era as a whole has already been a great success.

"It’s absolutely the end of an era," he said. "To have had your own home race and to have been able to win it a few times is very special. Of course, it’s a shame that it’s going away, but on the other hand, it has also given me a lot of great moments and memories."

Whether another memorable moment will be added remains to be seen, but Verstappen took a pragmatic view in conclusion.

"I’m really only satisfied when we win, but that’s going to be very difficult tomorrow," he said. "We’ve been a little too slow throughout this season and that’s not suddenly going to change in Zandvoort, but we’re just going to try to enjoy it one last time."

Sports.title: Russell defends “fair” decision to let Antonelli into second place | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell said letting his team mate and championship rival overtake him was the correct decision which minimised the risk to their races.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli ran ahead of Russell until he made an extra pit stop during a late Virtual Safety Car period. When Antonelli closed on Russell afterwards, Mercedes ordered the pair to swap positions.

Russell complied, though it handed Antonelli a six-point swing in the championship fight between the pair of them. That erased the gain Russell made in the previous day’s sprint race.

However Russell said letting his team mate by was the correct thing to do for Mercedes.

“We’ve always said as a team, when we’re on different strategies, we’re never going to fight and we’re always going to invert, and that’s always just been our rules,” he explained.

“The fact is Kimi was ahead of me before the VSC and he tried something different to protect us as a team. He kind of copy-pasted what the Ferraris did.”

Although Russell believes there was a chance he could have successfully defended his position from Antonelli – as he later did with Lewis Hamilton, thanks partly to the timing of another VSC period – he also said trying to defend could have compromised his race.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Could I have kept him behind? Maybe. But equally it could have been a P5 as well. So, in the end, you know, he deserved to be P2. I think P3 was a fair result for me.”

Russell fell behind Antonelli at the start of the race, then got stuck behind Oscar Piastri and never managed to get back on terms with his team mate. “It was tough,” he said.

“The first VSC came at a pretty awkward timing for me because I felt really strong on the hard [tyre]. I think Kimi’s and my race was kind of the opposite. I had a tough medium stint, he had a very strong medium stint, then I had a strong hard stint, he was struggling.

“But that VSC gave Lewis a free pit stop and obviously Kimi pitted as well. And from there on in, I knew I was going to be under threat.

“I was managing enough in the high-speed corners to allow me to be fast in sector three and defending into turn one [Tarzan]. So I was pleased with that performance.”

Sports.title: Antonelli says extra pit stop “put George at risk” too | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli was not convinced his extra pit stop in the Dutch Grand Prix was the right decision as it risked compromising his race.

The Mercedes driver made an extra pit stop 16 laps from the end of the race, taking advantage of a late Virtual Safety Car period. It dropped him from second place to third behind his team mate George Russell

Antonelli was able to repass his team mate for second place after Mercedes ordered Russell to let him through. However Antonelli was unable to gain on race leader Lando Norris.

Afterwards Antonelli said the strategy call had unnecessarily risked both their races, even though he had been struggling on his previous set of tyres.

“It was a difficult second half for me, especially in the last stint on the hards,” he said. “I was just really struggling. I had little confidence in the car and it was not easy.

“Then obviously we pitted [under the VSC] and also that was a bit tricky. But then also George, I have to thank him because he made my life a lot easier.

“But I still think probably we could have stayed out and gone until the end with the same set [of tyres] because it put us a little bit at risk. Also, I feel we put George at risk with having to let me by and everything.”

Although he led most of the race, Antonelli said he was unlikely to win it. “I still think, at the end of the day, it was a great team execution with how things were,” he said. “”I think today [second place] was the maximum we could have done because the pace of the McLarens, especially in the second half, was just too strong.”

“It was a good ending of a difficult weekend for me where I struggled with the feeling of the car, did a lot of mistakes on my side – sprint quali, quali, also in today’s race with Lando I could have defended a bit better,” he added. “So for sure there were things that I didn’t do well this weekend, and for sure the feeling wasn’t as good.”

Sports.title: “We weren’t unlucky”: Hamilton tells Ferrari their tactics cost him third place | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton told Ferrari they cost him a chance to finish third by failing to use team orders during the Dutch Grand Prix.

He finished fourth behind George Russell after losing time earlier in the race when he caught team mate Charles Leclerc. Hamilton repeatedly urged Ferrari to tell Leclerc to let him through, but the team instead to chose wait a lap and then bring the leading Ferrari into the pits.

“Let’s not hold ourselves up from an potentially better result,” Hamilton told the team when he caught Leclerc.

After spending a lap behind Leclerc, Hamilton warned Ferrari “we’re just losing time.” Once Leclerc came in, Hamilton sarcastically remarked: “Big waste of time guys, good job.”

Hamilton’s attempt to pass Russell at the end of the race was thwarted when the Virtual Safety Car was deployed. After he finished fourth race engineer Carlos Santi told Hamilton: “Thank you Lewis, was a bit unlucky with Russell.”

“We weren’t unlucky,” Hamilton replied, “we lost time earlier on and that cost us P3.”

“We can discuss it offline,” he added.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Hamilton explained his frustration after the race, pointing out Mercedes did not hesitate to swap the order of their two drivers when it benefitted them overall.

“I want to win,” said Hamilton. “I’m here to win and it is difficult when you’re looking ahead and you see the two Mercedes drivers, they get the call and it’s done and they execute straight away.

“They let Kimi by and let him get on with the race. I was on a different strategy and it was not the same here.

“That’s a little bit difficult but we just have to take it, we’ll take it off line. When I go back now, I’ll speak to them about it.”

Sports.title: Williams pair apologise for crash: ‘It’s not a Verstappen-Ricciardo Baku situation’ | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Both Williams drivers apologised for their roles in the collision between the pair during the Dutch Grand Prix.

However the stewards ruled Carlos Sainz Jnr was responsible for the collision which ended his team mate Alexander Albon’s race.

The collision occured as Albon tried to overtake Sainz on the outside entering Tarzan corner. Sainz locked up and made contact with the other Williams.

“It was a situation of the race put us with Alex on a fresher medium [tyre] behind,” Sainz explained. “I was struggling already a lot with my hard tyres there towards the end of the race and all of a sudden when I went to defend, a big bump in the braking area into turn one surprised me.

“I triggered a massive front lock and without wanting, obviously, I took Alex with me, which is the last thing you want to do with a team mate. But honestly I was caught off guard with that big bump there in the braking and triggered a massive front lock that I couldn’t recover later.

“So apologies for that and we will move on as a team. I think it’s just not the position we want to be in.”

The stewards handed Sainz a 10-second time penalty, ruling he “locked up and caused a collision between both cars” and was “wholly at fault”.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

However Albon also apologised for his role in the collision. He said it was not as serious as other clashes between team mates, notably the 2018 collision between Red Bull duo Max Verstappen and Daniel Ricciardo at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix which took both drivers out.

“It’s not good for the team,” said Albon. “Obviously we apologise to the team, but it’s not a Verstappen-Ricciardo Baku situation.

“We’ll review it for sure but I think he maybe just locked up and I tried to avoid it as well but we had damage so we had to retire.”

Sports.title: Hulkenberg explains how he avoided team mate Bortoleto in “scary” near-miss | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Nico Hulkenberg described how he made an “instinctive” last-second swerve to avoid T-boning his team mate in the Dutch Grand Prix.

Gabriel Bortoleto overtook Hulkenberg moments before spinning in front of him on the first lap of the Dutch Grand Prix.

“It was scary, sketchy,” said Hulkenberg. “You’re a passenger to some [extent].”

Bortoleto lost control of his car in the final corner, moments after Max Verstappen did the same and hit the barrier on the outside. Bortoleto kept his car on track but Hulkenberg had to make an immediate call whether to swerve to the left or right of the other Audi.

“I tried to react as late as possible and then just instinctively chose the side,” Hulkenberg explained. “Obviously I was waiting to see if he’s going to slide up or down. On a wet track it’s sketchy and difficult, but luckily we managed to avoid that.”

Bortoleto suspected he lost control of his car partly because he saw Verstappen going off ahead of him.

“I just saw big smoke coming out,” he said. “I think it was Max that crashed and then I maybe made a small reaction on the steering.

Both Audi drivers finished the race, Hulkenberg claiming points for eighth while Bortoleto’s poor start and spin left him 13th. Bortoleto said he had other “issues” in his race but was unwilling to elaborate on them.

“I don’t want to go too much into details, because I don’t know if I can say, or whatever. But we just need to understand some stuff that happened today, and we’ll move on.

“I had a few start problems today that almost made me not probably manage to run out of the grid box, but I appreciate the work of the team. They were really on it to make it happen and to fix everything.

Sports.title: Colapinto claims penalty for overtaking under yellow flags was “very harsh” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Franco Colapinto committed two yellow flag infringements during the Dutch Grand Prix and was given penalty points on his licence for each.

Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad were also penalised for failing to obey F1’s yellow flag rules.

Colapinto’s first penalty was for overtaking Yuki Tsunoda as they passed double waved yellow flags on the first lap of the race. The flags were shown in response to Max Verstappen’s crash at the final corner, which littered the track with debris, as well as Gabriel Bortoleto’s 360-degree spin at the same corner.

“Car 43 [Colapinto] was behind car 22 [Tsunoda] entering turn 14 and overtook car 22 in the double yellow flag sector before the [finishing] line at the end of lap one,” the stewards noted.

“Normally such infringement requires a 10 second stop[-and-]go penalty, but the stewards acknowledge the complications caused by the significant amount of debris on track at this point and take this into account as mitigating circumstances.”

The stewards issued the same decision regarding Arvid Lindblad who overtook Pierre Gasly at the same time. Both Colapinto and Lindblad received drive-through penalties and two penalty points on their licences.

Colapinto was already gaining on Tsunoda as they rounded the final corner when Verstappen crashed ahead of them. He continued to pass the Racing Bulls as the crash unfolded ahead of them.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The Alpine driver criticised the stewards’ decision, calling it a “very harsh penalty” which “Colapinto: compromised the whole of our race”.

“It’s quite tricky, I think, to manage those situations when there is a car and pieces of car everywhere flying around and you have to make a decision,” he explained. “It was clearly much more dangerous to slam on the brakes in the middle of the straight and on the water and on the banking and not doing what I’ve done.

“I guess the rules are written [this way] but it should be much more flexible and give a little bit more, not just consistency, but a bit of flexibility in different situations that you can clearly see that this shouldn’t be penalised exactly what the rules say. But in the end of the day we still lead an infringement.”

Colapinto received another penalty point, and a 10-second time penalty, for failing to slow sufficiently for yellow flags later in the race when Esteban Ocon retired. The stewards noted he “passed a single yellow flag without discernibly reducing speed although also

receiving a visible warning on the dash.”

“As the infringement was not considered dangerous or egregious, a penalty on the lower end of the available scale is imposed,” they added. They also found Liam Lawson guilty of the same infraction and issued the same penalty.

The decisions leave Colapinto on a total of four penalty points, Lawson on three and Lindblad on two.

Sports.title: Regis Prograis Calls Rocky Marciano Overrated
Sports.content:
“For me, I think Rocky Marciano was overrated,” Prograis said on social media. “He retired undefeated, right? But in this book, I bought this book about Sonny Liston. It said right here about Rocky Marciano that ‘his good fortune was to rise to prominence at a time when his major competitors were either old, like 37-year-old Joe Louis.’ He was 37 when he fought him. Joe Walcott was 37 years old. A natural light heavyweight like Ezzard Charles was 34 years old, and then Archie Moore was 41 at the time.”

The overall point has some merit, but several ages quoted by Prograis are inaccurate. Louis was 37, but Walcott was 38 when Marciano took his heavyweight title in September 1952. Charles was 32 in their first fight and turned 33 before the rematch, not 34. Moore’s birth year remains disputed, leaving him either 38 or 41 when he challenged Marciano in 1955.

Prograis also accused Marciano of avoiding 6-foot-3 Cuban contender Nino Valdes because of his size.

“They had a Cuban fighter called Nino Valdes, and he didn’t want to fight him,” Prograis said. “He said he was too big. So I know a lot of older guys say that Rocky Marciano was this and undefeated this. But I feel Rocky Marciano was overrated at the time.”

Valdes had a legitimate case after rising to the top of the heavyweight rankings, but saying Marciano simply refused to face him leaves out part of the story.

The Cuban lost a 15-round title eliminator to Moore in May 1955. Marciano then met Moore four months later and stopped him in the ninth round. Valdes also suffered numerous defeats during Marciano’s championship reign, making the claim that he was deliberately avoided difficult to prove.

Marciano’s leading opponents were older, and his era lacked the talent found in later generations. Still, Walcott, Charles, and Moore remained dangerous elite fighters. Those victories do not settle every historical argument, but dismissing his entire career as fortunate goes too far.

Sports.title: Rick Glaser Tattles on Eddie Hearn to Turki
Sports.content:
“Turki Alalshikh, you have a great event in the deep planning stage for November 20 on Netflix at the Mecca of Boxing Madison Square Garden in New York And as you know, Eddie Hearn is attempting to undermine your great event,” said Glaser on X. “Whatever Hearn’s reasons may be, personal gain, or other motives, it’s causing havoc in Boxing circles, & the sporting public, especially with Hearn saying on video’s “I don’t care who this upsets” as he mouths off. “Turki Alalshikh, you deserve much better than you are receiving from Hearn in his lack of respect. Best regards from Sonya & I.”

The sign-off completes the effect. Having reported Hearn’s alleged misconduct and lavished Turki with praise, Glaser closes the message as though he were sending a polite letter to a school principal.

Nothing in the post proves that Hearn is trying to damage the event for “personal gain” or any other hidden motive. He represents Anthony Joshua, who signed for the fight to take place at a UK stadium. Joshua prefers Wembley, while Turki and Tyson Fury favor New York.

As Joshua’s promoter, Hearn is supposed to argue his position, even when it clashes with Turki’s plans. That does not automatically make him disloyal or disrespectful.

The message presents the dispute as something more serious. In Glaser’s version, Hearn is creating chaos, sabotaging Turki’s work, and failing to show proper gratitude toward the man financing the event. It is an extraordinary display of public loyalty. Glaser did everything except ask Turki to send Hearn to the headmaster’s office.

Sports.title: Julio Cesar Chavez Broke Edwin Rosario Piece By Piece
Sports.content:
Rosario presented the kind of danger Chavez had not encountered. The WBA champion had knocked out Livingstone Bramble in two rounds the previous year and possessed genuine power in both hands. He also attacked Chavez’s opposition before the bout, dismissing many of his previous opponents as “guys right out of the bar.”

Rosario Could Not Keep Chavez Away

Any doubts about Chavez at lightweight disappeared quickly. Rather than feeling his way into the contest, the 25-year-old Mexican closed the distance and began digging hooks into Rosario’s body.

Rosario had success during the third and fourth rounds. He landed several hard punches and briefly forced Chavez onto the ropes, but nothing discouraged the advancing challenger. Chavez absorbed Rosario’s best shots, turned him, and reclaimed control with short combinations. Once the bout moved into close range, the difference became brutal. Chavez did not simply walk forward and throw punches. He slipped Rosario’s right hand, blocked shots with his elbows and gloves, then answered before the Puerto Rican champion could reset.

The body attack gradually robbed Rosario of his movement and power. Chavez mixed hooks downstairs with uppercuts and straight rights to the head, rarely wasting a punch. HBO’s PunchStat count credited him with landing 450 of 743 punches, an extraordinary 61 percent. Rosario connected with 263 of 731.

A Beating That Lasted Too Long

By the later rounds, Rosario’s left eye was swollen shut, his face was cut, and blood covered his nose and mouth. Still, he refused to go down. His courage allowed the punishment to continue far longer than it should have.

Chavez looked almost untouched as he drove Rosario into a corner during the 11th. With the champion taking another sustained attack, his corner threw in the towel. Referee Richard Steele stopped it at 2:38. All three judges had Chavez far in front: 98-92, 99-91, and 100-92.

The performance made Chavez a two-division champion and erased every question surrounding his move to lightweight. He had taken one of boxing’s most feared punchers, neutralized his power, and broken him down without ever needing a knockdown. Rosario brought danger into the ring that night, but Chavez made it disappear.

Sports.title: Teofimo Defeats Rolly, Now He Has His Eyes Set On Undisputed
Sports.content:
During the first three rounds of the world title bout, Lopez was in control as he used his jab and touched the body of Romero. Late in the fourth round, Romero landed a check left hook that knocked Lopez off balance.

In the fifth round, Rolly got more aggressive, and as a result, he landed a big left hook that produced a cut over Teofimo’s right eye.

Seconds later, Romero connected with a vicious overhand right that buckled Lopez’s knees.

Romero followed the big right hand with a flurry of shots, but Lopez was able to survive the round. Lopez bounced back in the sixth as he returned to his game plan of working off the jab and attacking the body.

Lopez continued to apply intelligent pressure in the seventh as he landed a solid right hand. As round seven was coming to a close, Romero caught Lopez with a powerful check left hook.

For the remainder of the WBA welterweight title bout, Teofimo Lopez fought a smart and very disciplined fight. Despite the low punch output, Rolly had the more eye-catching shots, but Teofimo outworked him and won by majority decision.

With the victory, Teofimo “The Takeover” Lopez (23-2, 13 KOs) became a three-division world champion. As soon as Lopez was announced as the winner, the boxing community was seeking the answer to the proverbial question: What’s next?

During the post-fight press conference, Teofimo Lopez spoke about his future and the path he plans to travel in his boxing journey.

“I think I’m here, this is the road to undisputed, you know what I’m saying? I’m here to reclaim and collect all of the next world titles, and whoever the next champion is, that’s what it’s all about.”

Teofimo Lopez went on to say, “Honestly, I got four fights with, well now three fights with DAZN, and all of them are the road to undisputed. We’re going right to every world title.”

Currently, the world champions in the welterweight division are Teofimo Lopez (WBA), Devin Haney (WBO), Ryan Garcia (WBC), and Liam Paro (IBF). In his quest to become undisputed, the first step for Lopez is to become a unified world champion.

If Lopez wants what looks like the softer touch, a unification bout with IBF champion Liam Paro may be next. If Lopez wants a fight that is going to be a big event, then he may want to pursue a bout with the Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn winner.

Sports.title: Moises Garcia Derails Mike Tyson Look-Alike’s Hype Train
Sports.content:
Coming into the bout, D’Angelo Evans was the featured attraction due to his look, his KO percentage, and his most recent knockout that went viral. Most fight fans didn’t know D’Angelo Evans existed until his viral moment.

Back in May 2026, with 2:05 remaining in the second round, D’Angelo “Muscle” Evans landed a vicious left hook that knocked Cesar Villarraga out cold. The match came to an abrupt end as Villarraga was immediately attended to.

Once the knockout video hit the internet, casual fans started comparing Evans to a young Mike Tyson because of his facial features and his KO power. Some casuals went as far as making fake videos claiming Evans is Mike Tyson’s son.

Going into his August 22nd bout, the people who jumped on the D’Angelo Evans hype train were expecting another viral moment. Unfortunately, they witnessed a moment that no one predicted.

Prior to the August 22nd bout, Moises Garcia lost two fights in a row. Garcia went back to the drawing board, and he bounced back by putting together a two-fight win streak.

In his April 2026 fight, Garcia lost by way of unanimous decision to Top Rank’s rising undefeated prospect Deric “Scooter” Davis. Four months later, Garcia was scheduled to fight another prospect who was rapidly gaining momentum.

On the night of August 22nd, with 1:47 remaining in the 5th round, Garcia landed a hard left hook that staggered Evans. D’Angelo Evans showed his inexperience by retreating straight backward rather than clinching or angling out.

Garcia pressed forward and landed a flurry of shots that produced a knockdown. D’Angelo Evans was unable to get up, and just like that, the hype train got derailed.

With the victory, the Puebla, Puebla, Mexico native Moises “Bam-Bam” Garcia improved to a record of (8-6-3, 4 KOs). Now the question is, will the big promotional companies take a chance on matching their rising prospects against the upset-minded Garcia?

For D’Angelo Evans, it’s time to regroup. From an offensive standpoint, Evans has some tools, but to bounce back effectively, he must work on his defense and learn to fight off the back foot.

Sports.title: Joe Joyce Wants Return Despite Suslenkov Memory Blank
Sports.content:
“I went back to the hotel room, and I was like, ‘What really happened?’ I felt like I was winning the fight, and then I watched it back, and I was like, ‘Whoa.’ I think what might have happened, I might have taken a big shot. I couldn’t really see,” said Joyce to talkSPORT Boxing.

Joyce is currently without a promoter and floated Dana White’s Zuffa Boxing as one possible destination. He did not claim that White had contacted him or made an offer.

“Zuffa would be—I’d be open to having a conversation with Dana White. Have a conversation with everyone, see what’s out there.”

Five of Joyce’s last six contests have ended in defeat. The decline began against Zhilei Zhang in April 2023, when repeated left hands damaged his right eye and forced a sixth-round stoppage. Zhang then knocked him out in three rounds in their rematch five months later.

Losses to Filip Hrgovic, Derek Chisora, and Suslenkov followed. The Chisora and Suslenkov defeats were especially revealing. Neither man performed like a top heavyweight. They were simply able to outwork and punish a version of Joyce who no longer resembled the fighter who stopped Joseph Parker in 2022.

His weight has not helped. Joyce was 256 pounds for the first Zhang fight after spending much of his earlier career in the 250s and low 260s. He rose to 281¼ for the rematch, 286½ against Kash Ali, 281¼ for Chisora, and a career-high 289 against Suslenkov.

Joyce was never quick, but carrying nearly 290 pounds has made him look even slower. His punches are painfully slow, his feet are heavier, and opponents have more time to land shots. Only Joyce knows why he has not returned to a lower weight. The way he looks now, he’s puffy and looks nothing like he did when he turned pro in 2017.

Trainer SugarHill Steward supported his decision to stop against Suslenkov after noticing signs of fatigue. Steward believes regular gym work can bring back some of the athletic ability missing from Joyce’s recent performances.

That is difficult to accept after watching his decline over the last three years. Joyce built his career around absorbing punishment and wearing opponents down, but his resistance is no longer reliable. Forgetting how the Suslenkov fight finished makes another return even more concerning.

Joyce named Daniel Dubois, Joseph Parker, Hrgovic, and Chisora as possible rematch opponents. That is a tough list for someone with one win since September 2022. At 40, with his durability fading and weight continuing to rise, there is little reason to believe he will become the fighter he was before Zhang. If Joyce remains in the 280s, more defeats are likely.

Sports.title: Putting Moses Itauma Behind A Paywall Hurts His Future
Sports.content:
Fans are being asked to pay to watch an unproven 21-year-old headline against an opponent who is respected within boxing but has little drawing power. A bare-bones undercard filled with domestic-level scrubs going nowhere gives undecided buyers zero reason to order the event.

Thin Card Leaves Itauma Carrying The Show

Sam Noakes against former WBO lightweight champion Denys Berinchyk is the strongest supporting fight. Constantin Ursu meets Ben Vaughan, Aloys Junior takes on 40-year-old Mike Perez, and Guido Vianello faces Moses Jolly.

Those fights may serve their purpose on a regular DAZN card, but this is a premium broadcast. None carries enough public interest to take pressure off Itauma and Hrgovic.

The promoters are trying to collect star-level money before Itauma has become a star. That strategy reduces the number of people who will see him and makes it harder for him to develop the support required to sell future events.

Exposure Should Come Before PPV

Regular cards should remain Itauma’s home until he is at least 26 and has been shown repeatedly to boxing fans. Five more years of accessible fights would let viewers follow his development, learn his personality, and become invested in his career.

Anthony Joshua became a major attraction because millions of British viewers watched his early fights. Itauma is being denied that broad introduction by a business model that demands payment without first establishing a connection with the public.

An IBF title would give Itauma a belt, but it would not automatically make him an attraction. Hiding him behind a paywall may bring in money on August 29. It also means fewer people will be watching when he takes the most important step of his career.

Sports.title: Hearn Claims TKO Paid For Tyson Fury Story Reposts
Sports.content:
“Firstly, that’s a plant,” Hearn said after revealing that BoxingScene reporter Lance Pugmire had contacted him about an email he received. “It was sent by TKO to journalists. I actually was told by a number of people that they’re financially incentivizing people to repost Tyson Fury’s story of him trying to spin the narrative. It’s absolutely wild what’s going on.”

Hearn then disputed how the circulated document had been presented.

“The email that was sent was an email between Matchroom and Sela detailing outstanding points that we want resolved. The addendum that was sent to Sela regarding the changes that we want to the contract if you want to do the fight in the US did not have one of those things from that leaked email in.”

Selective Leak or Paid Campaign?

At least two media outlets obtained the disputed information. Hearn named Pugmire, while The Sun stated that it was among several media organizations given the material. No complete list of recipients has been made public.

That reinforces Hearn’s contention that the email was circulated selectively, though it falls well short of proving that reporters received financial incentives. Providing favorable information to selected reporters is a familiar tactic during a contentious negotiation. Pugmire’s possession of the material only shows that someone wanted its contents made public. It does not reveal who sent it directly or establish that money changed hands.

The distinction between the email and the addendum is also central to Hearn’s defense. He maintains that the leaked correspondence covered unresolved business between Matchroom and Sela, while the addendum contained separate terms required for moving Joshua vs Fury from Britain to the United States.

Until Hearn produces evidence, the alleged paid media campaign remains hearsay. Obtaining a leaked document is not proof that a reporter was rewarded for publicizing it.

Ghana News.title: Accountability forum will continue to drive development – Central Regional Minister
Ghana News.content:
Ekow Panyin Okyere Eduamoah, the Central Regional Minister, has pledged to work closely with Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs) to accelerate development across the Region.

He made the pledge during a public accountability forum held at Twifo Hemang in the Twifo Hemang-Lower Denkyira District of the Central Region.

Mr Eduamoah said the accountability forum formed part of government efforts to engage residents and provide updates on development projects and programmes being implemented in their respective districts.

He said the forum would not be a one-off event, adding that the engagements would continue to enable residents to assess the performance of their local authorities and ensure the effective implementation of development projects.

Mr Patrick Fiable, District Chief Executive for Twifo Hemang-Lower Denkyira, said the district was beginning to witness significant development under the current administration.

He said the projects were evidence of the Government’s commitment to improving infrastructure and the living conditions of residents in the district.

Mr Lawrence Kwabena Agyensaim, Member of Parliament for the Twifo Hemang-Lower Denkyira Constituency, urged residents to refrain from activities that could encourage hooliganism and disrupt the peace of the area.

He noted that the district continued to face a number of developmental challenges and called on residents to support initiatives such as the public accountability forum to help address them.

Mr Agyensaim stressed the need for unity and cooperation among residents, traditional authorities and government officials to promote sustainable development in the constituency.

Ghana News.title: Parliament resumes today for five-day sitting amid pending ministerial nominations
Ghana News.content:
Parliament is set to resume sitting today, Monday, August 24, following a recall by Speaker Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin to enable the House to consider urgent parliamentary business.

The five-day sitting will run until Friday, August 28, at Parliament House in Accra, with proceedings scheduled to begin at noon today. The recall was issued by the Speaker on Wednesday, August 12, under Order 58(4) of the Standing Orders of Parliament.

Although the Speaker did not specify the matters to be considered during the special sitting, the recall comes at a time when several ministerial nominations from President John Dramani Mahama are awaiting parliamentary consideration.

President Mahama has nominated Klottey Korle MP Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings as Minister for Environment, Science and Technology, following the death of the substantive minister, Murtala Mohammed.

The President has also nominated Bawku Central MP Mahama Ayariga as Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, alongside the reassignment of two other ministers to new portfolios.

The nominations were submitted to Parliament on Friday, August 7, in accordance with Article 78(1) of the 1992 Constitution, which requires parliamentary approval before ministerial nominees can assume office.

Parliament is therefore expected to consider the nominations as part of its business during the five-day recall, including the vetting and approval or rejection of the nominees.

Ghana News.title: 50 pick forms to contest 11 NPP executive positions; five eye chairmanship
Ghana News.content:
Fifty aspirants have picked nomination forms to contest 11 national executive positions in the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) upcoming national executive elections, with five of them seeking the National Chairperson position.

The five are Paul Afoko, John Boadu, Boakye Agyarko, Sammy Crabbe, and Bernard Antwi Boasiako.

The incumbent National Chairman, Mr Stephen Ayesu Ntim, is not seeking re-election.

For the General Secretary position, incumbent Justin Kodua Frimpong is seeking a second term and faces competition from Eugene Boakye Antwi, Sylvester Tetteh and Charles Dwamena.

Eight aspirants picked forms for the National Organiser position.

They are Glover Daniel Nii Kwartei, Salam Mustapha, Kwame Prempeh, Archibald Korletey Gamor, Emmanuel Korsi Bodja, Nana Kwadjo Agyei Yeboah, Daniel Agyenim Boateng and Ali Maiga Halidu.

The National Youth Organiser position has attracted six aspirants: Clement Opoku Gyamfi, Chris Lloyd Nii Kwei Asamoah, Michael Osei Boateng, Vera Oye Bram-Larbi, Kumi Alfred Ababio and Abanga Fuseini Yakubu.

Three aspirants picked forms to contest the National Women Organiser position.

They are Mavis Hawa Koomson, Perpetual Ekua Lomokie Akwada, and Safia Mohammed.

The National Communications Director position has two aspirants – Dennis Miracles Aboagye and Evans Kodo.

Gordon Asare Bediako, who had expressed interest in the Communications Director position, withdrew from the race on Saturday and endorsed Mr Aboagye.

For the National Vice Chairperson position, 13 aspirants picked forms. They include Henry Nana Boakye, Kojo Fosu Boadu, Mustapha Abdul Hameed, Samuel Pyne, Richard Ahiagba, Abena Pokua Boaitey Amoah, Alhaji Masawudu Osman, Yaa Amponsah Frimpong, George Kwabena Abankwah Yeboah, Horma Miez, Richard Oti Aboagye, Bright Esselfie Kumi and Nana Akomea.

The National Treasurer position attracted four aspirants – Alfred Kojo Thompson, Collins Nuntwiri Nuamah, Tahiru Issahaku Moomin and Ahmed Ruka Saida.

Five aspirants picked forms for the National Nasara Organiser position. They are Issaka Muazo Kunata, Salim Bamba, Razak Tahiru Maiga, Awal Mohammed and Mohammed Ali Suraj.

The NPP National Officers Elections Committee said the purchase or collection of a nomination form did not, by itself, constitute a valid nomination or candidature.

An aspirant would become a nominee only after properly filing the completed nomination form and accompanying documents within the prescribed period, subject to vetting and other processes required under the party’s constitution and election regulations, it said.

Filing of completed nomination forms commenced on Sunday, August 23, and will close on Saturday, August 29, 2026.

The nominees will subsequently be vetted from Monday, August 31, to Thursday, September 3, 2026.

The committee said the date for balloting had not yet been fixed because it wanted the filing, vetting and possible appeals processes to be completed before determining the final field of candidates.

Ghana News.title: Getting heard in Parliament currently is difficult – Afenyo-Markin
Ghana News.content:
Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin says that getting the Minority's voice heard in Parliament has become difficult due to the Majority's numerical strength.

Speaking on Joy News’ The Probe on Sunday, he said the Minority has to work harder to ensure its views are heard despite having fewer MPs.

“It is a very difficult one because you are in opposition, and you need to work hard with your colleagues to ensure that, notwithstanding your numbers, your voice is heard,” he said.

The Effutu MP said the current parliamentary arithmetic presents a major challenge for the Minority, with the Majority holding 189 seats.

“So, getting your voice heard in a chamber where the majority is 189 can be very difficult,” he said.

He also pointed to the leadership of Parliament as another factor that makes the Minority’s task challenging.

“You have a speaker who is not on your side in terms of party affiliation, and you have a first deputy who is also part of the majority, and obviously, his first mandate will be to protect his side,” he said.

According to him, the situation requires the Minority to adopt a deliberate approach to its work in Parliament.

“So it calls for a lot of hard work, determination, and a focused strategy to make sure that you navigate well,” he said.

Afenyo-Markin, however, said the Minority is not intimidated by its current numbers.

He said the New Patriotic Party has previously operated in Parliament with a much smaller representation and still managed to grow its numbers.

“This is not the first time NPP is getting into the chamber with fewer numbers,” he said.

He cited the Second Parliament, when the NPP had 61 MPs against the National Democratic Congress's 133.

“You may recall that in 1992 we didn’t participate in the parliamentary elections. So, in the second parliament, we had 61, led by J. H. Mensah, and the NDC had 133,” he said.

Afenyo-Markin said the NPP later increased its parliamentary representation to 102 by the 2000 election.

“But through their industry, by the 2000 election, that 61 increased to 102,” he said.

He insisted that the current 87-member Minority would not be discouraged by the numbers.

“So I’m not perturbed at all by the numbers today. We’re 87. We say we are a mighty minority,” he said.

He said the Minority’s strength would be measured by the quality of its contribution rather than its numbers.

“We feel the might in the substance we put out, and we are not intimidated by the numbers,” he said.

“Our voice must be heard, and when people hear us, they must see substance in us,” Afenyo-Markin added.

Ghana News.title: GHS launches strategic PHEOC documents to strengthen public health emergency response
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Health Service (GHS) has launched five strategic documents to help strengthen public health emergency preparedness and response across the country.

The event saw the launch of the strategic National Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (PHEOC) documents and the presentation of a national roadmap for the operationalisation of PHEOC across Ghana.

The five documents launched were the National PHEOC Strategic Plan 2026-2030, National PHEOC Handbook 2026, and National PHEOC Standard Operating Procedures, Volume One.

The others are the National Health Workforce Search and Strategy Plan 2026-2034 and the National Public Health Workforce Search and Management SOP, Volume Two.

The documents were developed through collaboration among the Ministry of Health, GHS, security and emergency services, academia, research institutions, professional bodies, civil society and private-sector stakeholders.

This formed part of efforts by the service to build a more resilient, coordinated and sustainable public health emergency management system.

Dr Samuel Kaba Akoriyea, the Director-General of the GHS, said the launch marked an important step in strengthening Ghana’s national health security.

He said public health emergencies required a unified response from all relevant institutions, adding: “When disease spreads, success is not determined by plans left on the shelf. It is determined by our capacity to act as one unified system.”

Dr Akoriyea said early detection, timely treatment and prompt care were critical to saving lives as Ghana had experienced seasonal outbreaks of meningitis, cholera, typhoid and other diseases.

The Public Health Emergency Operations Centre, he said, would help bridge the gap between data collection and strategic action.

“PHEOC would also connect health agencies, emergency services, laboratories and animal health agencies” he noted, adding that the centre would help provide a platform for coordinated action during public health emergencies.

It would also support the implementation of the International Health Regulations and address gaps identified through joint external evaluations.

He noted that Ghana had learnt important lessons from major disease outbreaks, including the COVID-19 pandemic, saying the focus must now shift from documents to action and from preparedness on paper to readiness in practice.

He called for a functional, connected and sustainable emergency response system.

Dr Lawrence Lartey, Head of the National PHEOC, said the implementation strategy focused on seven key areas.

These include governance and institutionalisation, ICT and public health intelligence, logistics and infrastructure, emergency operations and incident management, workforce capacity, sustainability and multispectral coordination.

Dr Lartey said the strategy would promote the use of integrated dashboards and other digital systems to support timely decision making.

He said logistics and infrastructure would also be strengthened to support rapid deployment during outbreaks and emergencies, adding that trained and skilled workforce was necessary for effective emergency response.

Dr Lartey said the strategy would connect emergency operations at the national, regional, district and community levels, aimed to establish one coordinated system with common standards and shared situational awareness.

He said regular testing, monitoring and after-action reviews would help improve the health system while sustainable financing and accountability would also be critical to the success of the PHEOC.

Domestic financing must be strengthened while partner support was properly aligned, Dr Lartey said, and that “The launch is not the destination. It is a transition to implementation.”

Ghana News.title: MCE cuts sod for construction of storm drains in Ejura-Sekyedumase
Ghana News.content:
Rafiu Adam Seidu, the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) for Ejura-Sekyedumase, has cut the sod for the construction of storm drains at Kotokoliline in the Ejura township to address perennial flooding and improve sanitation in the municipality.

The sod-cutting ceremony was attended by Assembly Members, heads of departments and agencies, the Chief Imam, Sheikh Ishak Anasaree, traditional leaders, political party representatives and other stakeholders.

Mr Seidu said the project formed part of the Assembly’s efforts to build a resilient, safer and more prosperous municipality.

He said the construction of the drains went beyond the provision of concrete structures, explaining that it was aimed at addressing perennial flooding, protecting lives and property, improving sanitation and safeguarding businesses and livelihoods.

He said the intervention would also contribute to creating a safer and more resilient urban environment for residents.

After the ceremony, the MCE and other stakeholders inspected ongoing construction works at the Ejura 24-Hour Economy Market.

He described the market project as a key intervention that would stimulate economic activity, create opportunities for traders and entrepreneurs, generate employment, and contribute significantly to the municipality’s economic transformation upon completion.

He said the two projects demonstrated the benefits of collaboration among local authorities, stakeholders and development partners in advancing development.

Mr Seidu reaffirmed the Assembly’s commitment to engaging relevant authorities, stakeholders and development partners to attract more meaningful projects and investments to the municipality.

He said the Assembly would continue to work to ensure that development was visible, economic opportunities were expanded and all communities had a stake in the municipality’s progress.

Ghana News.title: Oti NPP Communication Director alleges region receives fewer birds under ‘Nkoko nkitinkiti’; NDC debunks claim
Ghana News.content:
Seidu Musah, Oti Regional Communication Director of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), has alleged that only 810 birds under the government’s ‘Nkoko Nkitinkiti’ initiative have been brought to the Oti Region, claiming that the beneficiaries were largely members of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC).

He questioned whether the reported number of birds was sufficient to meet the needs of beneficiaries across the region, considering the population, number of communities and the size of the NDC’s membership in the Oti Region.

Mr Musah made the allegation in an exclusive interview with the Ghana News Agency (GNA) to assess the performance of the NDC government in the region since assuming office.

He said the government had been in office for about one-and-a-half years and was approaching its second year, but, in his assessment, there were no significant tangible achievements to show its tenure in the region.

According to him, the government had made several promises to the people of Oti, but the pace of implementation of those commitments had fallen short of residents’ expectations.

He also called for greater transparency in the implementation of the Nkoko Nkitinkiti initiative, particularly regarding the number of birds supplied to the region, the criteria for selecting beneficiaries, and their geographical distribution.

He said such information would enable the public to assess whether the programme was being implemented fairly and achieving its intended objective of supporting livelihoods.

Mr Musah said the NPP would continue to monitor government programmes and policies in the region and hold the government accountable for its promises.

He, however, acknowledged that government programmes should ultimately be assessed based on their impact on ordinary citizens rather than political considerations.

Mr Musah urged the government to prioritise projects and interventions that would directly improve the livelihoods of farmers, young people, women and small-scale entrepreneurs.

Ghana News Agency investigations reveal otherwise as confirmed by Mr Williams Ntoso, Oti Deputy Director of Communication of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), who refuted Mr Musah’s claim, describing the allegation as untrue.

He said the Nkoko Nkitinkiti initiative had not supplied only 810 birds to the region as alleged.

According to Mr Ntoso, each of the nine Municipal and District Assemblies in the Oti Region received 10,000 birds under the programme, bringing the total number supplied to the region to 90,000 birds.

He therefore urged the public to disregard the claim that only 810 birds had been brought to the region, saying the actual figure was 90,000.

The NDC Deputy Regional Communication Director maintained that the programme was being implemented across the region and was intended to support beneficiaries and improve livelihoods.

Ghana News.title: Our voice must be heard – Afenyo-Markin warns Majority against taking NPP’s 87 MPs for granted
Ghana News.content:
Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin has warned the governing majority against taking the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) 87 MPs for granted, insisting that the Minority’s voice must be heard in Parliament.

Speaking on Joy News’ The Probe on Sunday, the Effutu MP acknowledged the difficulty of leading a smaller caucus in a chamber where the governing side has 189 MPs.

He said the Minority must work harder to ensure its concerns receive attention despite its numerical disadvantage.

“Well, it’s a very difficult one because you are in opposition, and you need to work hard with your colleagues to ensure that, notwithstanding your numbers, your voice is heard.”

Mr Afenyo-Markin said the task is made more challenging by the composition of Parliament’s leadership.

“You have a speaker who is not on your side in terms of party affiliation, and you have a first deputy who is also part of the majority, and obviously, his first mandate will be to protect his side.”

He said the situation requires the NPP caucus to adopt a deliberate approach to parliamentary business.

“So it calls for a lot of hard work, determination, and a focused strategy to make sure that you navigate well.”

Despite the current numbers, Mr Afenyo-Markin said he is not intimidated by the size of the governing majority.

He pointed to the NPP’s history in Parliament to argue that a smaller caucus can grow through sustained work.

“This is not the first time NPP is getting into the chamber with fewer numbers.”

He recalled that the NPP had 61 MPs in the Second Parliament after it did not participate in the 1992 parliamentary elections.

“You may recall that in 1992 we didn’t participate in the parliamentary elections. So, in the second parliament, we had 61, led by J. H. Mensah, and the NDC had 133.”

According to him, the party’s parliamentary fortunes improved significantly in the years that followed.

“But through their industry, by the 2000 election, that 61 increased to 102.”

He said that history gives him confidence that the current 87-member caucus can also make an impact.

“So I’m not perturbed at all by the numbers today. We’re 87. We say we are a mighty minority. We feel the might in the substance we put out, and we are not intimidated by the numbers.”

Mr Afenyo-Markin stressed that the Minority’s effectiveness should not be measured solely by its numerical strength.

“Our voice must be heard, and when people hear us, they must see substance in us.”

He said the focus, therefore, remains on ensuring the NPP caucus is heard and its contributions carry weight in Parliament.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
