World.title: Iraq’s IDC relocates drilling rig from Zubair oil field to East Baghdad field
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Drilling Company (IDC) is relocating the IDC-51 drilling rig from the Zubair oil field in the southern province of Basra to the East Baghdad South field.

Under the supervision of the state-owned Midland Oil Company (MOC), the step is part of a deal with EBS Petroleum, an Iraqi-registered subsidiary of Chinese state-owned firm ZhenHua Oil, to drill 17 horizontal wells to increase production capacity in Iraq’s central region.

The move entails disassembling the rig at Zubair, shipping components, reassembling, and conducting safety tests at East Baghdad South.

This project builds on the IDC’s past development phases in the same field, which featured distinct campaigns of 27 and 18 horizontal wells.

The East Baghdad South field is the extremely productive southern section of the larger, super-giant East Baghdad oilfield complex.

The oilfield is one of Iraq’s most unusual energy resources, measuring around 60 kilometers in length and 12 kilometers in its width. It is located just under the capital’s densely populated suburbs.

Appraisal drilling increased the proved reserves of the East Baghdad field to 15 billion barrels, including an enormous reservoir of medium and light oil.

World.title: Iraq’s PMF repels ISIS attack in Salah al-Din province
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) successfully foiled on Sunday an attack by ISIS terrorists on a military position in the Tuz Khurmatu region in the eastern province of Salah al-Din.

The raid targeted an isolated outpost belonging to the Commando Regiment of the PMF’s 63rd Brigade.

ISIS militants launched an armed attack from a mountain, resulting in an intense battle, with loud gunfire and explosions reported by civilians.

The Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) represent a coalition of Shia paramilitary groups that have been officially incorporated into Iraq’s national security forces. This coalition consists of various militias that have ties with Iran.

PMF fighters engaged the attackers immediately, compelling them to retreat into the challenging terrain without accomplishing any tactical objectives. No casualties have been reported among PMF personnel.

Iraqi Army and PMF soldiers started a coordinated, large-scale search operation in a nearby mountainous area to track down fleeing terrorists and identify their locations.

This failed attack highlights the ongoing threat of secret factions belonging to the ISIS group in isolated places.

Analysts see that these small-scale, opportunistic ambushes are intended to test local defense networks as Baghdad moves to autonomous state security ahead of the scheduled withdrawal of international coalition forces.

World.title: Iraq to repatriate 6,000 foreign prisoners held in prisons
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Justice has launched legal and diplomatic efforts to repatriate about 6,000 foreign inmates to their home countries.

The Iraqi National Security Council has authorized an official direction for this large-scale initiative.

The initiative involves over 6,000 detained and sentenced individuals from 61 foreign countries.

Syrian nationals make up the biggest group. Other notable nationalities are Moroccans, Americans, Canadians, Russians, Tunisians, and Turks.

The transfer process completely excludes convicts serving death sentences in Iraq.

Under the signed court accords, transferred individuals are expected to serve their remaining imprisonments in their home countries.

The great bulk of these foreign inmates are linked to the terrorist organization ISIS and were transferred to Iraqi custody earlier in 2026.

To prevent major jail breakouts, the US Central Command (CENTCOM) arranged the removal of thousands of terrorists from vulnerable northeastern Syrian detention sites.

Baghdad received the prisoners with the clear intention that they would not stay indefinitely and is now actively pressuring other countries to take responsibility for its residents.

World.title: Baghdad hosts Iraqi-Libyan Joint Committee meetings after 25-year hiatus
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Libya’s Acting Foreign Minister Taher al-Baour is in Baghdad heading a high-level delegation to co-chair the Iraqi-Libyan Joint Committee meetings, which have resumed after a 25-year break.

Al-Baour met with Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein to discuss strategies to enhance political, diplomatic, and regional ties between Baghdad and Tripoli.

Their discussions focused on aligning mutual political positions on regional problems and increasing combined consular and diplomatic presence.

Following their meeting, al-Baour and Hussein held a joint press conference. Al-Baour emphasized Libya’s immediate need to partner with Iraq to repair and staff key public facilities, particularly in education and healthcare.

The Libyan delegation is finalizing several memoranda of understanding covering a wide range of economic and development areas.

Al-Baour’s team includes officials from several government bodies affiliated with the Tripoli-based Government of National Unity (GNU).

According to the Iraqi Foreign Ministry, this diplomatic drive follows Iraq’s offer to resume coordination and signify a return to normalized, regular diplomatic ties between the two countries.

The delegation’s trip to Baghdad builds directly upon virtual expert meetings organized by the Libyan Ministry of Foreign Affairs to conclude trade agreements with Iraqi officials before signatures are authorized.

World.title: Japanese archaeological missions to return to Iraq for excavations and training
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Japanese archaeological excavation teams are preparing to return to Iraq to conduct scientific digs and provide hands-on field training for local researchers, according to statements made on Sunday, August 23, 2026, by Dr. Laith Majeed Hussein, Director of the Japanese–Iraqi Institute for Archaeological Education.

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Hussein outlined that bilateral cooperation is expanding beyond field excavation to encompass academic faculty recruitment from Japan and Egypt to support the Department of Japanese Language and Literature at the University of Baghdad’s College of Arts.

Key Academic Initiatives & Archaeological Milestones

Resumption of Japanese Excavation Missions: Japanese archaeological teams—holding a multi-decade legacy of Mesopotamian field research—are coordinating their return following improvements in domestic security conditions to resume field surveying, artifact conservation, and joint research.

Hands-on Field Training: Upcoming excavation seasons will integrate joint fieldwork, pairing Japanese specialists and university students with Iraqi researchers and trainees to teach modern stratigraphic excavation and surveying methods.

Expansion of Japanese Language Studies: To build language proficiency and strengthen cultural exchange, the University of Baghdad’s College of Arts is recruiting native instructors and specialized faculty from Japan and Egypt to teach within its Japanese Language Department.

Institutional Heritage Ties: Dr. Hussein highlighted the historical roots of bilateral academic engagement, citing the establishment of the Center for the Revival of Arab Scientific Heritage in Baghdad in 1977, founded in close partnership with Japanese academic institutions.

International Assyriology Conference: Hussein noted that Baghdad had finalized preparations to host the 2026 Rencontre Assyriologique Internationale (International Congress of Assyriology); however, regional security tensions prompted a postponement, with organizers preparing to reapply for international convening approvals for a future date.

The revival of Japanese archaeological missions reflects the broader international reintegration of Iraq’s academic and heritage institutions.

By combining field excavations with university-level language instruction and peer-reviewed publishing partnerships, the Japanese–Iraqi Institute for Archaeological Education aims to equip a new generation of Iraqi scholars with advanced excavation methodologies and promote the preservation of Mesopotamian cultural heritage.

World.title: Economist: Iran Hormuz permits ‘too late’ as tankers secure safe passage
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi economic expert Ziyad Al-Hashemi stated on Saturday, August 22, 2026, that international crude buyers have successfully expanded oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz independently, making Tehran’s recent exceptional passage permits redundant.

According to Al-Hashemi’s analysis, published on social media and reported by regional news platforms, maritime tracking indicators show that commercial operators adapted to regional security risks days before official Iranian clearances were publicized. Consequently, he described Tehran’s formal approval as a late public-relations gesture aimed at courting the Iraqi public rather than a decisive logistical breakthrough.

Maritime Analytics & Key Operational Metrics

1 to 2 Million BPD Flowing: Energy market and maritime analytics from Vortexa confirm that seaborne crude volumes traversing the Strait of Hormuz averaged between 1 million and 2 million barrels per day (bpd) over the past 10 days, primarily originating from Iraq and Saudi Arabia.

Regional Total Reaching 3M BPD: Adding daily crude and fuel consignments from Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates, total maritime throughput across the waterway reached approximately 3 million bpd.

Adoption of “Dark Sailings”: Energy trading firms and shipping lines adapted by deploying smaller tankers and executing “dark sailings”—turning off or minimizing Automatic Identification System (AIS) transponders—to obscure vessel positions and reduce targeting risks during transit.

Declining Maritime Attacks: Despite an increase in passing tanker traffic, maritime incidents and Iranian interdictions declined notably over the same period, signaling either altered strategic calculations regarding the Strait of Hormuz or diminished operational capacity to sustain maritime disruption.

Diminished Strategic Value of Permits: Because international buyers and shipping syndicates had already established functional transit routines, Al-Hashemi noted that Tehran’s publicized approvals arrived after navigational flows had already stabilized.

The analysis follows recent diplomatic and security discussions held in Baghdad between Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Iraqi officials, during which Tehran agreed to grant exceptional passage permits to designated Iraqi crude tankers navigating the chokepoint.

While state-level agreements sought to address maritime concerns, real-time energy flow tracking indicates that commercial charterers and global energy buyers utilized operational workarounds and alternative navigation protocols to maintain southern crude flows out of Basra’s offshore terminals.

World.title: Iraqi dinar exchange rates hold near 154,500 IQD per $100

World.title: 17th Agricultural Week opens in Baghdad: 30M date palm plan and tech deals
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The 17th Agricultural Week Exhibition for agricultural mechanization, animal production, and food processing officially launched at the Baghdad International Fairgrounds on Saturday, August 22, 2026.

Operating under the theme “Supporting Agriculture to Harvest a Sustainable Future,” the exhibition hosts public- and private-sector pavilions featuring 209 local and international agricultural enterprises showcasing modern farming technology, climate-resilient crop inputs, and livestock pharmaceuticals.

Key Regional Partnerships & Technological Initiatives

1. Saudi-Iraqi Plant Biotechnology & Date Palm Expansion

30 Million Palm Target: Plant tissue culture specialist Saleh Al-Tuwaijri announced a strategic initiative to expand Iraq’s date palm population from approximately 20 million to 30 million trees.

Five-Year Production Capacity: Advanced tissue culture propagation techniques are projected to fulfill 30% to 40% of Iraq’s total seedling requirements over the next five years.

Domestic Biotechnology Labs: With logistical coordination from the Iraqi Ministries of Agriculture and Trade, the Saudi firm finalized the establishment of a specialized plant tissue culture laboratory inside Iraq.

Executive Backing: Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi, accompanied by the Ministers of Agriculture and Trade, toured the biotechnology pavilion during the exhibition to inspect progress and confirm state support.

2. Climate-Resilient Agricultural Solutions (Debbane – Lebanon)

Field Support & Climate Adaptation: Bassem Mohammed Hassan Al-Amin, Director General of Lebanon’s Debbane Modern Agriculture, highlighted that ongoing climate change necessitates specialized heat- and drought-tolerant seeds and soil fertilizers.

Agronomic Field Consulting: Engineering teams are deployed across Iraqi farmlands to deliver on-site technical guidance to optimize seasonal crop yields.

3. Livestock & Veterinary Pharmaceuticals (Syria)

Aviation & Cattle Sector Growth: Ammar Mohammed Al-Qazwini, Director General of the Arab Company for Veterinary Medicine Industries (Syria), noted Iraq’s expanding poultry operations, commercial dairy farms, and feed manufacturing infrastructure.

Cross-Border Veterinary Expertise: Syrian pharmaceutical manufacturers are providing advanced veterinary medicines and poultry treatments to boost local livestock productivity.

The 17th Agricultural Week serves as a regional conduit for introducing climate-adaptive biotechnology, localized seed breeding, and livestock healthcare into Iraq’s domestic farming ecosystem.

By facilitating cross-border investments and establishing domestic biotechnology laboratories, Iraq seeks to strengthen its national date palm reserves, reduce agricultural import dependency, and enhance long-term food security amid ongoing regional climate challenges.

World.title: Change in revenue record doesn't create, end property title: SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Observing that mutation of a property in revenue records does not create or extinguish ownership, Supreme Court has said that title of property cannot be decided on the sole basis of revenue record and it must be weighed along with other evidence.

A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Augustine George Masih quashed the order of Madhya Pradesh HC which decided a title dispute on the basis of the revenue record. It said a right in immovable property cannot be treated as having been voluntarily abandoned because of a revenue entry in favour of another person. It must be independently established by the party relying on it.

The bench said,âIt is settled law that an entry in the revenue record neither creates nor extinguishes title and exists essentially for fiscal purposes.

The order of the naib tehsildar may regulate the revenue record, but it cannot, merely by recording one personâs name in place of another, operate as a conveyance or a relinquishment of proprietary rights, and the civil court remains fully competent to determine the underlying title, which the revenue entry follows .

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âThe statutory presumption of correctness attaching to a revenue entry under Section 117 of the MP Land Revenue Code, 1959, is a rebuttable evidentiary presumption and not a presumption of title, and it must be weighed along with the rest of the evidence.â





It said mutation of a property in revenue record does not create or extinguish title nor has it any presumptive value and it only enables the person in whose favour mutation is ordered to pay the land revenue in question. â SC said the starting point of the limitation canât be fixed merely by identifying the date on which the revenue entry was made.

World.title: Parliament monsoon session yet to be prorogued, BJP, Congress face off over women’s bill

âWhat explains the abnormal delay now? Is the Union home minister still in search of his super-tainted 2/3rd majority to get the constitutional amendment bill on delimitation passed in a special session,â Congressâs Jairam Ramesh asked.

Congress, too, was mindful of the possibility of a short upcoming session and claimed that BJP is still searching for âsuper taintedâ majority in Lok Sabha, in what was a swipe at govtâs alleged attempts to split opposition parties to reach the two-thirds majority in the House needed for the billâs passage.





Ramesh said the gap between Parliamentâs adjournment and its prorogation is generally two to four days. But the monsoon session, which ended on Aug 13, has not been prorogued yet.

When a session is prorogued, govt has to go through the protocol for calling a new session that conventionally requires a gap of 15 to 20 days.

World.title: On National Space Day, PM Modi hails Gen Z for building new tech; Isro chief says plan to launch 8 vehicle, 12 satellite missions

PM Modi interacting with CEOs of 20 space startups in New Delhi on Friday

NEW DELHI: On the 3rd National Space Day, PM Narendra Modi on Sunday hailed India's global rise in the space sector and praised Gen Z for building new technologies, saying this rise has made India a âmagnetâ for global investors.Sharing a video of his speeches, PM Modi said, âI said in Ayodhya that this is the beginning of a new cycle of change. In this new cycle, India is steadily expanding its space presence in the global order, and this is clearly reflected in our space programme. Together, we have resolved to make India a developed nation by 2047, and the space sector plays a vital role in achieving this goal.âPraising the youth of the nation, the PM said, âToday, these Gen Z engineers, designers, coders and scientists are building new technologies. Be it propulsion systems, composite materials, rocket stages or satellite platforms, India's youth is working in areas that were not even imagined some time ago.â He also hailed the private space sector saying, âIndia's private space talent is making its own identity in the world. âJust two days ago, the PM interacted with CEOs and founders of 20 space startups on Friday and highlighted India's cost-competitiveness in launching space ventures.He emphasised that the country's vast talent pool and high risk-taking capacity would allow India to rapidly establish a dominant position in the global space sector, according to the transcript of the interaction, which was released on Sunday. One of the CEOs told the PM that after India opened the space industry for private players, a very positive trend was observed and many Indian citizens living in the US and Europe now want to return and work in the country. Among the most closely watched missions is the first uncrewed flight under the Gaganyaan programme, which Isro expects to undertake within the next four months, he said. Narayanan said the Gaganyaan programme had completed about 8,000 tests and was now approaching its final stage. âWe are in the final leg,â he said.Space minister Jitendra Singh said on X, âOn National Space Day, we remember the historic success of Chandrayaan-3, a moment that placed India among the worldâs leading spacefaring nations. Remarkable achievement of our scientists, backed by the progressive vision of PM.PM Shri Narendra Modi continues to inspire generations. Celebrating our scientists, innovators and the unstoppable spirit of ViksitBharat. âWith the historic milestone of 100 launches and 548 satellites placed in orbit, including around 460 in the last decade alone, Indiaâs space sector is reaching new horizons, petroleum and natural gas minister Hardeep Singh Puri said on Sunday.

World.title: India’s satellite launch cost 4x US, says Cambridge study; space dept source contradicts report
World.content:
Indiaâs space price tag comes under scrutiny as Cambridge research flags high launch costs, while the government says key subsidies and savings were overlooked

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A 2026 University of Cambridge study has found that Indiaâs per-kilogram launch costs are four times higher than Americaâs and, in fact, the costliest in the world. However, a highly-placed source in the Department of Space told TOI that the study has not factored in Indiaâs subsidies, saving cost in transport and logistic costs and space manoeuvre costs.A peer-reviewed paper published in the respected Elsevier journal Economics Letters by economists Alessio Terzi of the University of Cambridge and Francesco Nicoli of Politecnico di Torino, Turin, points at a novel database covering more than 6,740 rocket launches between 1960 and 2025. The standardised dataset of rocket launches has covered 16 geographical entities, including all the major spacefaring nations: US, Russia, China, India, Europe, and Japan. It includes over 330 different rocket configurations and 4,405 launches.According to the article, at the end of 2025, the cost of launching a satellite from India stood at $13,302 (Rs 12.7 lakh) per kg aboard rockets available in the country, an amount that was more than four times the figure of US, wherein the cost is $3,225 (Rs 3.1 lakh). The study finds the US to be the lowest among all the markets studied. As per the study, India is more expensive than the European Union, Russia, China and Japan.After India, Europeâs rocket launch cost is the next most expensive at $9,897 (Rs 9.5 lakh) per kg.However, a highly-placed source in the Dept of Space told TOI that the study has not factored in various concessions provided by Isroâs commercial wing NSIL. The Indian space agency gives âsatellite customers 30% subsidy on cost of launchesâ. âSecondly, Indian customers save money in logistics and transport when launched from Sriharikota. Third foreign launchers normally send all satellites from one launcher to the same orbit, which leads to rise in launch cost as satellites piggyback on the primary payload have to be manoeuvred to their respective orbit,â the source said.Moreover, the Department of Space (DoS) and IN-SPACe has rolled out these financial incentives through two parallel frameworks: the Launch Services Price-support Scheme (LSPS) and Price Support Scheme. Both programmes are designed to significantly reduce the entry barriers for Indian non-govt entities. IN-SPACe also provides financial support ranging from 30% to 100% for satellite launches and related space infrastructure under its Rs 800 crore LSPS: up to 50% support for utilising Isro and Department of Space launch facilities; a 30% subsidy on launch costs (capped at $3,000/kg) for small vehicles carrying up to 500 kg; full 100% funding (capped at $13,000/kg for up to four missions) for payloads up to 120 kg.The Cambridge research also said, âThe expense of launching cargo into space will plummet over the next few years, with the cost of reaching orbit forecast to more than halve between now and the end of the decade, and fall around 93% by 2040. The cost of sending a kilogram of payload into low Earth orbit, an average of $3,868 last year, is set to fall more than 58% to just $1,569 by 2030, and could reach as little as 273 US dollars per kilo by 2040, the study suggests.

World.title: J&K govt warns against buying shock-emitting ‘dog sticks’, cites arms law
World.content:
J&K may bring electric 'dog sticks' under arms rules as authorities flag animal cruelty concerns and warn against their use on street dogs

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: Electronically operated, shock-delivering âdog sticksâ advertised online as protection against street dogs may be brought under the ambit of J&K Arms Rules, 2016, the govt has announced as such devices come under scrutiny for alleged violations of laws against animal cruelty.In a statement issued late Saturday, J&Kâs housing and urban development department (HUDD) cautioned that electric shock guns, stun devices, electric prods or similar devices should not be used for stray animals as they inflict unnecessary pain on them and contravene Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960.The advisory has been triggered by the online ads about such âdog sticksâ from âM/s Gambs Enterprisesâ, a Pulwama private firm. The department said it was examining the legal classification of such devices, the authority under which they are sold and their intended use.âAll dog catchers, agencies, contractors, animal welfare organisations, municipal bodies and the public are advised not to procure or use electric shock devices for catching, restraining or handling street dogs,â the statement reads. CM Omar Abdullah handles the department.HUDD secretary Mandeep Kour was not available for comment.The statement says specific licences are required under Section 5 of Arms Rules for sale, transfer or possession of âprescribed classes of armsâ, adding not having such documents amount to violations.âThe Arms Rules, 2016 specifically regulate Electronic Disabling Devices (EDDs). Depending upon their statutory classification and specifications, such devices may fall within the restricted or permissible arms categories, and Rule 89(3) provides that EDDs shall be sold only through authorised arms and ammunition dealers holding the requisite licence,â the statement says.J&K recorded over 2 lakh dog-bite cases in the past two years -- 1.2 lakh in Jammu and around 80,000 in the Valley. In Jammu district alone, 33,065 cases were reported in 2024 and 43,759 in 2025, taking its two-year total to 76,824. Srinagar had 12,557 cases in 2024 and 12,592 in 2025. A Srinagar municipal corporation survey in 2023 estimated the number of stray dogs at 64,416.

World.title: Ladakh gears up for flights from Thoise by December, Kargil later
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Ladakh authorities have stepped up efforts to start commercial flights from Kargil and Thoise, where such services are targeted for Dec this year. The Union territory at present has only one airport, Leh, for commercial flights.

At a meeting chaired by LG Vinai Kumar Saxena, IAF approved five acres of land for a new civil terminal at Thoise, located in Nubra Valley. Runway recarpeting is underway and is expected to be completed by Nov.

On Kargil, which has an airstrip for defence operations, the authorities decided to assess the existing infrastructure, technical requirements and other aspects necessary for starting civilian flights.

Officials from the defence ministry, IAF, Airports Authority of India and the UT administration attended the meeting held on Friday at Ladakh Bhavan in New Delhi.

âThe meeting focused on resolving infrastructure, regulatory and operational issues to enable early commencement of civilian flights from the strategically and socio-economically important airports. These will significantly boost connectivity in the border areas,â a govt spokesperson said.

Saxena emphasised the need for time-bound operationalisation, saying commercial flights from both points would also unlock the immense tourism potential of areas such as Kargil, Drass, Turtuk and Siachen Base Camp.





âCommercial flights are expected to provide greater accessibility to residents of Nubra and facilitate travel for visitors to destinations including Turtuk, Siachen and other parts while supporting tourism and local economic activity,â Saxena said.

In March this year, chief executive councillor (CEC) of Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council-Kargil (LAHDC) Mohd Jaffar Akhoon and Ladakh MP Mohmad Haneefa had met Union home minister Amit Shah in Delhi and sought civilian flights from Kargil. World.title: Kerala Forest officer booked over alleged misbehaviour with women on train
World.content:
The Railway police have registered a case against Kasaragod Divisional Forest Officer (DFO) Jose Matthew following a complaint that he allegedly behaved indecently towards women passengers and made obscene gestures while travelling on the Okha Express.

According to the complaint, the incident occurred when the women were travelling from Thiruvananthapuram to Kasaragod on Saturday. They alleged that the DFO behaved inappropriately towards them and made objectionable gestures during the journey.

The women alerted the police control room while the train was en route. Following alert a police person reached the train and collected preliminary information and RPF and local police also jointly care that initial details as part of measures to ensure passenger safety.

The Kasaragod Railway police subsequently registered a case and launched a detailed investigation. Officers are collecting statement from other passengers and examination evidence related to the complaint.

The police said further legal action would be taken if the allegations are substantiated during the investigation. This could include the arrest of the accused officer. The exact section of law to be invoked will be determine based on the findings of the investigation

Authorities said the version of the accused officer would also have to be examined as part of the investigation. No response has so far be obtained from Mr. Mathew regarding the allegations.

World.title: Odisha govt rejects Opposition demand for special Assembly session on mining Bill
World.content:
The Odisha government has rejected opposition BJD and Congress' demand for convening a special session of the Assembly to discuss the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, recently passed by Parliament.

Parliamentary Affairs Minister Mukesh Mahaling said on Sunday (August 23, 2026) that there was no need for a special session, as the issue could be discussed during the upcoming monsoon session, which would be convened soon.

The demand for a special session was made by Leader of Opposition Naveen Patnaik and Congress Legislature Party leader Ram Chandra Kadam.

Describing the proposed mining legislation as "anti-Odisha" and harmful to the State's interests, both leaders wrote to Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, seeking a special session and an all-party meeting on the issue.

The Congress criticised the BJP government over rejection of the demand for a special session.

"It is very unfortunate that the Minister has rejected the Congress' demand for a special session on the MMDR Bill. The State will lose about ₹10,000 crore in revenue annually, and will also have to bear the loss of lakhs of crores of rupees in arrears," state Congress vice-president Santosh Singh Saluja said.

The Congress leader alleged that the Centre was seeking control over Odisha's natural resources, including its water, forests, land and minerals, after coming to power in the State, in the name of 'Odia Asmita' (Odia pride).

Congress whip Razen Ekka said, "There will be demonstrations in the State, from the state capital to gram panchayats, and the houses of all BJP MPs will also be gheraoed in the coming days." Describing the BJP as a "party of businessmen", the BJD questioned the alleged silence of its 25 MPs from Odisha - 20 in the Lok Sabha and five in the Rajya Sabha - during the passage of the MMDR Amendment Bill in Parliament.

Addressing a press conference, BJD senior general secretary Pritiranjan Gharai claimed that the Bill was passed in Parliament without any discussion.

"This will cause extensive losses to Odisha. The revenue from all the mines in the State will go under the control of the central government," he asserted.

World.title: Chlorine gas leaks at water treatment plant in Nagpur, several hospitalised
World.content:
Chlorine gas leak at a water treatment plant in Nagpur shortly after midnight on Monday (August 24, 2026) sent nearby residents running for safety and left many people gasping for breath, officials said.

Several people were hospitalised after the leakage occurred in a 900-kg capacity chlorine gas cylinder at the water treatment plant in Godhani village at around 1 a.m., the Nagpur Municipal Corporation (NMC) said.

The gas spread to nearby residential areas, triggering panic. Many people experienced coughing and difficulty in breathing, it said.

#WATCH | Nagpur, Maharashtra: Rescue operations are underway after a chlorine gas leak was reported at a water purification plant belonging to the Maharashtra Jeevan Pradhikaran in the Godhni area pic.twitter.com/1QArLOZden — ANI (@ANI) August 24, 2026

Police later evacuated residents within a 200‑metre radius to safe locations and sealed off the affected area.

Residents of nearby settlements were instructed to move away, and several people were taken to hospitals for treatment, the NMC said in a release.

After being alerted, the civic fire personnel rushed to the spot with two water tenders and breathing apparatus. Staff of the Orange City Water Pvt Ltd (OCW), which supplies drinking water in Nagpur, and a team of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) were also called in for assistance.

At about 5.30 a.m., after the leak was plugged, the NDRF team, firefighters and OCW personnel placed the chlorine cylinder into a tank of water mixed with caustic soda, the civic body said.

An official at Mankapur police station said that security personnel evacuated residents within a 200‑metre radius to safe locations and cordoned off the area.

Many people went to hospitals on their own, while many others were hospitalised by the police, he said.

The police have appealed to people not to believe in rumours.

World.title: Footballers, coaches protest BMC proposal to turn Bandra ground into convention centre
World.content:
Hundreds of footballers, coaches, parents and supporters gathered at the Neville D'Souza Football Ground in Bandra on Sunday (August 23, 2026) to protest against a proposal to convert the ground into a convention-cum-exhibition centre, saying the redevelopment would take away one of the city's few accessible football grounds and affect thousands of players.

The protest came amid the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's push to clear the proposal. According to protesters, the ground is used by players ranging from young children to senior footballers for training, school tournaments and league matches.

The ground, which has been in use since 2018, sees football activity from early morning until late at night, with several academies and clubs using the facility for training and competitive matches.

“We have almost 14,000 people playing on this ground. Everyone from the ages of five onwards plays on this ground. School tournaments, league matches, and more happen here. It will be very sad if this ground is lost,” said Nigel Neville D'Souza, the son of the famous Indian footballer Neville D'Souza.

Coaches at the protest said losing the ground would disrupt training schedules and leave academies uncertain about where their players would practise and compete in the next season.

“In a week I coach more than 100-200 players from different age groups. I've been a part of this ground since its inception in 2018 and our club Mumbai Warriors FC played many matches here,” said Rajkumar Ashappa, head coach of Rafa Football Academy and Mumbai Warriors FC.

“If anything India needs to develop in football, it is more grounds. Then we may have a chance to compete at the Asian Cup. If you take away the existing grounds, that is unacceptable and uncalled for,” he said.

Mr. Ashappa said officials had told football groups that an alternative ground would be provided, but that no details had been given on where or when it would be made available.

Vishal Rathod, a senior coach with MSB Academy and the IOT club said the uncertainty was already affecting planning for the next season. “Both the academy and the club I am a part of play a lot of matches on this ground. I have been coaching here for seven years. It doesn't make sense to change the ground into a convention centre,” he said.

Mr. Rathod questioned the need for another convention facility in the area, pointing to the existing convention infrastructure around the ground.

“Planning for our club has been affected because we don't know where we will play next season. Parents are hesitant to send their children, and senior players are probably thinking about what will happen next season,” he said.

For younger players, the concern was more immediate.

“This is a very wrong move. We have to think about the future, about where we will play. If there is no ground, then how can we play? There is no other ground nearby and if we can't play, then how will we make our career?” said 15-year-old Waseem Yasin Khan, who plays in the second division of the BFC Neville Boys team.

Fellow player Deep Harmalkar, 15, who has played football since the under-8 level, said losing the ground could make it difficult for players to continue competing.

“If this ground goes away, then we will have to travel really far to play our Division Two matches, and our parents won't allow us to go then,” he said.

The Mumbai Football Association (MFA) also opposed the proposal, with its vice-president Nasir Hussain saying the city already had a shortage of football grounds.

“Mumbai hardly has any football grounds as it is. Every Indian dreams of a day when India will play in the World Cup. Our request to the government is that we need more grounds, but this ground itself is being sought after,” Mr. Hussain said.

He said matches at the ground begin as early as 6 a.m. and continue until late at night, adding that many parents attended Sunday's protest because they wanted their children to spend time playing sport rather than remaining indoors.

Former India goalkeeper and current goalkeeping coach of I-League club Real Kashmir, Mohammed Yusuf Ansari, also joined the protest and appealed for the ground to be protected.

“I am proud that I am an Indian player and a Maharashtrian player. But I feel deep regret for the young people. What is the future of these children if this ground goes away?” Mr. Ansari said.

Recalling the protection of football grounds in Mumbai in the past, Mr. Ansari said, “All the young footballers are our future.”

The protest also drew political support, with Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray, who is also the president of the MFA, alleging that open spaces and sports grounds in Bandra were increasingly being converted into privately controlled facilities.

“The problem is not with installing sports facilities, the problem is privatising them, gatekeeping them and ensuring that money is taken out of Mumbaikars' pockets,” Mr. Thackeray said.

He also criticised what he described as a broader lack of planning for football in Mumbai, referring to the recent visit of Argentine footballer Lionel Messi and the state government's proposed football development initiatives.

“When Lionel Messi visited Mumbai, he was taken to a cricket stadium because neither Mumbai nor the State football associations were properly involved. It was reduced to a photo op,” Mr. Thackeray said.

He also claimed that the announced 'Project Mahadeva' had stalled and that football grounds across Mumbai were being replaced by concrete structures.

“The selected kids have been sent back to their regular schools instead of being enrolled in the project. Meanwhile, football grounds across Mumbai are being stripped away and turned into concrete structures,” he said.

For the protesters, however, the immediate demand remained straightforward: preserve the Neville D'Souza ground and provide more spaces for football rather than reducing the number of existing grounds.

With academies, clubs and young players already planning their next season, the uncertainty over the ground's future has become a question not merely of one playing field, but of where Mumbai's next generation of footballers will train and compete.

World.title: Tihar redemption: From prison cells to lives of purpose
World.content:
When Lakshman, 28 (name changed on request), walked out of prison after seven years, one of the first things he had to learn was how to use a smartphone.

WhatsApp, digital payments and the many everyday functions of a phone were unfamiliar to him. “I felt like I was a decade behind the world,” he recalled. At times, the pace of life outside was so overwhelming that he wondered whether it might have been easier to remain inside.

His experience captures a less visible consequence of imprisonment: a sentence may end on paper, but reintegration can take much longer. For many former prisoners, education has offered a way to rebuild their lives after release. It has opened up opportunities for work, helping overcome stigma and, in some cases, giving them the means to return to the prison system to help those still behind bars.

Mr. Lakshman was convicted in a murder case in 2015 and remained in Tihar prison until 2022. His father had died in 2013, and his family was already struggling financially. In prison, he began working in the canteen, earning ₹85 a day after six months, and started sending part of his earnings home to support his sister.

The years in prison exposed him to the psychological toll of incarceration. He saw fellow prisoners die by suicide and said the loneliness of the night could make it difficult to process emotions. “The thought crossed my mind too,” he said, but work and education helped him stay focused.

He completed Class 12 and began pursuing a BA while in prison. When he learnt about BetterLife Prison School, a programme offering functional literacy and foundational education, he enrolled there as well.

Today, Mr. Lakshman works as a field lead with Project Second Chance, an initiative of the TYCIA Foundation focused on education, mental health support, life skills and legal assistance for prisoners. His work includes gender sensitisation among young inmates convicted of crimes against women, mental health counselling and legal support for released prisoners across Delhi, Uttarakhand and Haryana.

“My life’s purpose changed. I dreamt of becoming a police officer or joining the Army, but after my jail term, I wanted to become a social worker. I don’t want anyone to face what I faced,” he said.

A sister’s promise

For Karan Kumar, 27, education became a way to rebuild his life after prison.

He was 18 and preparing for his Class 12 examination while pursuing a course in graphic and 3D animation when a fight between students at his school left another boy seriously injured. Mr. Kumar was sent to Tihar in connection with the case in June 2017. The boy later succumbed to his injuries, and Mr. Kumar remained in prison until his release in April 2025, though he was granted short periods of bail, including during the COVID-19 pandemic. His case is currently closed, with no court dates pending.

His elder sister’s response became a turning point. During his first Raksha Bandhan in prison, his sister told him she would become a lawyer so she could help people like her brother. She eventually became a lawyer and is practising in the Delhi High Court. “My takeaway was, if my sister can be so affected by my experience and make it into something positive, why can’t I?” Mr. Kumar said.

In 2018, he completed Class 12 and subsequently pursued a BA from Delhi University alongside a Bachelor of Social Work. He also worked with the prison legal cell, where he learnt to draft bail petitions and RTI replies and underwent para legal volunteer training.

Today, he works with the Kunji helpline and Project ALT (Access to Legal Aid Through Tech), providing legal support to inmates and their families.

After securing bail, Mr. Kumar had to stay with his sister for nearly a year instead of returning home. The stigma attached to being a released prisoner, he said, can come not only from society but also from within one’s own family.

A second life

For Jeevan Waghmare, 44, education became the bridge from prison to a career helping others navigate the legal system.

Sentenced to life imprisonment in 2005 along with five other members of his family following a murder arising from a property dispute, Mr. Waghmare resumed his studies in prison. He completed a BA in History, followed by postgraduate degrees in sociology and history through Maharashtra’s prison distance-learning programme, and a postgraduate diploma in human rights from the Indian Institute of Human Rights in New Delhi.

He also taught history and sociology to fellow prisoners and helped inmates who could not afford lawyers draft applications for bail, parole and other legal relief.

After his release in 2022, he became a practising lawyer, assisting prisoners in navigating the legal system.

Mr. Waghmare said his experience convinced him that prisons needed to give greater emphasis to education, mental health support, skills and post-release assistance. “Once a person realises that they made a mistake, at least 80-90% want to improve themselves. But we continue to treat them as criminals, and then change becomes hard to achieve,” he said.

World.title: Those against reservation should be booked for sedition: Union Minister Ramdas Athawale
World.content:
Union Minister Ramdas Athawale has demanded that sedition charges be invoked against those opposing or seeking abolition of reservation, which he called a constitutional right.

In a statement issued on Sunday (August 23, 2026), Mr. Athawale said protests against quota, including those at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, had brought the issue back into focus. He claimed that campaigns were also running on social media, calling for the removal or changes to the quota system.

“Opposition to reservation is opposition to the Constitution. Those taking an anti-reservation stand are anti-constitutional and stringent action of sedition should be taken against them,” the Republican Party of India (Athawale) chief said.

Some people were demanding the abolition of reservation, he said, asserting that reservation cannot be abolished as it is a constitutional right.

The Delhi Police on Sunday (August 23) said no permission has been granted to any individual or organisation to hold a protest or gathering at Jantar Mantar over reservation reforms and warned people against assembling there based on “misleading” social media posts.

A large number of protestors had gathered at Jantar Mantar carrying banners, posters and saffron flags and raised slogans against caste-based reservation.

The protestors were demanding that economic criteria be given precedence over caste in determining eligibility for government support and reservation.

World.title: Kerala HC directs strict action against illegal vehicle modifications
World.content:
The Kerala High Court has directed the Enforcement wing of the Motor Vehicles Department (MVD) and the Kerala Police to impose strict penalties on all vehicles used in public spaces with illegal modifications in violation of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.

The court noted that the Enforcement wing had not taken any action against vehicles used in public places with wheels projecting outside the vehicles’ bodies, citing a specific instance of a modified four-wheeler, which had featured in the media after conducting rescue operations in Adoor that was impacted by the floods following the torrential rains in the first week of August.

The Transport Commissioner informed the court that the offending vehicle, with six additional lights, was fined ₹5,000, and an additional fine of ₹2,000 was imposed for a pollution-related violation. The court sought a complete report on the action taken on this four-wheeler and whether any permission was granted for the use of the vehicle in a public place.

The Division Bench of Justices Anil K. Narendran and S. Muralee Krishna directed that each instance of unauthorised modification to a vehicle, such as after-market multifunction lights, red-blue strobe lights, wheel spacers and wide tyres, which result in the vehicle projecting laterally beyond the body of the vehicle, after-market exhaust systems with ‘flame-kits’, would attract a fine of ₹5,000 per alteration.

The court found that the use of such vehicles in public places without complying with the provisions under the governing laws would endanger the safety of other road users. The Motor Vehicles Act and the subsequent rules detailed every aspect of the construction and maintenance of vehicles, and if an aspect was not mentioned, it should be assumed that it was specifically excluded, the court stated.

World.title: Three newborns die in fire at government hospital in Amravati, Maharashtra
World.content:
Three newborn babies died after a fire broke out at the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) of Amravati’s District Women’s Hospital, a government hospital, at 3.30 a.m. on Monday (August 24, 2026), prompting an emergency evacuation of dozens of infants undergoing treatment, according to Gorakhnath Jadhav, Senior Police Inspector, Gadage Nagar Police Station in Amravati.

The fire happened after a ventilator exploded on the third floor, killing three newborns with severe burns and smoke inhalation. Six other infants were rescued and are in critical care. The ventilator fire was put out within 10 to 15 minutes.

As many as 36 other newborns were rescued after the incident occurred at the District Women’s Hospital, Amravati Police Commissioner Rakesh Ola told news agency PTI. A ventilator in the hospital’s NICU, which houses premature and critically ill babies, caught fire at around 3.15 a.m., he said.

Maharashtra Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule, who is also Amravati’s guardian minister, said he has ordered a comprehensive inquiry into the incident and assured that those injured were receiving all necessary medical assistance.

अमरावतीमधील आजच्या दुर्घटनेमुळे मी खूप दुःखी झालो. माझे मन हेलावून गेले आहे.



दगावलेल्या नवजात बालकांना अतिशय व्यथित अंतःकरणाने श्रद्धांजली व्यक्त करतो. त्यांच्या पालकांना हे दुःख सहन करण्याची ताकद ईश्वर देवो, अशी प्रार्थना करतो.

या घटनेच्या संपूर्ण चौकशीचे आदेश मी दिले आहेत. जे… — Chandrashekhar Bawankule (@cbawankule) August 24, 2026

The NICU has three compartments: one each for inborn and outborn babies, and one for step‑down care for children ready to be discharged, Mr. Ola said, adding that 39 infants were admitted across the three sections.

A ventilator in the outborn babies’ compartment caught fire. Three of the newborns there died, while the other six babies were rescued, the official said. Another official said six infants have been admitted to a super speciality hospital.

After the blaze erupted, the hospital staff on duty rushed to the spot and safely evacuated the other children, Mr. Bawankule said in a post on X.

He said the fire broke out around 4 a.m. at the special newborn care unit in the new building of the District Women’s Hospital, where premature, low-weight and critically ill newborns were undergoing treatment.

Some infants were shifted to the Divisional Referral Services Hospital for further treatment. Four children were undergoing treatment there, with one reported to be in a critical condition, Mr. Bawankule said.

Fire personnel and the PWD’s electrical wing have been informed, and they will find out the cause of the fire, Mr. Ola said.

Mr. Bawankule said he was deeply distressed by the deaths and assured the families that the government would extend all necessary assistance.

“I am deeply saddened by today’s incident in Amravati. My heart is heavy,” he said.

“The government stands with the relatives of the deceased children and the government and administration are providing all possible help,” he stated.

The Minister further said he had discussed the incident with officials concerned and the administration was keeping a close watch on the situation.

(With PTI inputs)

World.title: Nawaz consults leaders on AJK govt formation
World.content:
LAHORE/MUZAFFARABAD: PML-N President Nawaz Sharif chaired a party meeting to discuss AJK government formation and potential candidates for the prime ministerial slot, as six candidates contest five women’s reserved seats in the Legislative Assembly today.

The meeting also deliberated on the country’s overall political situation, the health of PTI founder Imran Khan, and recent decisions handed down by the Supreme Court.

PML-N leaders Shah Ghulam Qadir and Tariq Farooq have emerged as the primary contenders for the top office. Sources said that one of the two is likely to be nominated as the party’s candidate for prime minister.

PML-N finalises strategy for reserved seats polls; legislative assembly to meet today; six candidates vying for five women’s constituencies

The meeting also focused on the party’s future political strategy and key decision-making processes. The PML-N leadership has previously held multiple rounds of consultations on AJK government formation as part of its ongoing efforts to consolidate its political strategy in the region.

Election strategy finalised

Meanwhile, the parliamentary party of the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) met to finalise its strategy for Monday’s election to the seven reserved seats of the AJK Legislative Assembly.

The meeting was chaired by PML-N AJK president Shah Ghulam Qadir and was also attended by Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry and Senator Anusha Rahman.

The meeting expressed full confidence in the leadership of PML-N supremo Nawaz Sharif, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz.

According to a resolution adopted at the meeting, the parliamentary party reiterated its commitment to working for the development of AJK, supremacy of the Constitution and law, and restoration of merit and justice in accordance with Mr Nawaz’s vision.

It also reaffirmed its commitment to the ideology of accession to Pakistan and the slogan “Kashmir Banega Pakistan”.

The resolution expressed full support for the measures taken by the Pakistan armed forces, under the leadership of Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, against the country’s internal and external enemies, and satisfaction over Pakistan’s recognition at the international level.

The meeting resolved that the incoming AJK government would make every effort to improve law and order, revive the stalled process of development and formulate comprehensive policies for the welfare of the people.

It also expressed confidence in the electoral process held in AJK and congratulated the Chief Election Commissioner and administration for conducting the elections.

On the Kashmir dispute, the resolution expressed concern over the situation in India-held Jammu and Kashmir and called upon the international community to take notice of what it termed Indian war crimes in the territory.

It said India had illegally revoked the special status of occupied Kashmir in 2019 in violation of UN and Security Council resolutions and accused New Delhi of misleading the international community about the situation in the region.

The meeting paid tribute to the Kashmiri people for their “unprecedented sacrifices” and steadfastness in their struggle for the right to self-determination.

It also appreciated the political, moral and diplomatic support extended by the people and government of Pakistan to the Kashmiri people.

The meeting rejected remarks about Kashmir attributed to the US ambassador to India and demanded that the Kashmir dispute be resolved in accordance with UN resolutions.

Reserved seats for women

On the other hand, six candidates will contest five seats reserved for women in the AJK Legislative Assembly today, according to the final list issued by the Election Commission on Sunday.

The candidates in the fray are PML-N’s Riffat Abid, Sehrish Qamar, Maryam Idrees and Maryam Zaman, also known as Maryam Kashmiri, and PPP’s Farzana Yaqoob and Zobia Khurshid Raja.

Seven candidates had originally filed nomination papers for the five women’s seats. However, PPP candidate Shaheen Kosar Dar withdrew her nomination papers on the day fixed for withdrawals under the election schedule, the Election Commission Spokesperson Raja Muhammad Shakeel said.

For the seat reserved for Ulema and Mashaikh, PPP’s Hafiz Tariq Mahmood will face PML-N’s Mohammad Mazhar Saeed.

Similarly, PML-N’s Barrister Syed Iftikhar Gillani and PPP’s Sahibzada Zulfiqar Ali will contest the seat reserved for technocrats and professionals.

PML-N’s Chaudhry Abdul Rehman Arain was the only candidate to have submitted his nomination papers for the seat reserved for state subjects residing abroad. He was consequently declared elected unopposed.

Polling for the women’s, Ulema and Mashaikh, and technocrats and professionals’ seats will be held on Monday (today) from 10am to 1pm at the Assembly Hall in Muzaffarabad.

As the inaugural session of the incoming Legislative Assembly has already been summoned for 2pm on Monday, shortly after the announcement of the results, all newly elected members will take an oath at the hands of outgoing Speaker Chaudhry Latif Akbar, who failed to retain his seat in the elections.

Published in Dawn, August 24th, 2026

World.title: Comstech chief remains defiant in face of ‘damning inquiry’
World.content:
• President-ordered probe found OIC official guilty of ‘misconduct, non-compliance’

• Accused official calls inquiry ‘one-sided’, claims Presidency was ‘misused’

ISLAMABAD: An inquiry committee formed on the directives of President Asif Ali Zardari has declared the top official of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation’s (OIC) Standing Committee on Scientific and Technological Cooperation (Comstech) guilty of multiple charges of misconduct.

According to the inquiry report seen by Dawn, Comstech Coordinator General Dr Iqbal Choudhry was accused of financial irregularities, violation of executive orders and non-compliance with court directives.

However, the official in question has questioned the legality of proceedings against him, calling it a “one-sided inquiry”.

According to the inquiry report, Dr Choudhry was initially appointed by then-president Arif Alvi in 2020 during the PTI’s tenure, and was subsequently reappointed by President Zardari for another four-year term in October 2024.

Under Articles 12(2), read with 16(3) of the Comstech statute, the President of Pakistan is the appointing authority for the post of the body’s coordinator general.

Comstech was created in January 1981 at the Third Islamic Summit in Makkah, Saudi Arabia. Headquartered in Islamabad, Pakistan, it aims to promote science, technology and research cooperation among OIC member states.

The inquiry committee was headed by Dr Asim Hussain, the chancellor of Ziauddin University.

Its members included Pakistan Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (PCSIR) Chairman Dr Syed Hussain Abidi, Ministry of Science and Technology Secretary Shahid Iqbal Baloch and its Chief Finance and Accounts Officer Muhammad Saeedullah Yousafzai.

Inquiry findings

The committee held that Dr Choudhry had failed to implement instructions issued by the president, terming the alleged failure “misconduct”. It also accused him of violating court orders, and failing to reply to complaints.

The inquiry found that meetings of the Comstech Executive Committee had not been convened for the last four years, and that most decisions were taken by Dr Choudhry alone, terming this “maladministration”.

It further maintained that expenditures had been incurred for several years without budgetary approval, which the committee declared “unauthorised and illegal”.

The report recommended strict disciplinary action over the alleged misuse of Comstech funds, including expenditure allegedly made for personal benefit.

The committee alleged that Dr Choudhry undertook more than 70 foreign trips over the last six years without prior approval from the president in his capacity as Comstech chairman. Some of the visits, it said, were to countries not associated with Comstech, while funds were also allegedly used to cover the travel and accommodation expenses of female associates.

The report also pointed out that Dr Choudhry simultaneously held the posts of Comstech coordinator general and director of the International Centre for Chemical and Biological Sciences (ICCBS) from April 8, 2020, to Nov 12, 2024, a period of around four and a half years, despite directives from the ministry to relinquish the additional charge.

The inquiry also cited complaints regarding forced resignations and dismissals of employees, a lack of transparent procedures in disciplinary proceedings, and allegations of nepotism and favouritism in recruitment.

It noted that the World Academy of Sciences, Trieste, Italy, had also issued a reprimand letter to Dr Choudhry.

The inquiry committee has recommended that the matter be referred to anti-corruption institutions for further investigation and appropriate action against Dr Choudhry on multiple counts of alleged misconduct.

The recommendations in the inquiry report have been submitted to the competent authority for further proceedings.

Official’s response

When approached for comment, Dr Choudhry told Dawn he was unaware of any such report, but raised questions over the legality of the inquiry, noting that procedural requirements had not been fulfilled.

He claimed that neither any complaint nor a show cause notice was shared with him, and said that there were “serious procedural flaws in this one-sided inquiry”.

“You cannot do it on the basis of a fake complaint,” he remarked.

He maintained that the president, in his capacity as Comstech chairman, draws his powers from OIC procedures, and could not as as head of the state take a unilateral action against an OIC body which enjoys diplomatic immunity.

Alleging that the Presidency was being misused, he said any inquiry or report prepared without proof or documentation has no legal or ethical standing, and is liable to be challenged in court.

Published in Dawn, August 24th, 2026

World.title: Fazl blames lack of joint opposition for unchecked legislation
World.content:
JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman addresses a workers’ convention in Peshawar.—PPI

PESHAWAR: JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman on Sunday pointed out a structural weakness on opposition benches, noting that the opposition leader failed to unite parties to effectively challenge the recent government legislation on armed forces command.

While noting that opposition walkouts without act­ive resistance have harmed democratic checks and balances, the JUI-F chief urged joint opposition coordination inside parliament to prevent further unche­cked legislative actions.

“The recent legislation was passed in a great haste, without any debate and even opposition members did not examine it in detail,” Maulana Fazl added while addressing party workers’ convention, organised by the JUI-F Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chapter, in Peshawar.

In his speech, he offered scathing critique of the recent legislations, creation of new provinces and law and order situation in the country.

Calls new provinces move ‘a tactic’ to roll back NFC Award

He said that they supported Pakistan’s strong defence capability, but rejected military’s interference in politics.

Maulana Fazl regretted that even the administrative powers of prime minister within the armed forces have now been vested in one person. He noted the laws also had an overriding effect over other legislations that were in conflict with it.

He claimed that when they had raised in parliament the issue of making the Holy Quran and Sunnah as the supreme law of the land in the past, the then chief justice of Pakistan declared that all clauses of the Constitution were equal and no single clause could be superior to another.

However, he said that legislation was carried out to concentrate power and authority in establishment with overriding effect over other laws that were in conflict with it.

The powers that should have been vested in parliament were concentrated within a person, he reiterated, adding that his office’s authority had been extended over the army, air force, and the navy as well and it would hold all powers, including dismissing someone, extending someone’s service, accepting and rejecting someone resignation, and all these powers were previously vested in the federal government.

He said that the wishes of the head of one institution were being imposed on all other institutions and the entire nation.

Maulana Fazl said that as the federal government surrendered its authority and it could also enact any other legislation whenever need arises, taking the parliament out of the equation. He said that it was the opposition leader’s job to unite all the parties sitting on opposition benches and it was lacking there.

He said he met the opposition leader and discussed a joint strategy to play their role as joint opposition inside the parliament. He said he has proposed to the opposition leader to keep an eye on such things inside the parliament. “They have done a big damage and we do not even know what has happened,” he said.

He also said that the same law immediately went to Senate and passed within 30 minutes and the opposition was happy about staging a walkout.

The JUI-F chief underscored the importance of a strong opposition in parliament to force the government to listen to them.

New provinces

Referring to the security situation in KP, Maulana Fazl also criticised the formation of new provinces, saying that it was not prudent to talk about divisions when the house itself was on fire.

He believed the creation of new provinces was aimed at reversing the National Finance Commission Award and “capturing” the mineral resources of provinces.

He recalled that they had also opposed the Fata merger with KP and the situation vindicated their stance.
